criteria: A 'default' netrc stanza with neither login nor password reaches the parsenetrc success path.
parsenetrc returns NETRC_SUCCESS without any real credential being found.
override_login sets conn->bits.netrc=TRUE on that success.
bits.netrc lets http.c resend credentials after a redirect to a different host, leaking them.
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: a nonmatching specific login receives another login's buffered password, and a null-pointer dereference in str_has_ctrl when netrc returns partial credentials.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A netrc 'default' entry with no login or password still returns NETRC_SUCCESS. This sets bits.netrc, so credentials are resent to a different host after a redirect.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds `else if(!login && !password) retcode = NETRC_FILE_MISSING;`, which breaks the GT chain for a credential-less default entry. Scanner finding 1 describes a different bug: a password from a nonmatching specific login is returned. Finding 2 is a null dereference in str_has_ctrl. Neither finding covers a default entry with no credentials yielding NETRC_SUCCESS, or bits.netrc enabling a cross-host redirect leak.

criteria: ldap_set_option() is called with a NULL handle, which targets the process-global LDAP context
The NULL-handle calls set TLS-critical options such as LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_REQUIRE_CERT or LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_CACERTFILE
The cause is setting options before ldap_init(), so no per-connection handle exists yet
Concurrent threads can see each other's weakened TLS settings, a cross-transfer data race
The NULL-handle pattern is still present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: One finding: OpenLDAP LDAPS hardcodes verify_cert=0 and sets LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_NEVER on the connection handle, so an attacker can impersonate the server (MITM). It does not mention NULL handles, global context, or threads.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ldap_do sets TLS options via ldap_set_option(NULL, ...) before ldap_init(), mutating the global OpenLDAP context. Concurrent transfers can then inherit weakened certificate verification (a DataRace).
judge.reasoning: In the PR, ldap_init() now runs first, and every ldap_set_option call, including the TLS ones, uses the server handle instead of NULL. That breaks the GT chain of global-context mutation. The scanner instead reports a hardcoded verify_cert=0 that disables certificate verification on the per-connection handle. That is an adjacent bug, not the global-state data race.

criteria: Trigger: QUIC/HTTP3 connection with wolfSSL to a host where peer->sni is NULL, such as an IP literal
Incorrect guard: the wolfSSL check runs only when peer->sni is non-NULL (`peer->sni && check_fails`)
Effect: when SNI is missing, verification is skipped entirely instead of failing closed
Result defaults to CURLE_OK, so any certificate is accepted for IP-literal hosts
Location: Curl_vquic_tls_verify_peer wolfSSL branch in lib/vquic/vquic-tls.c
judge.findings_summary: One finding: for IP-literal HTTP/3 with wolfSSL, the fallback calls wolfSSL_check_domain_name after the handshake. The scanner says this call does not inspect the received certificate, so a wrong identity is accepted.
judge.ground_truth_summary: An inverted guard made the wolfSSL QUIC peer check run only when peer->sni is set. IP-literal hosts with no SNI skip verification entirely and return CURLE_OK, enabling MITM.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR has no SNI-conditional skip. It always calls wolfSSL_check_domain_name, falling back from peer->sni to peer->hostname, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner instead argues that this post-handshake call does not really verify the certificate. That is a different mechanism (API misuse), not the GT inverted-guard skip.

criteria: sanitize_cookie_path strips the trailing '/' of a lone "/" path, reducing len to 0
Curl_memdup0 then allocates an exact-size 1-byte spath holding only NUL
replace_existing calls strchr(clist->spath + 1, '/') without checking spath[0], reading out of bounds
Trigger: an insecure cookie overlays an existing secure cookie with path "/" on the same domain
No len>1 guard or spath[0] check breaks the chain
judge.findings_summary: One finding: TAB before an attribute stops the strparse-based parsing loop early, so Secure is skipped and the cookie can be sent over cleartext HTTP.
judge.ground_truth_summary: For path "/", sanitize_cookie_path strips the lone slash, so Curl_memdup0 makes a 1-byte spath. replace_existing's strchr(spath+1) then reads out of bounds during a secure-cookie overlay check.
judge.reasoning: The PR already contains the fix. sanitize_cookie_path uses `len > 1`, and replace_existing guards strchr with `if(clist->spath[0])`. The scanner reports a different bug: TAB whitespace handling in the attribute parser that can drop the Secure flag. It does not mention spath under-allocation or the out-of-bounds strchr read.

criteria: Peer-sent PING frames trigger automatic PONG generation (source/trigger).
ws_enc_add_cntrl itself eagerly encodes each PONG into ws->sendbuf and flushes it.
The only guard is enc.payload_remain==0, with no check that earlier sendbuf bytes were transmitted.
ws->sendbuf uses BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT, so appends never fail on capacity.
A non-reading peer causes unbounded sendbuf/heap growth.
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the curl_ws_recv postamble eagerly materializes pending PONGs into the soft-limit sendbuf, bypassing ws_flush's queue gate. Under peer backpressure this causes heap growth in connect-only mode.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ws_enc_add_cntrl eagerly encodes and flushes each auto-PONG into the soft-limit sendbuf, guarded only by payload_remain==0. A non-reading peer that floods PINGs causes unbounded memory growth.
judge.reasoning: In this PR, ws_enc_add_cntrl only overwrites a single pending slot and does no encoding or flushing. That breaks the GT chain at its primary location, and the task note confirms the fix is applied. The scanner instead flags the curl_ws_recv postamble calling ws_enc_add_pending. That is a different trigger site and path, an adjacent concern rather than the exact GT eager-encoding chain in ws_enc_add_cntrl. For this benign snapshot, it does not count as a detection.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: req->path (request/easy-handle lifetime) is a borrowed pointer into smbc->share (connection-owned heap)
No private copy of the path is made at parse time
Connection teardown (smb_conn_dtor/disconnect) frees smbc->share while the request still holds req->path
Later use of req->path (tree-connect/open message building) reads freed memory → use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: One finding: a reused SMB connection keeps the prior share while req->path holds the later URL's path, so tree-connect and open target mismatched resources. Classified as Other, not a UAF.
judge.ground_truth_summary: req->path pointed into connection-owned smbc->share. When the connection was freed before the easy handle, req->path dangled, and later message building read freed memory.
judge.reasoning: The PR copies req->path with strdup and frees it in smb_done, so the request no longer borrows connection memory and the UAF chain is broken. The scanner explicitly says the patch correctly separates path ownership from connection lifetime. Its finding is a different logic bug: a reused connection keeps an old share and pairs it with a new path. That is not a use-after-free.

criteria: NTLM-wanting request with mismatched credentials evaluates the NTLM-reuse fallback in the connection-match predicate
The fallback guard checks only http_ntlm_state == NTLMSTATE_NONE and is missing http_negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE
A connection already in-progress or authenticated via Negotiate/SPNEGO therefore passes the guard
That connection is reused by a request for a different user, keeping user1's authenticated session
judge.findings_summary: Reports that the NTLM fallback can select an active multiplexed neutral connection, replacing its shared credentials so that a later Negotiate on an earlier stream uses the wrong identity. It acknowledges the negotiate-state check is present.
judge.ground_truth_summary: url_match_auth_ntlm lacked the http_negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE check, so Negotiate-authenticated connections passed the NTLM-neutral guard and were reused by a different user's request.
judge.reasoning: The PR guards the fallback with both the NTLM and Negotiate state checks, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner itself says active NTLM or Negotiate state prevents selection. It reports a different bug instead: an in-use multiplexed neutral connection has its credentials replaced. That is a different trigger and a different missing guard (idle/in-use), not the missing negotiate-state check.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Curl_auth_gsasl_is_supported allocates gsasl->ctx via gsasl_init
On gsasl_client_start failure, gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx) frees the context
gsasl->ctx is not set to NULL after that free
Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup later calls gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx) unconditionally on the stale pointer
Result is a double free of the GSASL context
judge.findings_summary: Two leak findings: the decoded challenge is not freed on successful gsasl_step, and GSASL sessions can be orphaned after fallback. Neither reports a double free of ctx in is_supported.
judge.ground_truth_summary: gsasl->ctx is freed but not nulled when gsasl_client_start fails, and cleanup then calls gsasl_done on it again, causing a double free. The fix (setting ctx to NULL) is already in the PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR code sets gsasl->ctx = NULL right after gsasl_done on the client_start failure path, so the double-free chain is broken. No scanner finding reports this double free. Finding 1 is a memory leak of the decoded challenge in the token function. Finding 2 is a cleanup-ownership leak in curl_sasl.c. Both are adjacent bugs, not the GT.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Referer bufref refresh moved from setopt.c into Curl_pretransfer
Curl_pretransfer handles only the non-NULL STRING_SET_REFERER case
No else branch clears data->state.referer when the option is NULL
Setting CURLOPT_REFERER to NULL leaves the stale referer cached
Stale Referer header is sent on later transfers
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reports a UseAfterFree: replacing or clearing CURLOPT_REFERER frees the configured string while the non-owning state.referer alias stays live. Getinfo, dup, or header sinks could then read freed memory before the next pretransfer.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Curl_pretransfer lacked an else branch to clear state.referer when CURLOPT_REFERER was set to NULL. The old referer stayed cached and was sent on later requests.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds an else branch that calls Curl_bufref_free on data->state.referer when STRING_SET_REFERER is NULL. That breaks the GT chain, so the vulnerability is not present. The scanner reports a different bug: a use-after-free from a dangling alias between setopt and the next pretransfer. It even says Curl_pretransfer repairs the pointer before the next transfer, so it does not match the GT stale-referer logic error.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: write_paused state drives cf_h2_update_local_win to shrink the HTTP/2 stream receive window to zero
On unpause (http2_data_pause), the updater grows the window via nghttp2_submit_window_update
nghttp2_session_set_local_window_size is not called before the window update, so nghttp2's internal local window stays inconsistent
Result: the paused HTTP/2 stream stays blocked at a zero window and cannot resume receiving
judge.findings_summary: One finding: cw-pause soft-limit queue with no aggregate cap lets an ngtcp2 HTTP/3 peer exhaust heap while a stream is paused; HTTP/2 is cited as properly limiting the window.
judge.ground_truth_summary: HTTP/2 write_paused shrinks the stream window to zero; on unpause the window update is submitted without first setting nghttp2's local window size, so the stream stays blocked. Fixed in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already calls nghttp2_session_set_local_window_size before nghttp2_submit_window_update, so the GT chain is fixed. The scanner reports a different bug: unbounded HTTP/3 pause buffering in cw-pause.c, a memory-exhaustion issue. It never mentions the HTTP/2 window restore logic, and it describes the HTTP/2 path as a working control.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Sink is strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") in tool_read_cb in src/tool_cb_rea.c
per->uploadfile can be NULL on some paths that reach the read callback
No NULL check guards the strcmp dereference
Result is a NULL pointer dereference crash
judge.findings_summary: Two findings, both in tool_doswin.c: a loopback STDIN bridge that accepts an unauthenticated peer (information disclosure), and a use-after-free/double-free race in thread cleanup. Neither concerns tool_read_cb.
judge.ground_truth_summary: tool_read_cb calls strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") without a NULL check, so a segfault occurs when uploadfile is NULL. The benign PR already includes the NULL guard.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated diff guards the comparison with 'per->uploadfile && !strcmp(...)', which breaks the NULL dereference chain. Neither scanner finding addresses tool_cb_rea.c or a NULL uploadfile. Finding 1 is an unauthenticated loopback peer in tool_doswin.c. Finding 2 is a cleanup race in tool_doswin.c. Both are unrelated bugs.

criteria: Curl_http_cookies in lib/http.c traverses cookie list returned by Curl_cookie_getlist
List elements are live jar Cookie pointers (not copies)
CURL_LOCK_DATA_COOKIE share lock released before traversal/dereference of nodes
Concurrent Set-Cookie update on shared handle can free node during traversal (UAF)
judge.findings_summary: One finding: a NULL pointer dereference when an Expires attribute has no value. valuep is passed to Curl_getdate_capped in lib/cookie.c:719.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Curl_http_cookies drops the cookie share lock after Curl_cookie_getlist but before traversing the live Cookie pointers. A concurrent Set-Cookie on a shared handle can then free a node, causing a UAF.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, Curl_share_unlock is called only after the list is traversed and destroyed, so the GT lock-scope UAF is not present. The scanner reports an unrelated NULL dereference in the cookie.c Expires parsing path. It does not mention share locking, concurrency, or a use-after-free in Curl_http_cookies.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Vulnerable code is Curl_ssl_scache_take in lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c
Shared peer->sessions list is read via Curl_llist_count in trace logging
The read happens after Curl_ssl_scache_unlock releases the scache lock
Concurrent threads mutating or freeing the peer/sessions list cause a data race or UAF-style read
Finding must identify the missing lock coverage (unlock ordered before trace)
judge.findings_summary: One finding: ngtcp2 recv/send early-data guards return the tls_vrfy_result CURLcode as an ssize_t byte count with *err=CURLE_OK, misreporting verification failures as I/O progress.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Curl_ssl_scache_take releases the scache lock before trace logging reads peer->sessions via Curl_llist_count, creating a data race or possible UAF with concurrent cache mutation.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the trace logging that calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions) runs before Curl_ssl_scache_unlock. The read stays inside the critical section, so the GT race is not present. The scanner reports a different issue: verification-error return codes in the ngtcp2 recv/send paths in curl_ngtcp2.c. It does not mention vtls_scache.c, locking, or a data race. No match.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: RTMP* ownership is registered in the connection meta hash with a destructor
The RTMP_SetupURL failure path triggers cleanup on a malformed URL
That error path manually calls RTMP_Free(r) while r is still registered in meta
The meta destructor later frees the same pointer again, causing a double-free
judge.findings_summary: One finding: if Curl_conn_meta_set fails, the destructor calls RTMP_Close on an uninitialized RTMP object because registration happens before RTMP_Init. Low impact.
judge.ground_truth_summary: rtmp_setup_connection calls RTMP_Free(r) on RTMP_SetupURL failure even though r is registered in the conn meta hash, so the meta destructor frees it again (double-free).
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the manual RTMP_Free is gone from the URL-parse-error path, and a comment defers cleanup to rtmp_conn_dtor. That breaks the double-free chain. The scanner reports something different: metadata insertion failure runs the destructor before RTMP_Init. That has a different trigger (allocation failure) and a different defect (init order), not a double-free.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: In common_init, the ch_layouts parsing loop grows buf->channel_layouts with av_realloc_array()
The realloc result held in tmp is never assigned back to buf->channel_layouts
The following memset dereferences the stale pointer: NULL on the first pass, dangling after a moved realloc
Secondary issue: memset clears one element instead of two, so the terminator stays uninitialized
Trigger: abuffersink with a channel layout option string (e.g. 'abuffersink=::a')
judge.findings_summary: One finding: legacy ch_layouts parsing sets nb_channel_layouts, which switches query_formats to the new-option branch and drops legacy sample format/rate constraints; claimed downstream PCM out-of-bounds read.
judge.ground_truth_summary: av_realloc_array result is not assigned back to buf->channel_layouts in common_init, so memset dereferences NULL or a dangling pointer; memset also clears only one element.
judge.reasoning: The PR assigns buf->channel_layouts = tmp and memsets two elements, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner reports a different bug: converting legacy ch_layouts to the new state makes asink_query_formats skip the legacy sample_fmts/sample_rates constraints, leading to a downstream OOB read. It does not mention the missing realloc assignment or the NULL/dangling memset. Different root cause, and the GT is absent.

criteria: Untrusted num_parameters is read via ffio_read_leb in audio_element_obu
No upper bound (<=2) is enforced on num_parameters for Channel-based audio elements
The loop calls param_parse repeatedly, allowing duplicate DEMIXING/RECON_GAIN types
A repeated type overwrites the demixing_info/recon_gain_info pointer, leaking the earlier allocation (memory DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: substream array OOB from layer counts, sound_system map OOB, negative IPCM index, unpadded AAC extradata read, and null deref in cleanup after allocation failure. None address the num_parameters limit or the leak.
judge.ground_truth_summary: audio_element_obu does not cap num_parameters at 2 for Channel elements. Duplicate param_parse calls overwrite demixing/recon_gain pointers and leak memory (CVE-2025-1816). In this benign snapshot the fix is already applied.
judge.reasoning: This is a benign task: the fix is already applied, so the num_parameters bound exists in the evaluated code. No scanner finding covers num_parameters, duplicate param_parse calls, or a param-definition memory leak. The findings concern substream OOB, the sound_system index, the IPCM index, AAC padding, and cleanup null derefs. These are adjacent bugs in the same file and do not match the GT root cause.

criteria: Trigger: a low fps (unbounded VIDEO_RATE) and/or low timeclamp gives step = sample_rate/(fps*count) larger than fft_len
No divisibility or bound check keeps step <= fft_len
After a CQT plot, remaining_fill is set to step, so j = fft_len - remaining_fill becomes negative
Sink: filter_frame writes fft_data[j+m] at negative offsets, a heap underflow
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: low input sample rates make ceil(log2(rate*timeclamp)) negative, so 1<<fft_bits is undefined behavior before FFT init and allocation in config_output.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unbounded fps and the removed rate%(fps*count) check let step exceed fft_len. j = fft_len - remaining_fill then goes negative, and filter_frame writes fft_data before the start of its heap allocation.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports a negative shift exponent in config_output when the sample rate is very low, which then affects FFT sizing. The GT is a negative fft_data index in filter_frame when step exceeds fft_len, caused by unbounded fps and the removed divisibility check. The trigger, sink and missing guard all differ. The benign task note also says the fix is already applied in this PR.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: monochrome (chroma_format_idc==0) SPS containing PCM coding blocks
Sink: PCM block length calculation in hls_pcm_sample used for skip_bytes/init_get_bits
Missing guard: chroma contribution to length not conditioned on chroma_format_idc
Effect: inflated length over-skips the bitstream, causing parse desync and possible OOB reads
Vulnerable chain must still exist in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: One finding: hevc_ps.c removes the chroma_format_idc whitelist without adding a 0..3 range check, so out-of-range values index four-entry subsampling tables out of bounds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: hls_pcm_sample computed PCM length with chroma terms even for YUV400, inflating skip_bytes and desynchronizing the bitstream. The evaluated PR already guards the chroma terms.
judge.reasoning: The PR guards the PCM length calculation with `chroma_format_idc != 0 ? ... : 0`, so the GT chain is fixed in the evaluated code. The scanner's only finding is a different bug: an unchecked chroma_format_idc upper bound used to index subsampling tables in hevc_ps.c. It does not involve hls_pcm_sample or the PCM length calculation.

criteria: get_eia608_packet assumes a single atom: one avio_skip(pb, 8), then all remaining bytes are treated as caption byte pairs
Headers of later atoms (cdat/cdt2) are misread as caption data
Hardcoded 0xFC cc_type cannot tell CC field 1 from field 2
No overflow check on ((size-8)/2)*3, so an undersized allocation can lead to a heap overflow
Path is reached from mov_read_packet for AV_CODEC_ID_EIA_608 samples
judge.findings_summary: One finding: c608 parsing allocates based on declared sizes and keeps looping past EOF because avio_r8 returns zero, causing memory/CPU exhaustion. It notes the overflow check and in-bounds writes.
judge.ground_truth_summary: get_eia608_packet skipped only the first 8-byte atom header, so later atom headers were treated as caption data. It also hardcoded field 1 (0xFC) and lacked an overflow check on the output size calculation.
judge.reasoning: The PR code parses each atom header in a loop, derives cc_field from cdat/cdt2, and adds an INT_MAX/3 overflow check. That breaks the GT chain. The scanner reports a different issue: resource consumption from avio_r8 returning zero at EOF. It also says outright that the multiplication is overflow-checked and the writes stay in bounds, which contradicts the GT vulnerability.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: submit_packet() runs during draining for a no-delay codec (e.g. vp3/theora) because the early return was removed
State error: the guard only skips update_context_from_thread() but still sets prev_thread to a thread that never received VLC state
Propagation: ff_thread_flush() copies context from that VLC-less prev_thread into thread[0] via vp3_update_thread_context, setting coeff_vlc to NULL
Sink: after decoding restarts, unpack_dct_coeffs() dereferences the NULL coeff_vlc
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the worker loop retains every decoded frame before handing them to the caller, with no aggregate budget, which could exhaust memory.
judge.ground_truth_summary: submit_packet sets prev_thread to a VLC-less thread during no-delay draining. ff_thread_flush then propagates NULL coeff_vlc, and unpack_dct_coeffs dereferences it (NULL deref).
judge.reasoning: The task is benign: the PR title says VLCs are initialized once during init, so the NULL coeff_vlc chain is fixed. The scanner's only finding is unrelated. It describes unbounded frame retention in the worker loop, which could exhaust memory (APV decoder). It does not mention prev_thread during draining, flush context propagation, or the vp3 VLC NULL dereference.

criteria: Vulnerable function is ff_dnn_execute_model_tf in libavfilter/dnn/dnn_backend_tf.c
TaskItem 'task' is successfully pushed onto tf_model->task_queue, transferring ownership to the queue
A later error branch (extract_lltask_from_task failure or request_queue pop failure) calls av_freep(&task) while task remains queued
dnn_free_model_tf later walks task_queue and frees the same task, causing a double free
Missing ownership tracking: the task must not be freed after the queue push succeeds
judge.findings_summary: One UseAfterFree finding: the execute_model_tf error path calls ff_dnn_free_model_tf on the shared model. Later owner teardown, result or flush paths then use or free stale model state.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In ff_dnn_execute_model_tf, error branches after a successful ff_queue_push_back(task) free the task. dnn_free_model_tf later frees the same queued TaskItem again, causing a double free.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports a model-wide ff_dnn_free_model_tf call added to execute_model_tf's err label, leading to use-after-free. That is a different function, trigger and sink. The GT is av_freep(&task) after the task was queued in ff_dnn_execute_model_tf, causing a double free during queue teardown. The scanner never mentions the TaskItem or its queue-ownership transfer. The diff for this benign task shows no post-push av_freep(&task), so the GT chain is not present.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Untrusted 32-bit seek_back read from the file tail is used to compute end_pos
end_pos can fall below end_buffer_pos (the start of the allocated buffer)
Guard checks only end_pos < 0 plus the upper bound and omits the end_pos >= end_buffer_pos lower bound
AV_RL32 at end_buffer + (end_pos - end_buffer_pos) + 16 reads before the start of the heap buffer
judge.findings_summary: One OutOfBoundsRead finding: the upper-bound check `end_pos+16 > end` allows a 4-byte AV_RL32 read to overrun the tail buffer end. It explicitly notes the lower-bound check is present.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The get_duration end_pos lower-bound check is missing (end_pos < end_buffer_pos is not rejected), so an attacker-controlled seek_back makes AV_RL32 read before the start of end_buffer.
judge.reasoning: The PR guard checks `end_pos < end_buffer_pos`, so the GT underflow chain is fixed. The scanner reports a different bug: the upper bound allows a 1-4 byte read past the buffer end. It also says outright that the lower-bound check is present. That is an adjacent bug with a different missing guard, not the GT underflow, so it is not detected.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled 32-bit decoded_size read from the codec48 bitstream header
Sink: rle_decode() writes decoded_size bytes into the frm0 frame buffer in the compr==2 path
Missing guard: decoded_size is not checked against ctx->buf_size before the write
Impact: heap out-of-bounds write past the frame buffer
judge.findings_summary: One finding: codec48_block applies packet-controlled motion displacements in compression mode 3 without bounds checks, causing out-of-bounds reads from frm2.
judge.ground_truth_summary: old_codec48 passes an unvalidated attacker-controlled decoded_size to rle_decode in the compr==2 path, causing a heap overflow of frm0. The fix adds a check against ctx->buf_size.
judge.reasoning: The PR already has the fix: the compr==2 path checks decoded_size > ctx->buf_size and rejects the frame before rle_decode. The scanner instead reports out-of-bounds reads caused by motion vectors in codec48_block under compr==3. That is a different trigger, a different sink (read rather than write), and a different missing guard. It does not match the GT, and the GT chain is not active in this snapshot.

criteria: Untrusted rle_raw_size is read from the DWA compressed header
rle_raw_data is allocated with rle_raw_size bytes
The alpha loop reads ai0/ai1 at y*xsize + x and + rle_raw_size/2 across ysize*xsize iterations
There is no check that rle_raw_size >= 2*xsize*ysize, and no INT_MAX cap
The resulting out-of-bounds heap read leaks memory into decoded pixels
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: DWA partial-block heap write, luma three-plane overwrite, zlib OOB read after skip, null/stale AC buffer read, and ignored rle() error. None address the rle_raw_size versus xsize*ysize alpha read.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dwa_uncompress uses untrusted rle_raw_size to allocate rle_raw_data and index ai0/ai1 without verifying it covers 2*xsize*ysize or capping it, causing an OOB heap read. The benign PR already includes these checks.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds a check rejecting rle_raw_size > INT_MAX and a check rejecting 2*xsize*ysize > rle_raw_size. Together these break the GT causal chain. No scanner finding targets the rle_raw_data alpha-loop read. The findings cover other issues: 8x8 block overwrite, luma channel layout mismatch, zlib read past the packet after the skip, missing AC buffer, and ignored RLE error. criteria: Source: file-controlled index_start_position (possibly a huge negative value) feeds the edit_unit clamp in mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset

criteria: Trigger: a remote peer sends repeated PING frames while not reading, so outbound writes are backpressured
Auto-PONG path (ws_enc_add_cntrl/ws_enc_add_pending) encodes each PONG into ws->sendbuf
The guard (enc.payload_remain==0) ignores whether earlier sendbuf bytes were actually flushed
ws->sendbuf uses BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT, so writes allocate past max_chunks
Result: unbounded heap growth of sendbuf, leading to memory exhaustion (DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Auto-PONG enqueue into the soft-limit sendbuf under outbound backpressure keeps appending headers without rollback or a hard cap. Peer PINGs can therefore cause unbounded heap growth.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ws_enc_add_cntrl eagerly encodes auto-PONGs whenever payload_remain==0, ignoring the unsent backlog. The soft-limit sendbuf never rejects writes, so a peer that sends PINGs without reading causes unbounded memory growth.
judge.reasoning: The scanner traces the same chain: peer PINGs reach the auto-PONG path, which appends to the soft-limit sendbuf while the client is backpressured. The guard does not bound unsent bytes, so heap growth is unbounded. It stresses header-without-rollback on CURLE_AGAIN, a narrower framing, but it still names the soft-limit queue and the missing hard cap on unsent control bytes. The PR adds no bound.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: req->path (easy-handle lifetime) is assigned a pointer into connection-owned smbc->share heap memory in smb_parse_url_path
Lifetime mismatch: connection can be freed (smb_conn_dtor frees share) while smb_request still references it
Dangling req->path is later dereferenced (tree-connect/file-open message building or easy dtor), reading freed memory
Missing fix: no private copy/ownership of the path string in the request
judge.findings_summary: One finding at smb.c:991 reports that connection reuse pairs a stale cached share with the new request path. It is classified as a cross-share access/logic issue, not a memory-safety issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: req->path points into smbc->share, which is owned by the connection. When the connection is freed before the easy handle, req->path dangles and is later read: a use-after-free caused by a lifetime mismatch.
judge.reasoning: The scanner flags the same line (req->path = slash) but describes a logic/correctness bug: a reused connection's stale share is combined with a new request path. It never mentions connection-freed memory, a dangling pointer, or use-after-free. The trigger (connection teardown before request) and the lifetime rule are absent. It also assumes the share stays allocated and valid. This is a near match on the same line with a different root cause.

criteria: Trigger: an NTLM-wanting request whose credentials differ from a cached connection reaches the new 'upgrade' fallback
Guard checks only http_ntlm_state == NTLMSTATE_NONE before setting chosen = check
Missing guard: no check that http_negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE
A connection already authenticated via Negotiate/SPNEGO (ntlm state NONE) is wrongly selected
Impact: the second user's request runs over a connection still authenticated as the first user
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the host-NTLM fallback selects a connection before the proxy NTLM checks run, so a later request can inherit another principal's proxy NTLM-authenticated state.
judge.ground_truth_summary: url_match_auth_ntlm fallback reuses connections where only NTLM state is NONE, missing a negotiate-state check. Negotiate-authenticated connections are therefore reused for a different user's request.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds the vulnerable fallback, which checks only NTLM state, so the GT bug is present. The scanner flags the same fallback line, but its missing guard is proxy NTLM credential and state compatibility, skipped by the early continue. It never mentions Negotiate/SPNEGO or http_negotiate_state, which is the GT root cause. That makes it an adjacent bug in the same location, not the exact GT chain.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Curl_auth_gsasl_is_supported calls gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx) when gsasl_client_start fails
gsasl->ctx is not set to NULL after that gsasl_done call
gsasl->ctx persists in the connection state
Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup calls gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx) again with no NULL check, freeing the same context twice
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reported an OOB read from Curl_base64_encode called with zero length and a memory leak of decoded chlg in Curl_auth_gsasl_token. Neither involves gsasl->ctx lifetime.
judge.ground_truth_summary: When gsasl_client_start fails, gsasl_done(ctx) runs but ctx is not nulled. Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup later calls gsasl_done on the stale pointer again, causing a double free.
judge.reasoning: The PR code still contains the GT double free: is_supported frees ctx without nulling it, and cleanup frees it again unconditionally. Neither scanner finding addresses this. One reports an out-of-bounds read from base64 encoding with size zero, the other a leak of the decoded challenge in Curl_auth_gsasl_token. Both are different bugs in the same file.

criteria: Trigger: NULL (clear) passed to CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD on a handle that already holds proxy credentials
setstropt_userpwd parses into fresh temporary u/p locals, which stay NULL
Freeing/overwriting of STRING_PROXYUSERNAME/STRING_PROXYPASSWORD happens only inside the `if(!result && u)` / `if(!result && p)` guards
Result: the old proxy credentials stay in persistent state and are reused or sent by later transfers
Location: lib/setopt.c Curl_vsetopt CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD handler, about lines 1598-1612
judge.findings_summary: One finding: a combined NULL clear of CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD leaves old proxy username and password in place because the guards check u/p for non-null, so later transfers send stale proxy auth.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactor put clearing and replacement of proxy credentials inside u/p non-null guards. Passing NULL to CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD therefore never clears the stored credentials, which leak into later transfers.
judge.reasoning: The scanner points to lib/setopt.c:1607-1612 and names the same trigger (NULL clear), the same mechanism (fresh local u/p pointers plus non-null guards that skip replacement), and the same outcome (stale credentials sent to a later proxy). The PR diff confirms the guards. The PR adds no fix, and the scanner presents the issue as active.

criteria: Trigger: the application sets CURLOPT_REFERER to NULL on a reused handle after an earlier non-NULL referer.
The PR removed the unconditional Curl_bufref_set of state.referer from setopt.c.
Curl_pretransfer in lib/transfer.c updates state.referer only when STRING_SET_REFERER is non-NULL and has no else-branch to clear it.
The old state.referer value survives and is read when the next request's Referer header is built.
The flaw is present in the evaluated PR code and no added guard clears it.
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: clearing CURLOPT_REFERER leaves state.referer dangling because the pretransfer sync is incomplete, and the header builder reads it. Finding 2: disabling AUTOREFERER keeps the redirect-generated referer (adjacent issue).
judge.ground_truth_summary: The PR moved referer bufref sync to Curl_pretransfer but only for non-NULL values. Setting CURLOPT_REFERER to NULL no longer clears state.referer, so a stale Referer is sent on later transfers.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain: CURLOPT_REFERER set to NULL, the removed setopt sync, and the missing clear in Curl_pretransfer (transfer.c:540-544). The stale state.referer then reaches the Referer header builder. It labels this a use-after-free, since the bufref aliases the freed configured string. That is a more precise consequence of the same root cause and missing branch, not a different bug. The PR diff confirms the flaw is present.

criteria: Trigger: mqtt_doing retries an existing remainder by passing mq->sendleftovers to mqtt_send while keeping a local alias to it
mqtt_send fails on Curl_memdup allocation and returns before replacing mq->sendleftovers
mqtt_doing frees the captured alias without clearing the owner member or its count (ownership not detached)
The newly added mqtt_done frees mq->sendleftovers again, which is the second free (sink)
The PR adds no ownership transfer or nulling that breaks this chain
judge.findings_summary: One DoubleFree finding at lib/mqtt.c:703. A retry allocation failure leaves sendleftovers dangling after mqtt_doing frees it, and the new mqtt_done frees it again.
judge.ground_truth_summary: mqtt_doing frees a captured sendleftovers pointer after an mqtt_send allocation failure while the owner still holds it, and the newly added mqtt_done frees it a second time.
judge.reasoning: The scanner gives the exact GT chain. A retry in mqtt_doing aliases sendleftovers, and the Curl_memdup failure in mqtt_send leaves the member unchanged. mqtt_doing frees the alias without clearing it, and the new mqtt_done then frees it again via Curl_safefree. The PR diff confirms that mqtt_done was added with no detach or nulling in mqtt_doing. The location matches line 703, and the suggested remediation matches the GT fix.

criteria: Vulnerable code is lib/http2.c cf_h2_update_local_win, reached through the new write_paused state set in h2_xfer_write_resp and http2_data_pause
Pausing drives the HTTP/2 stream's local receive window to zero
On unpause, nghttp2_submit_window_update is called without first setting nghttp2's internal local window size (no nghttp2_session_set_local_window_size)
Result: a stream whose window reached zero stays blocked or stalled after resume (a LogicError, not memory growth)
judge.findings_summary: One finding: ngtcp2 HTTP/3 replenishes receive credit while cw-pause buffers paused body data in a soft-limit queue, allowing unbounded memory growth. It treats HTTP/2 pause handling as correct.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The write_paused bridge shrinks the HTTP/2 receive window to zero. On unpause, cf_h2_update_local_win submits a window update without setting nghttp2's local window size, so the stream can remain blocked.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports unbounded heap growth in the ngtcp2 HTTP/3 pause queue (cw-pause.c soft limit). That is a different file, trigger and sink. It cites the HTTP/2 window-zeroing code only as a correct negative control. It never mentions the missing local-window setter or the stuck stream on unpause, so it treats the GT path as working correctly.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: a transfer reaches tool_read_cb() while per->uploadfile is NULL
Sink: strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") in tool_read_cb (src/tool_cb_rea.c ~line 95)
Missing guard: no NULL check on per->uploadfile before the strcmp
Impact: NULL pointer dereference / segfault introduced by the new non-blocking stdin branch
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: the Windows stdin bridge accepts the first loopback peer without authentication, so a competing local process could receive stdin upload bytes (src/tool_doswin.c).
judge.ground_truth_summary: tool_read_cb calls strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") without a NULL check. Transfers that use the read callback with a NULL uploadfile crash with a NULL dereference.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff still shows the unguarded strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") in tool_read_cb, so the GT bug is present. The scanner's only finding is a different bug: an unauthenticated loopback accept race in tool_doswin.c that could leak stdin data. It does not mention tool_read_cb, a NULL uploadfile, or the strcmp sink. Its quoted strcmp code is in tool_operate.c, used only as the entrypoint.

criteria: Curl_cookie_getlist returns live jar-owned Cookie pointers/nodes rather than independent copies
Curl_http_cookies releases CURL_LOCK_DATA_COOKIE right after getlist, before traversing the list
Traversal dereferences cookie nodes and fields after unlock
A concurrent locked cookie mutation on a shared jar (e.g., Set-Cookie replacement) can free a selected node, causing use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: UseAfterFree: borrowed intrusive cookie nodes used after Curl_http_cookies drops the share lock; a concurrent replacement can free them or a second selection can relink them during traversal and destroy.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The 2024 refactor returns live Cookie pointers, but Curl_http_cookies unlocks the cookie share before traversing them. A concurrent Set-Cookie can free nodes mid-traversal, causing a UAF.
judge.reasoning: The scanner names the same chain. Getlist links jar-owned Cookie nodes, Curl_http_cookies unlocks before traversing them (http.c 2263-2274), and a concurrent Set-Cookie replacement frees the selected cookie. The PR diff confirms the unlock comes before the loop, and no fix is present. The scanner's note that cross-thread cookie sharing is documented as unsupported is a caveat, not a denial; it calls the issue reportable.

criteria: tftp_state_timeout() detects expiry via Curl_timeleft() returning a negative value
The expired branch sets FIN/TFTP_ERR_TIMEOUT but returns literal 0 instead of the negative timeout_ms
Caller tftp_multi_statemach() guard changed from '<= 0' to '< 0', so a 0 return no longer aborts
Result: CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT is not returned and the transfer keeps running despite the expired timeout
judge.findings_summary: One finding: an expired TFTP timeout is converted to 0 by tftp_state_timeout(), and the changed '< 0' check accepts it. The transfer continues instead of aborting with a timeout error.
judge.ground_truth_summary: tftp_state_timeout() returns 0 instead of the negative timeout_ms when the timer has expired. Combined with the caller's guard tightening to '< 0', this skips the CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT abort.
judge.reasoning: The scanner traces the exact chain. Curl_timeleft() returns a negative value on expiry, tftp_state_timeout() replaces it with 0 at lines 1210-1213, and the changed '< 0' guard in tftp_multi_statemach() accepts 0. As a result, the timeout abort is skipped and the transfer stays live. The PR diff confirms each step and adds no mitigation. The scanner's remediation, returning the negative timeout_ms, matches the GT.

criteria: Location is Curl_ssl_scache_take in lib/vtls/vtls_scache.c
Curl_ssl_scache_unlock is called before the trace logging code runs
Trace logging reads the shared peer->sessions list via Curl_llist_count without holding the lock
Concurrent threads can modify or free peer/sessions, causing a data race or use-after-free read
judge.findings_summary: One finding: GnuTLS+ngtcp2 caches a NewSessionTicket without requiring a verified peer, letting a later connection send 0-RTT HTTP/3 data to an unverified peer.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Curl_ssl_scache_take releases the scache lock before trace logging, which reads peer->sessions via Curl_llist_count. This is an unlocked shared-list read (data race, possible use-after-free).
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows the bug is present: the unlock comes before CURL_TRC_CF, which calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions). The scanner instead reports a trust-boundary problem: an unverified QUIC peer's ticket gets cached and later authorizes 0-RTT data in curl_ngtcp2.c. It only mentions Curl_ssl_scache_take as a caller. It does not identify the post-unlock read, the lock scope, or any race. Different bug class, sink and root cause.

criteria: CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYSTATUS (conn_config->verifystatus) is requested for the connection
ossl_connect_step1 still loads/offers a cached session under ssl_config->primary.sessionid without a verifystatus guard and sets reused_session
servercert at openssl.c:4345 skips verifystatus() when connssl->reused_session is true
Result: the connection completes without the requested OCSP status check (fail-open revocation control)
judge.findings_summary: One finding: reused_session is set when a cached session is offered in step1, before SSL_connect. servercert at 4345 then skips the requested verifystatus OCSP check, so a revoked certificate can be accepted.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The PR makes servercert skip verifystatus when reused_session is set. Step1 still loads cached sessions when verifystatus is requested, so the OCSP check is bypassed. The fix gates the session cache with !verifystatus.
judge.reasoning: The scanner ties the same trigger (cache lookup at step1 offering a session and setting reused_session while verifystatus is on) to the same sink (the servercert gate at 4345). It shows the requested OCSP check is bypassed, and the PR adds no guard. However, the scanner frames the flaw as stale pre-handshake state and implies a real resumption may skip OCSP. The GT says the cache should not be used at all when verifystatus is set. Same chain, narrower framing, so partial confidence.

criteria: Vulnerable site is reuse_conn in lib/url.c, which shallow-copies old_conn->conn_to_host into conn
After the copy, the source's conn_to_host.encalloc is not NULLed, while host.rawalloc/encalloc and conn_to_host.rawalloc are
Both structs then alias the same encalloc heap allocation
old_conn teardown (conn_free -> Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname) frees encalloc
A later free or use through conn->conn_to_host causes a double free or use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: DoubleFree at lib/url.c:3540: reuse_conn copies conn_to_host but leaves old encalloc non-null; conn_free(old_conn) frees it; later teardown frees it again or reads it.
judge.ground_truth_summary: reuse_conn copies conn_to_host from old_conn, NULLs only rawalloc and not encalloc, so conn_free(old_conn) and the later cleanup of conn both free the same encalloc.
judge.reasoning: The scanner names the exact incomplete move in reuse_conn: conn_to_host is copied and only rawalloc is cleared, so encalloc is left shared. The newly added conn_free(old_conn) frees it, and the later free of conn->conn_to_host is a double free. The PR diff confirms this chain, and nothing in the PR clears conn_to_host.encalloc.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: RTMP* is allocated and registered in connection meta with the rtmp_conn_dtor destructor before RTMP_SetupURL
RTMP_SetupURL failure path directly calls RTMP_Free(r) without removing the meta entry
Connection teardown (disconnect or meta cleanup) invokes rtmp_conn_dtor on the same stale pointer
Result is a double free (RTMP_Close/RTMP_Free) triggered by a malformed RTMP URL in rtmp_setup_connection
judge.findings_summary: One DoubleFree finding at curl_rtmp.c:237. The RTMP_SetupURL failure branch frees r while it remains in connection meta, and teardown then invokes rtmp_conn_dtor to free it again.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Moving RTMP* ownership to the connection meta hash left the manual RTMP_Free on the URL-parse-failure path. The meta destructor later frees the same pointer again: a double free in rtmp_setup_connection.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff keeps RTMP_Free(r) on the RTMP_SetupURL failure path after Curl_conn_meta_set registers rtmp_conn_dtor. The scanner finding identifies the same trigger (setup URL failure), the same first free, the stale meta entry, and the destructor's second free during teardown. No mitigation exists in the PR.

criteria: Location is Curl_get_line in lib/curl_get_line.c, specifically the while(1) fgets loop
Trigger: fgets() returns NULL because of a non-EOF I/O error, so feof() stays false
Missing guard: no ferror() check and no return on the NULL-fgets / non-EOF branch
Effect: rlen is 0, there is no trailing newline and eof is false, so the loop retries forever (infinite loop / DoS)
The PR's rewrite introduces the defect and adds no mitigation
judge.findings_summary: The scanner reports that Curl_get_line keeps calling fgets on a non-EOF read error without checking ferror. This causes an infinite loop that blocks the cookie, HSTS, alt-svc and netrc loaders.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The rewritten Curl_get_line loop exits only on EOF, a completed line or an append error. A persistent fgets I/O error leaves feof false, so the loop spins forever.
judge.reasoning: The scanner flags Curl_get_line lines 49-69 and names the same trigger (fgets returns NULL while feof is false on a read error), the same missing guard (no ferror check or return), and the same infinite-retry result. The PR diff confirms the old else-break fallback was removed and nothing replaced it. The scanner's lower likelihood rating does not contradict that the bug is present.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: legacy ch_layouts option string parsed in common_init of buffersink.c
av_realloc_array result stored in local tmp but never assigned back to buf->channel_layouts
Subsequent memset/element access dereferences stale field (NULL on first iteration, dangling later)
Vulnerable code present in evaluated PR diff with no assignment fix
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reports a NullPointerDereference at buffersink.c:203. The realloc result is kept only in tmp and not assigned to buf->channel_layouts, so the memset writes through NULL when the legacy ch_layouts option is used.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In common_init, the av_realloc_array result is not assigned back to buf->channel_layouts, so the memset dereferences NULL or a dangling pointer when parsing ch_layouts. Secondary issue: the memset clears one element instead of two.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows tmp from av_realloc_array is checked but never assigned to buf->channel_layouts, and memset then writes through the stale NULL field. The scanner names the same trigger (the ch_layouts option), the same missing assignment, the same memset sink, and the same location (line 203). It omits the dangling-pointer and one-element memset details, but these are secondary. The core causal chain matches exactly.

criteria: Source: num_parameters read via ffio_read_leb in audio_element_obu for Channel (type 0) elements
Missing guard: no upper bound (max 2) on num_parameters; only Scene elements are checked for 0
Sink: the loop calls param_parse repeatedly, allowing the same parameter type (DEMIXING/RECON_GAIN) more than once
Impact: element->demixing_info/recon_gain_info pointer is overwritten by a new allocation, leaking the earlier one (memory DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: substream index OOB in layer config, negative index in the IPCM table, sound_system map OOB, AAC rewrite bit overflow, and unbounded LEB counts driving allocations. None cover num_parameters or the param pointer leak.
judge.ground_truth_summary: audio_element_obu does not cap num_parameters at 2 for Channel elements. Duplicate param types then overwrite the demixing/recon_gain param pointers, leaking memory (CVE-2025-1816).
judge.reasoning: No scanner finding mentions num_parameters, duplicate parameter types, or the overwrite of demixing_info/recon_gain_info that leaks memory. Finding 5 covers unbounded counts (subblocks, substreams, labels, submixes) causing large allocations. That shares the resource-exhaustion class but has a different trigger, sink, and mechanism. The other findings are unrelated OOB issues.

criteria: Trigger: the fps/rate option is an unbounded VIDEO_RATE (formerly a bounded int) and the divisibility check was removed
Derived step = sample_rate/(fps*count) can exceed fft_len
remaining_fill is set to step after a CQT plot with no step<=fft_len bound
j = fft_len - remaining_fill becomes negative in filter_frame
Writes to fft_data[j+m] at negative offsets cause a heap buffer overflow
judge.findings_summary: One BufferOverflow finding: an unchecked rational frame rate yields a step larger than fft_len, stored in remaining_fill. The next pass computes a negative index and writes before fft_data.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The showcqt rewrite makes fps an unbounded VIDEO_RATE and drops the divisibility check. Step can then exceed fft_len, so j = fft_len - remaining_fill goes negative and fft_data writes underflow the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: The scanner traces the same chain. The rate option is an unbounded VIDEO_RATE, so the derived step can exceed fft_len. That step is stored unchecked in remaining_fill, and filter_frame then computes a negative j = fft_len - remaining_fill and writes fft_data[j+m] out of bounds. The PR code in the diff confirms the relaxed rate option and the step computation. No guard is added. Omitting the removed divisibility check is minor.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger is a monochrome (chroma_format_idc==0) SPS that the PR newly accepts
Vulnerable operation is the PCM length calculation in hls_pcm_sample
The chroma contribution to length is not guarded by chroma_format_idc, even though the put_pcm calls are
hshift/vshift are 0 for YUV400, so length is inflated by about 2*cb_size^2*bit_depth_chroma
Result: skip_bytes over-skips, desynchronizing the bitstream parse
judge.findings_summary: One finding: monochrome SPS lets the SEI decoded-picture-hash parser read three component digests instead of one, overreading the payload when the bit reader is unchecked.
judge.ground_truth_summary: hls_pcm_sample's length calculation includes the chroma planes for YUV400 even though the put_pcm calls skip them. Inflated length makes skip_bytes over-skip and desynchronize the bitstream.
judge.reasoning: The scanner identifies the same trigger (monochrome SPS acceptance) but a different sink: the decoded-picture-hash SEI loop in hevc_sei.c, which reads three components. It never mentions hls_pcm_sample, the unguarded PCM length calculation, or skip_bytes desynchronization. This is a same-trigger, different-sink near match, so it does not count as detected.

criteria: Identifies get_eia608_packet, reached from mov_read_packet, as parsing c608 samples
Recognizes that a c608 sample can hold multiple atoms (cdat/cdt2), each with its own 8-byte header
Identifies that the single avio_skip(pb, 8) skips only the first header, so later atom headers are emitted as caption byte pairs
Notes that the hardcoded 0xFC cc_type cannot mark field-2 (cdt2) data, and/or that the output size ignores the extra headers
judge.findings_summary: One finding: get_eia608_packet allocates from the untrusted declared sample size, skips av_get_packet's limits, and treats EOF reads as zeros, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion on truncated MOV files.
judge.ground_truth_summary: get_eia608_packet assumes a c608 sample has one atom. It skips only the first 8-byte header, treats later cdat/cdt2 headers as caption data, and hardcodes 0xFC, so field-2 data is mislabeled and sizing is wrong.
judge.reasoning: The flawed single-atom parsing is present in the PR. The scanner instead reports memory/CPU exhaustion on truncated input: allocation is sized from the declared sample size, ffio_limit is bypassed, and avio_r8 returns zeros at EOF. It never mentions multiple atoms, subsequent atom headers being misread as caption data, or field-1/field-2 misidentification. Same function and sink, but a different root cause and trigger, so this is an adjacent bug.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: The trigger is the new ff_dovi_configure() wrapper, which round-trips through an AVCodecParameters and calls avcodec_parameters_to_context(avctx, codecpar).
avcodec_parameters_to_context frees all existing avctx->coded_side_data, including the CPB props, and replaces them with copies.
A caller (libaomenc aom_init) keeps the cpb_props pointer from ff_encode_add_cpb_side_data() across the ff_dovi_configure call.
The caller later writes through the stale pointer, causing a heap use-after-free.
No PR change keeps the side-data pointers valid or makes the caller reacquire them.
judge.findings_summary: One UseAfterFree finding: the ff_dovi_configure round-trip via avcodec_parameters_to_context frees coded_side_data, so libaom's retained cpb_props pointer dangles and is written to later.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ff_dovi_configure's new AVCodecParameters round-trip calls avcodec_parameters_to_context, which frees and replaces coded_side_data. Callers such as libaomenc then hold a dangling cpb_props pointer and write to it (UAF).
judge.reasoning: The scanner gives the exact GT chain: aom_init keeps cpb_props, the new wrapper calls avcodec_parameters_to_context, which frees coded_side_data, and later cpb_props writes are use-after-free. The PR diff shows the round-trip is present and nothing in the PR mitigates it. Locations match dovi_rpuenc.c:226, libaomenc.c and codec_par.c.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Task is successfully pushed onto tf_model->task_queue, transferring ownership to the queue
PR-added av_freep(&task) in an error branch after the successful push (extract_lltask failure and/or request pop failure)
Task is not unlinked from task_queue before being freed
Later teardown (dnn_free_model_tf queue walk) or queue consumer frees/dereferences the same task again, causing a double free
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the error path frees the whole model through an interior pointer (UAF). Finding 2: the extract-failure branch frees a task still in task_queue, so teardown or result collection dereferences and double-frees it.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In ff_dnn_execute_model_tf, the PR adds av_freep(&task) in error branches after ff_queue_push_back succeeded. The task stays in task_queue, so dnn_free_model_tf frees it again (double free).
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT chain. The task is pushed to task_queue, then the PR-added av_freep in the extract_lltask_from_task failure branch frees it without unlinking it. dnn_free_model_tf teardown later frees it again. The finding labels this UseAfterFree but explicitly describes the second free. It discounts the second branch (request pop) as unreachable, but covering one GT branch with the exact root cause is sufficient. Finding 1 is a separate bug.

criteria: Vulnerable code is in dump_stream_group in libavformat/dump.c, in the AV_STREAM_GROUP_PARAMS_TILE_GRID case
The loop bound comes from tile_grid->nb_tiles instead of stg->nb_streams
The array subscript tile_grid->offsets[i].idx comes from parsed, untrusted container metadata
There is no check that offsets[i].idx < stg->nb_streams before indexing stg->streams[]
The result is an out-of-bounds read of stg->streams[] and a dereference of an invalid AVStream pointer (st->index, printed[])
judge.findings_summary: One OutOfBoundsRead finding at dump.c:786. The unchecked offsets[].idx indexes stg->streams; duplicate tile references or global overlay indices from the MOV parser can exceed nb_streams, causing a crash.

The scanner names this exact sink at dump.c:786, the same untrusted source (HEIF/AVIF tile metadata), the same missing guard (idx < nb_streams), and the same mismatch between nb_tiles and nb_streams. criteria: Source/trigger: an attacker-controlled 32-bit seek_back value read from the file tail buffer
end_pos is computed as end_buffer_pos + offset - seek_back + 8 and can fall below end_buffer_pos
The guard checks only end_pos < 0 and the upper bound, with no end_pos >= end_buffer_pos lower-bound check

The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR's get_duration
