judge.reasoning: Finding 1 points to the front-loaded native_context() call at line 2763 in SerializeObject. It names context-less maps whose meta-map is the RO meta_map root, including global proxies, as the trigger. It identifies the missing meta_map guard and attributes the regression to the hoisting. The PR diff shows the unguarded call. The finding focuses on remote rather than detached globals, but the root cause is the same.

criteria: Vulnerable location is the Float16 ±0 early-return branch in TypedElementsAccessor::LastIndexOfValueImpl (elements.cc)
Trigger: the fromIndex ToInteger conversion runs user valueOf, which shrinks a resizable ArrayBuffer, leaving start_from stale
The new branch returns before the post-conversion GetLength re-read and start_from clamp
Sink: do-while loop reads data_ptr + k with k >= current typed_array_length, an OOB read
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the Float16 ±0 fast path in LastIndexOfValueImpl bypasses the start_from clamp after the RAB shrinks in valueOf, causing an OOB read. Includes a PoC and a fix suggestion.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The Float16 zero special case in LastIndexOfValueImpl exits early with a stale start_from, before the post-ToInteger length re-check. A RAB shrink during fromIndex conversion then causes an OOB read.
judge.reasoning: The scanner identifies the same function and the same Float16 zero branch. It names the same trigger (valueOf resizing the RAB during fromIndex conversion), the same bypassed guard (the GetLength re-read and clamp), and the same sink (GetImpl(data_ptr + k) past the current length). The PR diff confirms the branch sits before the clamp and adds no mitigation. Labeling it BufferOverflow rather than OutOfBoundsRead is immaterial, since it describes a read.

criteria: Location is Typer::Visitor::ObjectIsArrayBufferView in turbofan-typer.cc
TypedArray is a distinct bitset, disjoint from OtherObject, after TypeJSCreateTypedArray/constants were retyped
The PR adds an Is(TypedArray) true-return but leaves the false guard as !type.Maybe(OtherObject)
Union types containing TypedArray plus non-OtherObject types (e.g. TypedArray|Boolean) are wrongly typed singleton_false_
The wrong typing causes a typer contradiction or miscompilation
judge.findings_summary: One finding: an incomplete fix in ObjectIsArrayBufferView. The OtherObject-based false guard wrongly folds unions containing TypedArray to false. The scanner proposes adding TypedArray to the Maybe check.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ObjectIsArrayBufferView keeps the !Maybe(OtherObject) false guard after TypedArray became a disjoint type. Unions like TypedArray|Boolean return singleton_false_, which causes a typer contradiction and an UpdateType FATAL.
judge.reasoning: The scanner pinpoints the unchanged !type.Maybe(OtherObject) false-guard in ObjectIsArrayBufferView. It explains that TypedArray is disjoint from OtherObject, so unions like TypedArray|Undefined are typed false even though the value can be a typed array. That matches the GT root cause and is present in the PR snapshot. The scanner describes the consequence as miscompilation rather than the UpdateType FATAL, but the causal guard defect is identical. Its hedge on security impact does not deny the bug.

criteria: New kTransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap case added to NodeProperties::InferMapsUnsafe
Only the trivial IsSame(receiver, object) aliasing case is handled
Non-IsSame path breaks without setting result = kUnreliableMaps, unlike other side-effecting opcodes
Receiver and object may alias at runtime via different SSA nodes, so the op can change the receiver's map
Callers therefore get stale maps treated as reliable and optimize on a wrong type
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1-2 identify the missing kUnreliableMaps in the InferMapsUnsafe TransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap case when receivers alias. The other findings cover frame-state/Checkpoint hardening and AssumeMap concerns.
judge.ground_truth_summary: InferMapsUnsafe's new TransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap case handles only IsSame and breaks without setting kUnreliableMaps. Aliasing nodes then receive stale maps marked reliable, leading to wrong optimizations.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1, and Finding 2 as well, matches the GT exactly. Both point to node-properties.cc:447-455, where the non-IsSame branch breaks without setting kUnreliableMaps. Both explain that aliasing SSA nodes let the map transition go unnoticed, so stale maps come back as reliable to MapInference and its callers. The PR diff shows this code. Nothing in the PR mitigates it, and neither finding calls the issue hypothetical or fixed.

criteria: Untrusted wasm bytes with the 0xfa AsmJs prefix reach DECODE(AsmJs) through the general opcode handler table
read_prefixed_opcode LEB-decodes the index, so index > 0xff gives (0xfa<<12)|index, and index > 0xfff gives 0 with an error
The decoded opcode is forwarded to DecodeAsmJsOpcode with no validation
DecodeAsmJsOpcode uses V8_ASSUME((opcode>>8)==kAsmJsPrefix) instead of a VALIDATE guard, so a DCHECK abort occurs in debug builds and UB in release
The is_asmjs_module check runs only after the assume and does not prevent the violation
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: V8_ASSUME in DecodeAsmJsOpcode is violable through a 0xfa prefix with LEB index > 0xff or > 0xfff, causing a DCHECK abort or UB. Finding 2: signature aliasing on the low byte (hardening only).
judge.ground_truth_summary: DecodeAsmJsOpcode asserts the AsmJs prefix with V8_ASSUME rather than validating it. LEB-decoded indices > 0xff from read_prefixed_opcode break the assumption, causing a DCHECK crash in debug builds or UB in release.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain exactly: 0xfa prefix, then LEB index > 0xff or > 0xfff in read_prefixed_opcode, then DECODE(AsmJs), then the violated V8_ASSUME in DecodeAsmJsOpcode, giving a DCHECK crash or release UB. The PR diff confirms the unguarded assume. The finding's triage note about low release impact does not deny the active DCHECK/UB vulnerability. No mitigation exists in the PR.

criteria: In ResumeJSObject, property_index is set to descriptor_idx unconditionally, outside the kWithMapCache-only block
kBuildingMapCache (and kWithoutMapCache) mode uses descriptor_idx as the field index without validating descriptor order == field order
The resulting slot load (in-object offset or property_array index) reads the wrong or out-of-layout property slot
The only guard is DCHECK_EQ(descriptor_idx, field_index); it is absent in release, so the check fails in debug and access is wrong in release
The finding asserts this as an active, reachable defect rather than a hypothetical hardening concern
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: a map is cached as true despite skipped keys (escaping injection); map cache state is lost across an encoding change; descriptor_idx is used as the field index in all modes, but this is dismissed as hypothetical hardening.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ResumeJSObject assigns property_index = descriptor_idx unconditionally, so kBuildingMapCache mode uses descriptor order as the field index without validation. This causes a DCHECK failure in debug and wrong-slot or out-of-layout reads in release.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 names the exact location and mechanism: descriptor_idx replaces field_index() in all modes, guarded only by a DCHECK. However, it states the invariant holds and calls the issue a hardening gap, not a demonstrated out-of-bounds read. Under the strict rules, a hypothetical or not-demonstrated description does not count. Findings 1 and 2 cover adjacent map-cache correctness bugs (escaping and lost cache state), not the GT's field-index root cause.

criteria: Lazy new-space page allocation breaks the invariant that allocation failure implies to-space is at target capacity
EnsureAllocation slow path in main-allocator.cc lacks a guard (to_space current_capacity_ >= target_capacity_) before calling AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity
AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity is reached when Available() equals the full target capacity (Capacity = max(current, target), Size ~0)
DCHECKs in AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity (Available < size_in_bytes, !AddFreshPage) fire when fresh-page allocation fails from OOM before reaching target
judge.findings_summary: Ten findings: page-pool reuse UAF, MakeUnusedPagesInToSpaceIterable null current_page, Shrink rewinding live pages, an age-mark loop null bound, and page_low/high null deref. None covers the EnsureAllocation capacity guard.
judge.ground_truth_summary: With lazy growth, EnsureAllocation can call AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity before to-space reaches target capacity, for example on an OOM fresh-page failure. Available() is then the full target capacity, which violates DCHECK_LT(Available(), size).
judge.reasoning: No finding identifies the missing capacity guard in EnsureAllocation. None describes the violated precondition of AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity that Available() < size when page allocation fails early. Findings 5 and 7 cite AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity only as a way for to-space to exceed target, which feeds a different Shrink/RewindPages UAF hypothesis. The remaining findings cover page-pool reuse, iterability, and null-pointer concerns, which are adjacent issues.

criteria: Regular WASM_FUNCTION code now emits SetStackPointer (central stack switch) around Fast API calls
CodeGenerator::AssembleCode SetFPRelativeOnly guard omits WASM_FUNCTION code kind
ARM64 SlotToMemOperand converts FP-relative slots to SP-relative operands when FPRelativeOnly is false
SP-relative accesses during the stack-switch window hit the wrong (central) stack memory, corrupting/misreading slots
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: C-API wrapper missing central-stack switch (two findings), WKI fast-API fallback hitting Unreachable, and a kRuntimeTypeError runtime call made before the stack switch. None address the SP-relative operand guard.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The SetFPRelativeOnly guard in AssembleCode excludes WASM_FUNCTION. After this PR adds SetStackPointer to regular wasm Fast API calls, ARM64 may use SP-relative slot operands while SP points to the central stack.
judge.reasoning: No finding mentions the FPRelativeOnly guard, the code-generator code-kind check, or SP-relative operand generation in ARM64 SlotToMemOperand. The findings cover different issues: missing stack switches in the C-API wrapper, an Unreachable on the WKI fallback path, and a kRuntimeTypeError CEntry path. All of these are adjacent bugs. The PR's wasm switching paths do support the GT chain, but none of the findings identify it.

criteria: Fast-iterable cache state lives on the shared DescriptorArray rather than per-map or per-invocation
ResumeJSObject<kUnknown> iterates only nof_descriptors = map->NumberOfOwnDescriptors(), a possible prefix of the shared array
End-of-loop promotion to kJsonFast lacks a nof_descriptors == descriptors->number_of_descriptors() guard
A later stringify of a child map sharing the array takes the kJsonFast path, skips validation of unchecked tail descriptors, and assumes descriptor_idx == field_index, causing a wrong read or crash
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: shared DescriptorArray marked kJsonFast after validating only the parent map's prefix, so a child map wrongly takes the fast path. Finding 2: an adjacent issue where keys of undefined/symbol-valued properties are skipped before validation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ResumeJSObject promotes a shared DescriptorArray to kJsonFast after iterating only NumberOfOwnDescriptors, possibly fewer than number_of_descriptors(). Child maps then use the fast path and assume descriptor_idx == field_index on unvalidated descriptors, causing a DCHECK crash or wrong reads.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It states that only NumberOfOwnDescriptors is iterated and the whole shared DescriptorArray is still set kJsonFast via set_fast_iterable_if. A child map sharing the array then skips the checks and assumes property_index == descriptor_idx. It proposes the same nof_descriptors == number_of_descriptors() guard. The PR diff shows the unguarded promotion and adds no mitigation. The 'TypeConfusion' label is only a different consequence framing of the same root cause.

criteria: kArchCallCFunction/kArchCallCFunctionWithFrameState are placed after kArchCallBuiltinPointer, outside the IsCallWithDescriptorFlags() range check
MiscField for the CFunction opcodes holds ParamField/FPParamField counts instead of CallDescriptor::flags
VisitCall therefore cannot encode kHasExceptionHandler for fast API C calls
The code generators (e.g. x64 AssembleArchInstruction) never register an exception handler at the fast API call site
A throwing fast API call then traps because no handler is registered
judge.findings_summary: 40 findings: missing opcode cases on ppc/s390/riscv/loong64, ineffective lazy deopt at fast C call sites, stale fast_c_call_threw_exception flag, a CFG bug on overload failure, and d8 helper issues. None covers the dropped exception-handler flag or descriptor-flags range.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new CFunction opcodes fall outside IsCallWithDescriptorFlags (arch_opcode <= kArchCallBuiltinPointer). MiscField holds parameter counts instead of flags, so kHasExceptionHandler is never encoded and no exception handler is registered for throwing fast API calls.
judge.reasoning: The GT chain is present in the PR: the CFunction opcodes sit outside the descriptor-flags range, so the exception-handler flag is dropped. No finding names this. Findings 1, 4 and 17 cite instruction-codes.h and VisitCall, but they report missing cases on other architectures. The rest cover lazy-deopt patching, stale-flag desync, or graph-builder CFG issues. These are adjacent bugs in the same files, so they count as near matches.

criteria: KnownMapsMerger::IntersectWithKnownNodeAspects now yields EmptyNodeType when every known map is filtered out by IsInstanceOfNodeType
BuildCheckMaps subset/done branch returns Done without detecting that the combined merger/object type is empty (impossible)
Missing guard: no unconditional deopt or abort when CombineType(merger.node_type(), GetType(object)) is empty
Dead-code graph continues with an empty-typed object into store lowering
Sink: BuildStoreTaggedFieldNoWriteBarrier's DCHECK(CanElideWriteBarrier) fails because of the impossible type
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the BuildCheckMaps subset branch elides the check on an empty intersection; it is self-assessed as sound and not demonstrated. Finding 2: GetSmiValue lacks an empty-type guard. Finding 3: the constant fast-path uses a CheckValueEqualsString alternative.
judge.ground_truth_summary: After EmptyNodeType is returned for empty map intersections, BuildCheckMaps lacks an impossible-type guard. Dead code then proceeds with an empty object type, and BuildStoreTaggedFieldNoWriteBarrier's DCHECK(CanElideWriteBarrier) fails.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 does flag the BuildCheckMaps subset branch that returns Done with an empty intersect set and suggests a deopt guard. But it claims the empty type is never propagated, since IntersectType is an OR. Its sink is a stale-map type confusion, not the write-barrier elision DCHECK. Its own assessment calls the path sound dead code that needs a separate, undemonstrated bug. That makes it adjacent and dismissed, not a match.

criteria: Empty NodeType introduced as a dead-code sentinel, with NodeTypeIs treating empty as a subset of every type
TryBuildStoreField double-field/transition path reads the accumulator without checking for an empty type
Empty-typed value is wrapped in Float64ToHeapNumberForField and passed to BuildStoreTaggedField
CanElideWriteBarrier gives an inconsistent answer for that value, causing a DCHECK/type contradiction
The missing guard is an early bailout in TryBuildStoreField for empty-typed values
judge.findings_summary: 13 findings on empty-type propagation via string sub-leaves, EnsureType/CheckType elision, GetFloat64ForToNumber Smi path, GetInternalizedString, TaggedEqual folding, and NodeTypeMayBeNullOrUndefined. None covers store-field or write-barrier.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Type refactor makes the empty type a subset of all types. TryBuildStoreField lacks an empty-type bailout on the double-field transition store, so the value reaches BuildStoreTaggedField/CanElideWriteBarrier and causes a write-barrier DCHECK contradiction.
judge.reasoning: Scanner findings 8 and 12 cover the general idea that empty types satisfy every NodeTypeIs check. No finding names TryBuildStoreField, the double-field store path, Float64ToHeapNumberForField, BuildStoreTaggedField or CanElideWriteBarrier/write-barrier analysis. The findings focus on string leaf staleness, GetFloat64ForToNumber, GetInternalizedString and equality folding. These are adjacent sinks, not the GT chain, and are mostly marked speculative.

criteria: Vulnerable function is the SIMD single-char atom matcher RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern
Uses a local matches accumulator initialized to 0 and then assigns *number_of_matches = matches instead of accumulating
Caller's MatchGlobalAtom cache TryGet pre-fills number_of_matches on a cache hit, making it an in-out parameter
The overwritten (possibly zero) count is written back to the cache via TryInsert, so a later call hits DCHECK_GT(number_of_matches, 0) or returns a wrong count
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the one-char SIMD path overwrites the cached match count, corrupting the cache and triggering DCHECK_GT. Finding 2: the scalar tail loop reads one element past the subject end.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The SIMD rewrite assigns *number_of_matches = matches instead of adding to it. This discards the count pre-filled on a cache hit, stores 0 in the cache, and makes the next call fail DCHECK_GT.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the assignment at line 2249 that replaces the count, the TryGet pre-fill on a cache hit, the corrupted value written back through TryInsert, and the later DCHECK_GT failure. The PR diff shows the assignment with no accumulation. Finding 2 is an unrelated over-read, which does not affect the verdict.

criteria: Vulnerable code is in Uint8ArrayToBase64 (builtins-typed-array.cc ~677)
uint8array->GetBuffer()->backing_store() is called inside a DisallowGarbageCollection no_gc scope
GetBuffer() may allocate on the heap (it materializes the JSArrayBuffer for on-heap typed arrays)
Allocating inside no_gc breaks the GC invariant (DCHECK failure in debug builds)
Fix: read the source with DataPtr(), which does not allocate
judge.findings_summary: Six findings. #2 identifies the allocating GetBuffer() inside the no_gc scope with DataPtr() as the fix. Others cover int truncation, a byte_offset logic error, a byte_length double-fetch, SAB races and bootstrapper casts.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Uint8ArrayToBase64 calls GetBuffer()->backing_store() inside DisallowGarbageCollection. GetBuffer may allocate, which triggers a DCHECK failure; the fix is DataPtr().
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 names the same call, GetBuffer() inside DisallowGarbageCollection in toBase64 at line 677. It explains that GetBuffer can allocate (materializing the buffer for on-heap arrays) and recommends DataPtr(), which matches the GT exactly. It adds a speculative release-build UAF angle, but the root cause, sink and fix are identical. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code present with no mitigation.

criteria: Located in VisitSpeculativeAdditiveOp in simplified-lowering.cc
The new outer guard BothInputsAre(node, Type::Signed32()) is too narrow and excludes Unsigned32 inputs that the old kAdditiveSafeIntegerOrMinusZero check covered
Unsigned32 inputs therefore skip the Int32Add/Sub path and fall through to a different lowering path
The two phases assign different UseInfo to the same input, violating monotonicity between PROPAGATE and LOWER
Consequence is an IsUseLessGeneral DCHECK failure in debug builds, or incorrect code in release builds
judge.findings_summary: Three findings. One: a typer range mismatch on the word32-truncated path. Two: SpeculativeNumberAdd reaching UNREACHABLE via the Signed32 branch. Three: restriction_type causing a phase mismatch. None cites the Unsigned32 exclusion.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactor narrowed the guard to Type::Signed32(), so Unsigned32 inputs miss the Int32 path. This causes a UseInfo mismatch between PROPAGATE and LOWER and trips the monotonicity DCHECK.
judge.reasoning: No finding identifies the Signed32 guard as excluding Unsigned32 inputs. Finding 2 targets the same branch but raises a different issue: an opcode mismatch that reaches UNREACHABLE. Finding 3 describes a PROPAGATE/LOWER mismatch, but its trigger is restriction_type in CanSpeculateAdditiveSafeInteger, an adjacent bug. The scanner also treats this code as the post-fix version rather than recognizing the regression.

criteria: Trigger: setFromHex is called on a zero-length Uint8Array
Missing guard: no array_length==0 early return after the detached/out-of-bounds checks
Sink: uint8array->DataPtr() returns nullptr for a zero-length array and is passed to ArrayBufferFromHex
Impact: null pointer dereference/crash inside ArrayBufferFromHex even though output_length is clamped to 0
judge.findings_summary: Reported: scalar-loop OOB write in ArrayBufferFromHex, SAB UNIMPLEMENTED abort, toBase64 GC hazard, NEON vmovn validation bug, toHex ignoring byte_offset. None mentions a null DataPtr on a zero-length array.
judge.ground_truth_summary: setFromHex has no array_length==0 check, so a zero-length Uint8Array's null DataPtr() is passed to ArrayBufferFromHex, causing a null pointer dereference crash.
judge.reasoning: The PR code still has the bug: there is no zero-length check before DataPtr() is passed to ArrayBufferFromHex. No scanner finding names the zero-length trigger, the null DataPtr, or the missing array_length==0 guard. Findings 1-2 describe a different root cause: the scalar loop is bounded by input_length, causing an overflow on non-SIMD builds. Finding 5 is the SharedArrayBuffer UNIMPLEMENTED() abort, a different trigger and sink. These are near matches only.

criteria: Constant-folding a string element or charAt access in Maglev reaches GetConstantSingleCharacterStringFromCode via TryReduceConstantStringAt
The trigger is a character code above kMaxOneByteCharCode (the two-byte path)
The two-byte path wraps a freshly allocated local-isolate string with MakeRef(broker(), ...)
The fresh string is not a canonical or persistent handle known to the broker, so the MakeRef/HeapObjectRef invariant fails
The result is a CHECK failure ('Ref construction failed') that crashes the engine
judge.findings_summary: One finding: two-byte single-char constant folding allocates and internalizes a string on the background compile thread. The scanner deems this probably safe, with no race found, and suggests matching TurboFan's one-byte-only folding.
judge.ground_truth_summary: GetConstantSingleCharacterStringFromCode calls MakeRef on a freshly allocated two-byte single-char string from the local isolate factory. The string is not broker-canonical, so Ref construction hits a CHECK failure and crashes V8.
judge.reasoning: The scanner points at the correct line and the two-byte trigger, which are present in the PR code. However, it frames the issue as a background-thread allocation and string-table concurrency concern, not a broken MakeRef/broker invariant causing a CHECK failure. It also concludes the code is 'probably safe', finds no concrete race, and calls it a design-consistency concern rather than a vulnerability. That contradicts the GT crash.

criteria: CheckedSafeIntAsWord64 in use-info.h still uses Truncation::Any() with check_safe_integer=false
CheckedSafeIntTruncatingWord32 was changed to Word32WithSafeIntCheck (check_safe_integer=true)
IsLessGeneralThan now requires check_safe_integer to be monotonic (true <= false fails)
A node visited first with a true flag and later with a false flag fires the DCHECK in SetAndCheckInput (IsUseLessGeneral) in simplified-lowering.cc
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings about check_safe_integer being ignored in Phi/Select/TypeGuard, Int32Div/Mod, the word32 passthrough at representation-change.cc:1104, and chained adds causing wrong-value miscompiles. None concern CheckedSafeIntAsWord64 or the monotonicity DCHECK.
judge.ground_truth_summary: CheckedSafeIntAsWord64 was not updated to carry check_safe_integer=true. Mixed use infos break the new IsLessGeneralThan monotonicity, firing the DCHECK in SetAndCheckInput in simplified-lowering.
judge.reasoning: The GT bug is still present in the PR diff: CheckedSafeIntAsWord64 keeps Truncation::Any(), so the new monotonicity check can fail. No scanner finding mentions CheckedSafeIntAsWord64, the IsLessGeneralThan monotonicity requirement, or the SetAndCheckInput DCHECK. The findings instead cover an adjacent class: Phi/Div/Word64 paths that ignore check_safe_integer and cause wrong-value miscompiles. Same feature area, but a different root cause and sink.

criteria: Sink: the scalar/slow-path fallback loop in ArrayBufferFromHex, which writes buffer[index++]
Incorrect bound: the loop limit is still input_length rather than output_length (output_length*2)
The guard was relaxed from DCHECK_EQ to DCHECK_LE, which allows output_length < input_length/2
Trigger: setFromHex clamps output_length to the target array length and passes a raw DataPtr, so a hex string longer than the target overflows
SIMD paths are correctly bounded; only the scalar path is vulnerable
judge.findings_summary: Six findings. The top two exactly describe the scalar-fallback heap overflow in ArrayBufferFromHex reachable via setFromHex. The others cover hardening gaps, a SAB UNIMPLEMENTED abort, and a toHex offset bug.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The DCHECK was relaxed to DCHECK_LE for setFromHex, but the ArrayBufferFromHex slow-path loop is still bounded by input_length, so writes run past an output_length-sized buffer.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 (and its caller-side duplicate, Finding 2) identify the same chain. The scalar fallback in ArrayBufferFromHex loops to input_length while setFromHex passes a clamped output_length and a raw DataPtr. The guard relaxation to DCHECK_LE is noted, and the SIMD paths are correctly described as bounded. The PR diff confirms the loop bound was left unchanged and adds no mitigation.

criteria: The force or intersect pack validation (SLPTree::HasInputDependencies, called from NewForcePackNode and NewIntersectPackNode) is incomplete.
The missing guard is either an IsSideEffectFree check over the intermediate BFS or hoisted nodes, or tracking of reorder inputs across SLP trees.
Invalid pairings reach ReduceForceOrIntersectPackNode, which uses ReduceInputsOfOp to emit the partner's input tree out of order.
The result is incorrect code generation or a crash, reachable through the new intersecting ForcePackNode or ReplaceLane force-pack paths.
judge.findings_summary: 13 findings. F1 and F7 report that ReduceInputsOfOp hoists input trees with no effect check, because the dependency checks are pairwise only. The others cover overlap asymmetry, merge conflicts, Phi mapping, and type-cast hardening.
judge.ground_truth_summary: HasInputDependencies omits reorder-input tracking across SLP trees and an IsSideEffectFree check on intermediate BFS nodes. Force and intersect packs can therefore form invalid pairings, which ReduceInputsOfOp emits out of order, causing a crash.
judge.reasoning: Findings 1 and 7 match the GT's second gap and cover its roles. They say validation is limited to HasInputDependencies' data-path BFS plus pairwise IsSideEffectFree. So ReduceInputsOfOp hoists the partner's transitive inputs past effectful ops, and the fix is an effect check over the hoisted tree. The PR diff adds this unguarded path. The cross-tree reorder-input gap is not covered, and the scanner understates the impact, so confidence is medium.

criteria: Located in the kUnknown branch of ParseJsonObjectProperties in json-parser.cc
Trigger: the last key mismatches feedback or is slow (is_slow || !key_match) and no comma follows
Missing return true lets control fall through to ++idx
idx reaches descriptors_end, so set_fast_iterable_if marks the descriptors kJsonFast
Wrong kJsonFast state violates the stringifier's fast-key invariant (IsFastKey DCHECK)
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1 and 2 report the missing return on a last-key mismatch, which falls through to ++idx and wrongly marks the descriptors kJsonFast, leading to unescaped stringify. The other findings cover stale counts, GC trimming and hardening.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The kUnknown branch omits 'return true' after a mismatch or slow key with no comma. ++idx then makes idx == descriptors_end, the descriptors are marked kJsonFast, and the stringifier's IsFastKey DCHECK fails.
judge.reasoning: Findings 1 and 2 state that the kUnknown branch has no 'return true' on a mismatch with no following comma, so control reaches ++idx and the kJsonFast mark at 1646-1650. That is the GT chain. The PR diff confirms the missing return and adds no fix. Both findings cite the stringifier's DCHECK-only fast-key handling as the consequence.

criteria: Trigger: call feedback whose target is a FeedbackCell (not a JSFunction) with a present SharedFunctionInfo
Location: new FeedbackCell branch in MaglevGraphBuilder::BuildCallWithFeedback
Missing guard: no IsClassConstructor(shared->kind()) check before reduction
Sink: direct TryBuildCallKnownJSFunction inline/known call instead of throwing ConstructorNonCallable TypeError
Consequence: class constructor executes without `new` / without the spec-required TypeError
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1 and 2 report the missing IsClassConstructor check in the FeedbackCell call path, letting class constructors run without `new`. Finding 3 is an adjacent HasBreakInfo issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Maglev's FeedbackCell call reduction inlines or calls via TryBuildCallKnownJSFunction without an IsClassConstructor guard, so calling a class constructor without `new` skips the TypeError.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows the FeedbackCell branch checking only shared.has_value() and then calling TryBuildCallKnownJSFunction with no IsClassConstructor guard. Findings 1 and 2 name this exact trigger, sink and missing guard. They also contrast it with the existing kThrowConstructorNonCallableError handling and propose that fix. The extra exploit speculation does not weaken the match, and no mitigation appears in the PR.

criteria: Newly added AddRhsIsStringConstantInternalize{WithVector,Trampoline} builtins in builtins-number-gen.cc are the vulnerable site
In both builtins, `left` is declared Parameter<String> and `right` Parameter<Object>, swapped relative to the Rhs variant's semantics
Root cause is copy-paste from the Lhs variant without inverting the parameter types
Trigger: an arbitrary non-string left operand (e.g., GSAB or other object) reaches the String-typed parameter through Maglev/TurboFan/baseline calls of the Rhs builtin
Effect: type confusion on the String-typed cast, leading to a debug-check failure on non-string objects
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1 and 2 report swapped parameter types in both Rhs builtins, copied from the Lhs variant, causing type confusion and debug assertion failures. The other two findings are unrelated hardening notes.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A copy-paste error leaves `left` typed Parameter<String> and `right` typed Parameter<Object> in the new AddRhsIsStringConstant builtins. Non-string left operands such as a GSAB are then treated as String, triggering a JSArrayBuffer::byte_length DCHECK.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the exact builtins, lines and swapped Parameter<String>/Parameter<Object> declarations. It identifies the copy-paste origin and the trigger: a non-string lhs reaching the builtin via Maglev/TurboFan. It says this causes a debug-build assertion abort, which matches the GT's DCHECK-level impact. The PR diff confirms the code. The scanner downplays release-mode impact, but it does not call the bug fixed or hypothetical.

criteria: Location is BuildCallWithFeedback, in the FeedbackCell call path of maglev-graph-builder.cc
The IsClassConstructor early return calls Runtime::kThrowConstructorNonCallableError with target_node
The early return comes before BuildCheckJSFunction(target_node) and BuildCheckValueByReference on the feedback cell
As a result, an unvalidated runtime target that does not match the feedback can reach the runtime throw instead of deoptimizing
The flawed ordering is present in the evaluated PR code and is not fixed by it
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the class-constructor early throw in BuildCallWithFeedback happens before BuildCheckJSFunction and the feedback-cell CheckValue. A mismatched target throws wrongly instead of deoptimizing. The scanner calls this a correctness bug.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The class-constructor early return was placed before the BuildCheckJSFunction and feedback-cell guards. An arbitrary value can reach ThrowConstructorNonCallableError, which casts it to JSFunction and hits a DCHECK failure.
judge.reasoning: The scanner names the same site, sink, and bypassed guards, and proposes the correct reordering fix. It confirms the bug is present in the patched code. It underrates the impact: it misses that the runtime casts the argument to JSFunction, and its trigger is an ordinary callable rather than a non-JSFunction. The root cause still matches, and the GT is itself a LogicError.

criteria: Uint8ArrayFromBase64 holds a DisallowGarbageCollection scope with a live String::FlatContent of the input string
ArrayBufferFromBase64 is called while that FlatContent is live
The callee opens a nested AllowGarbageCollection scope and allocates (NewJSArrayBufferAndBackingStore), which can trigger GC
GC can move the input string, so the FlatContent lifetime invariant is broken and the ~FlatContent checksum CHECK fails
judge.findings_summary: Six findings. Finding 2 identifies the nested AllowGarbageCollection inside DisallowGarbageCollection with a live FlatContent, GC moving the string, and the ~FlatContent checksum failure. The others are unrelated simdutf, memcpy and bootstrapper concerns.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ArrayBufferFromBase64 nests AllowGarbageCollection inside the caller's DisallowGarbageCollection while the input string's FlatContent is live. The allocation can trigger GC that moves the string, failing the FlatContent checksum CHECK.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT chain exactly. It names the no_gc scope and FlatContent in the builtin, the nested AllowGarbageCollection at line 399, the GC-triggering JSArrayBuffer allocation, and the string moving so that ~FlatContent's slow-DCHECK checksum fails. The PR diff shows this code unfixed. The finding rates it as not exploitable in release builds, but the GT is this same debug invariant and CHECK failure, so the downgrade does not contradict it.

criteria: Location is JSTypedArray::GetVariableByteLengthOrOutOfBounds in the length-tracking (RAB/GSAB) branches
Returned byte length is the raw buffer_byte_length - byte_offset
The guard that is missing is a RoundDown to a multiple of element_size
Consequence: the byte length is not a multiple of element size, so length*element_size != byte_length (DCHECK failure or logic error)
Trigger: a buffer length not evenly divisible by element size, e.g. a 129-byte GSAB backing a Float64Array
judge.findings_summary: Four sandbox-hardening findings: UAF via orphaned extension in GetBuffer, UAF via Detach of a wasm buffer, trusting in-sandbox RAB byte_length, and a GSAB null deref. None addresses alignment.
judge.ground_truth_summary: GetVariableByteLengthOrOutOfBounds returns an unaligned byte length for length-tracking TypedArrays because RoundDown to element size is missing. This causes length*element_size != byte_length mismatches.
judge.reasoning: The PR code does lack element-size rounding, so the GT bug is present. No finding mentions alignment or RoundDown, or a byte length that is not a multiple of element size. Findings 3 and 4 cite the same function but describe other issues: trusting the in-sandbox byte_length, and a null backing-store dereference. Finding 3 even calls the function safe on its own terms.

criteria: FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad zero-initializes last_continuation/after_continuation as a 'not found' sentinel
A CallProperty* bytecode whose operand 0 does not match the Star register skips the assignment and only breaks; default:return {} does not cover this case
The function falls through to return ContinuationOffsets{0,0} (a non-empty optional) instead of nullopt
TryBuildPolymorphicPropertyAccess treats {0,0} as a valid continuation, and the DCHECK iterator_.current_offset()==last_continuation fails
judge.findings_summary: Nine findings on the maglev poly-call continuation logic. Finding 7 identifies {0,0} being returned instead of nullopt on a CallProperty register mismatch, and the resulting DCHECK failure in the caller.
judge.ground_truth_summary: On a CallProperty register mismatch, FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad returns ContinuationOffsets{0,0} instead of nullopt. The caller treats it as a found continuation, causing a failed DCHECK on the iterator offset.
judge.reasoning: Finding 7 matches the GT causal chain exactly. In the CALL_PROPERTY_BYTECODES switch, a register mismatch falls through to return {0,0}, and the caller treats it as a real continuation, so the DCHECK at 7697 fails. The PR diff shows the code unchanged, with no guard added. The finding's impact assessment (a debug DCHECK failure) matches the GT consequence. It does not deny that the bug is active.

criteria: Root cause sits in FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad's pattern matching across iterator_.Advance() calls
After each Advance, no IsOffsetAMergePoint or loop-header check is made on the Star or CallProperty offsets inside the continuation
Trigger: the GetNamedProperty->Star->CallProperty pattern straddles a merge point or loop back-edge, so a mid-continuation offset is a merge target
Sink: the continuation is built through a merge or loop block mid-stream, bypassing proper predecessor entry and leaving the block state invalid (the kBlockPointer DCHECK)
Fix: reject the continuation when any scanned offset is a merge point
judge.findings_summary: Nine findings: dead-arm predecessor and merge-state miscount at after_continuation (OOB Phi write, null loop merge state), iterator mishandling on abort and generic paths, unmerged registers across arms, and a {0,0} continuation on register mismatch.
judge.ground_truth_summary: FindContinuationForPolymorphicPropertyLoad advances into Star or CallProperty offsets without checking for merge points or loop headers. Continuations that straddle a merge are built mid-block, corrupting Maglev block state.
judge.reasoning: The PR code does lack the merge-point check, so the GT bug is present. No finding names a missing merge-point guard on the Star or CallProperty offsets inside the continuation. F1 and F5 cover a different trigger: dead continuation arms calling MergeDead on a merge or loop state at after_continuation, followed by a predecessor-count mismatch. Their suggested loop-header guard targets after_continuation, not the straddled offsets. This is an adjacent bug in the same area, so not detected.

criteria: FeedbackNexus::IsOneMapManyNames classifies feedback by shape only (weak map plus a Smi handler equal to LoadGeneric/StoreGeneric) and never checks FeedbackSlotKind.
KeyedHasIC feedback on a Wasm object map can therefore be misclassified as '1 map, many names'.
The PR changes ReadFeedbackForPropertyAccess so this misclassification is routed to ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess.
ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess runs DCHECK(keyed_mode.string_keys()), but FromNexus hard-codes string_keys=false for KeyedHas, so the assertion fails.
judge.findings_summary: 16 findings. Most cover Proxy-trap holder and field-index misuse, dependencies, UNREACHABLE, and i32 key handling. Finding 12 matches the GT: IsOneMapManyNames lacks a slot-kind guard, causing a DCHECK failure for KeyedHas.
judge.ground_truth_summary: IsOneMapManyNames lacks an IC-kind guard, so KeyedHasIC feedback is misclassified. The PR's new ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess call then hits DCHECK(string_keys), which crashes debug builds.
judge.reasoning: Finding 12 identifies IsOneMapManyNames comparing handlers without a slot-kind check. It traces KeyedHas feedback on a Wasm map being classified true, then routed by the PR to ProcessFeedbackMapsForKeyedPropertyAccess, where DCHECK(string_keys) fails. It notes LoadSlow and StoreGeneric share Smi(11) and recommends restricting the check by IC kind, which is the same root cause and fix. The diff supports the chain. The finding's 'debug-only' framing matches the GT's DCHECK crash.

criteria: Vulnerable code is InsertUnreachableIfNecessary<LOWER> in simplified-lowering.cc
The ternary selects GetControlInput(node,0) whenever ControlOutputCount()==0
Missing guard for nodes with zero control inputs, e.g. pure nodes like SameValue
Trigger is a node typed None reaching the unreachable-insertion path
Sink is the CHECK failure (crash) in NodeProperties::GetControlInput
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: CheckBounds lowered to abort mode on feedback types, and Fast API float32/uint64 use-info mismatch. Both are self-described as unchanged upstream code or speculative.
judge.ground_truth_summary: InsertUnreachableIfNecessary<LOWER> calls GetControlInput(node,0) for any node without control outputs. A pure node typed None has no control input, so this hits a CHECK failure and crashes.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports CheckBounds weakening based on feedback types and a Fast API argument representation mismatch. Neither finding touches InsertUnreachableIfNecessary, the control-input ternary, or pure nodes that have no control inputs. Both findings are in the same file but cover unrelated sinks and triggers, so the GT causal chain is not identified.

criteria: Effectful node in the LOWER phase with a None-typed value input takes the new is_dead path in RepresentationSelector::VisitNode
The node gets feedback_type None and the function returns early, without lowering the node or converting it to DeadValue
InsertUnreachableIfNecessary only patches the effect chain and does not replace the node itself
The node stays in the lowered graph with its original opcode and a None/invalid type, breaking the typed-node invariant (IsTyped/GetType DCHECK) and risking miscompilation
The scanner presents this as an active defect of the PR on ordinary dead-value inputs, not as speculative hardening
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: two Turboshaft graph-builder frame-state and phi issues, pure-node feedback typing, dead effectful nodes left un-lowered (called speculative), a FinishRegion CHECK crash, and DCHECK-only Map invalid indices.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new is_dead path marks effectful nodes with None-typed inputs as None and returns early after InsertUnreachableIfNecessary. Nodes are left with their original opcode and a None type rather than becoming DeadValue, breaking the typed-node invariant.
judge.reasoning: Finding 4 identifies the right construct: dead-marked effectful nodes keep their original op, skip lowering, and are not converted to DeadValue. However, it says the code is safe whenever a preceding Unreachable exists. It treats the issue as needing a separate typer bug and calls it speculative hardening matching upstream. It never ties the flaw to the None-type invariant or verifier failure. Finding 5 is an adjacent CHECK crash; the other findings concern graph-builder or pure-node paths.

criteria: Bug is in BytecodeGenerator::BuildOptionalChain where a HoleCheckElisionScope is placed around expression_func()
Hole check elision scope wrongly covers the optional chain's base object load, which no prior check dominates
Missing ThrowReferenceErrorIfHole for a TDZ variable used as the chain base (e.g. delete tdz_var?.prop)
TheHole passes the JumpIfUndefinedOrNull check and leaks into JS
Fix scopes the elision to OptionalChainNullLabelScope (consecutive links only)
judge.findings_summary: 18 findings on TDZ elision flaws in try/catch, finally, break/continue, switch, do-while, for-in/of, plus an uninitialized copy-constructor field. None covers optional chains.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The HoleCheckElisionScope at the start of BuildOptionalChain elides the TDZ check on the chain's base variable, so TheHole slips past the null/undefined check and leaks into JS (e.g. delete tdz?.prop).
judge.reasoning: Every scanner finding is about the same hole-check elision feature but hits a different construct: try/catch/finally, labeled blocks, switch, do-while, for loops, for-in/of targets, or the Variable copy constructor. None mentions BuildOptionalChain, optional chains, or elision of the chain base's hole check. These are adjacent bugs in the same file and feature with different triggers, so they do not count as detection.

criteria: Location is the scalar tail loop in RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern (runtime-regexp.cc ~2241)
The for-loop initializer `c = *block` dereferences before the `block < end` check
Trigger: the SIMD loops leave block == end, so no remaining characters are scanned
Sink: a one-element read at subject.data()+length, past the end of the subject buffer
Missing guard: the bounds check must precede every dereference
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the tail loop reads one SChar past the subject end via the initializer and the increment, with a reliable ASan OOB read. Finding 2: an unrelated cache-count overwrite logic bug.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The scalar tail loop's for-initializer dereferences *block before checking block<end. When SIMD consumes everything, this reads one char past the subject buffer end.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the exact line and loop. It shows that the initializer reads *block when block==end, before the check, causing a one-past-end read. It also notes the increment-path read, which is consistent with the GT. The PR diff contains the vulnerable loop with no guard. The scanner calls the issue real but low-impact; that is a severity judgment and does not contradict the GT.

criteria: Location is SourceTextModule::GatherAvailableAncestors, the async parent loop
GetCycleRoot(isolate) now runs unconditionally for every async parent because the && operands were reordered
An async parent that fails synchronously while depending on an async child leaves cycle_root as the_hole
The_hole is cast to SourceTextModule and status() is read from it, causing type confusion
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings: d8 resolver type confusion, an errored-root CHECK crash in Module::Evaluate, d8 crashes from aborting Maybe calls and realm disposal, and missing stack checks in module recursion. None covers a hole cycle_root.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Reordering the && in GatherAvailableAncestors makes GetCycleRoot run unconditionally. For an async parent that failed synchronously, cycle_root is still the_hole, so the hole is treated as a SourceTextModule (type confusion).
judge.reasoning: No finding says GetCycleRoot can be called on an uninitialized (hole) cycle_root in GatherAvailableAncestors. Finding 6 describes the reordered check as 'the fix' that is already applied, which contradicts the GT. Finding 2 covers an errored cycle root that trips a CHECK in Module::Evaluate, an adjacent bug with a different trigger and sink. The other findings concern d8 or recursion depth.

criteria: Reader: WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize/EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption calls signature_storage.TotalReservedSize(), which iterates storage_
Reader path: NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption calls module_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() before acquiring allocation_mutex_
Writer: concurrent instantiation (fast API signatures) mutates the mutable signature_storage on a const WasmModule
Missing synchronization causes a data race on the std::vector storage_ bookkeeping
Introduced by the replacement of signature_zone with WasmModuleSignatureStorage in this PR
judge.findings_summary: Multiple findings report the data race between unlocked TotalReservedSize() in EstimateStoredSize and fast-API instantiation push_back under allocation_mutex_. Other findings cover unrelated decoder issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Data race: EstimateStoredSize reads signature_storage.TotalReservedSize() without a lock, called before allocation_mutex_ in NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption, while instantiation concurrently mutates signature_storage.
judge.reasoning: Findings 2, 4, 7 and 8 each identify the unsynchronized TotalReservedSize() read at wasm-module.cc:733, reached from NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption before allocation_mutex_ is taken. They also name the concurrent fast-API instantiation writer that push_backs into storage_. The PR diff shows the new non-atomic iteration with no locking added, so the GT causal chain is present and active.

criteria: Location is Shell::ResetOnProfileEndListener in src/d8/d8.cc
Early return gated on options.enable_inspector is placed before profiler_end_callback_.erase(isolate)
The erase must always run, independent of console type; only the D8Console-specific teardown should be gated
Stale isolate-keyed map entry (Global<Function>/Global<Context>) outlives Isolate::Dispose at teardown call sites
Later access to the stale entry (lookup/trigger on address reuse, or Global destruction) is a use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: Four findings. #3 is the exact match: the early return skips the map erase, leaving dangling Global handles (UAF). The others cover a leaked CpuProfiler, a map race, and a type-confused cast in ProfilerTriggerSample.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ResetOnProfileEndListener returns early when the inspector is enabled, before erasing the isolate's profiler_end_callback_ entry. This leaves dangling Isolate-keyed Global handles after isolate disposal, causing a use-after-free.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 matches the GT exactly. An early return on enable_inspector skips profiler_end_callback_.erase, so stale Global handles survive isolate disposal. These are later used via Has/TriggerOnProfileEndListener on address reuse or freed by static destructors. The PR diff confirms the guard sits before the erase, and nothing in the PR mitigates it. The 'pre-existing'/'not a security boundary' caveat concerns severity and does not deny the bug.

criteria: Locates the new constant-elision early return in MaglevGraphBuilder::BuildCheckSmi (TryGetInt32Constant + Smi::IsValid)
Identifies that for kTagged inputs the skipped check is CheckSmi, a tag-bit check that numeric equivalence does not imply
Identifies TryGetInt32Constant resolving through the checked_value alternative to a HeapNumber constant
Identifies the source of that alternative: BuildCheckNumericalValue's HeapNumber branch, guarded only by CheckFloat64SameValue, which Smi and HeapNumber both pass
Consequence: a HeapNumber flows into Smi-assuming sinks (type confusion, missing write barrier)
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: BuildCheckSmi constant shortcut skips CheckSmi for tagged nodes with a HeapNumber checked_value alternative, so a HeapNumber reaches Smi sinks. Finding 2: Array ctor concern with no independent issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: BuildCheckSmi elides the check when TryGetInt32Constant is Smi-valid. That is unsound for tagged inputs, whose checked_value may be a HeapNumber constant validated only by a same-value float check, so a HeapNumber bypasses CheckSmi.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain exactly. It names the early return at lines 4137-4139, the tagged/CheckSmi distinction, and the TryGetConstantAlternative fallback to a HeapNumber checked_value set by BuildCheckNumericalValue after CheckFloat64SameValue. It also names the Smi-only sinks, including the missing write barrier. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code and adds no mitigation. The finding's caveat questions exploitability but still affirms a real bug.

criteria: Source: declared (import-excluded) function index decoded from the Smi in the Liftoff frame's feedback slot in Runtime_WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish
Trigger: trace_deopt_verbose path taken when the feedback vector is missing (Smi::zero)
Sink: NativeModule::GetCode(declared_func_index), which expects a module-scoped index that includes imports
Incorrect guard/conversion: num_imported_functions is subtracted a second time, and bounds are checked only by DCHECK
Impact: wrong or negative code_table_ index, giving an out-of-bounds read in release builds
judge.findings_summary: Nine findings. Finding 3 identifies the declared index passed to GetCode in the WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish trace path, causing a double import subtraction and a code_table_ underflow. The others are unrelated sandbox or deoptimizer hardening issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Runtime_WasmLiftoffDeoptFinish passes a declared function index to NativeModule::GetCode, which expects a module index. The imports are subtracted twice, causing an OOB read of code_table_ under trace_deopt_verbose.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 matches the GT chain. It covers the declared index from the feedback slot, the trace_deopt_verbose path when the vector is missing, and GetCode re-applying declared_function_index (a double subtraction checked only by DCHECK). The result is a code_table_ OOB read. The PR diff shows the vulnerable call is present. The finding's caveat about the debug-only flag matches the GT's precondition and does not deny the bug.

criteria: TryInferApiHolderValue calls MapInference::InsertMapChecks, which can abort graph building (unconditional deopt terminates current block)
Abort result is collapsed into the same not_found sentinel used for ordinary holder-not-found
Caller (TryBuildCallKnownApiFunction) cannot distinguish abort and continues emitting nodes (CallBuiltin)
Downstream code (AttachExceptionHandlerInfo/AddNewNode) dereferences null/terminated current_block_
Code is present in evaluated PR snapshot without propagation fix
judge.findings_summary: Finding 2 identifies the swallowed DoneWithAbort in TryInferApiHolderValue leading to node emission into a terminated block. The other findings concern stale maps, catch-block KNA, DCHECKs and hardening.
judge.ground_truth_summary: TryInferApiHolderValue returns not_found when InsertMapChecks aborts. The caller then keeps emitting nodes into an aborted block, so AttachExceptionHandlerInfo dereferences a null current_block_.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT exactly. It cites line 12057 in TryInferApiHolderValue, where the abort from InsertMapChecks is mapped to not_found. It traces the caller continuing with GetConvertReceiver and CallBuiltin after EmitUnconditionalDeopt has terminated the block, and notes there is no null-block guard. The PR diff shows this code was newly added. The scanner downgrades severity to crash/DoS but still calls the issue real, which is consistent with a NullPointerDereference GT.

criteria: The direct-recursion check in the refactored MaglevReducer::CanInlineCall reads current_provenance().unit->shared_function_info().
Provenance/unit comes from optional labeller/debug state, not from the always-valid compilation unit.
When no graph labeller or tracing is active, unit can be nullptr.
Reaching CanInlineCall in that configuration causes a null pointer dereference.
judge.findings_summary: 12 findings. Most cover context misuse, catch depth, missing feedback-vector checks, and handler ordering. Finding 10 identifies the null current_provenance().unit dereference in CanInlineCall when no graph labeller is present.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactored CanInlineCall direct-recursion check uses labeller-derived current_provenance().unit instead of the compilation unit. That pointer is only populated under gdbjit/tracing, so release builds hit a null dereference.
judge.reasoning: Finding 10 matches the GT. It cites reducer-inl.h:1291, where CanInlineCall dereferences current_provenance().unit. It explains that provenance is only populated when a graph labeller exists, so unit is nullptr otherwise, and traces the path from VisitCall to CanInlineCall. The diff confirms this code. The scanner calls the trigger flag-gated, but it treats the bug as real, and that does not change the root cause.

criteria: Descriptors::remove unconditionally pushes the removed fd onto the free list
fd_renumber calls remove(from) then inserts `to` into used without removing `to` from free and without handling from == to
This leaves an fd both in used and on free (identity case or renumber onto a previously closed fd)
A later push pops the poisoned fd and the assert!(insert(...).is_none()) panics the host (guest-triggerable DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1 and 2 report that fd_renumber corrupts the free list (identity case and renumber onto a closed fd), causing the push assert! panic. The other findings cover unrelated perms, readlink, leak, random_get, todo! and table issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: fd_renumber with remove() pushing onto free leaves an fd both in used and on free (from==to or `to` previously closed). A later push asserts exclusive insert and panics the host.
judge.reasoning: Findings 1 and 2 match the GT. They name the same chain: remove() pushes onto free, fd_renumber inserts `to` without clearing it from free, both the from==to case and the close-then-renumber case, and the push assert panic. The PR diff shows remove() and push() with the assert and no guard. Neither finding describes the bug as fixed.

criteria: Memory::new/_new accepts a MemoryType with shared=true and performs no is_shared() rejection
The shared type flows to a runtime SharedMemory backing an ordinary wasmtime::Memory handle
Safe Memory APIs (data/data_mut) hand out &[u8]/&mut [u8] slices, guarded only by debug_assert, over memory other threads can write
Result is a data race / unsoundness reachable from safe Rust; the fix is rejecting shared types in Memory::_new
judge.findings_summary: Several findings (7, 10, 14, 16, 17, 18, 22) report that Memory::new accepts a shared MemoryType, leading to racy safe slices and a grow panic. Most other findings cover unrelated DoS, panic and limiter issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Memory::_new does not reject shared MemoryType, so the safe wasmtime::Memory API (data slices) can wrap shared linear memory and permit data races in safe Rust; the coredump path also exposes shared memories.
judge.reasoning: Findings 10, 16, 17 and 7 match the GT root cause. Memory::_new never checks is_shared. new_dynamic wraps the allocation in a SharedMemory and returns it as a plain Memory. data/data_mut have only a debug_assert, so release builds allow a safe-Rust data race. The suggested fix, rejecting shared types in Memory::new, is the GT fix. The PR adds no guard. The coredump path is not covered, but the primary chain is matched.

criteria: The x64 ISLE fcopysign rules (F32 and F64) pass the scalar operands a/b as XmmMem rather than forcing them into registers.
Load sinking (put_in_reg_mem / is_mergeable_load) can fold a scalar f32/f64 load into the memory operand of ANDPS/ANDNPS/ANDPD/ANDNPD.
These packed SSE instructions read 128 bits, while the intended scalar load is 32 or 64 bits.
The widened read extends past the bounds-checked region, into guard pages (crash) or out-of-sandbox memory.
judge.findings_summary: Five findings. Findings 1-2 cover constant-pool sinking into packed SSE ops. Findings 3-4 cover scalar heap-load sinking into 128-bit ANDPS/ANDPD (over-read plus alignment faults). Finding 5 is an unrelated roundss upper-lane issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The x64 fcopysign ISLE rules do not force operands into registers. Load sinking then folds scalar loads into 128-bit ANDPS/ANDPD memory operands, causing an 8-byte out-of-bounds read past the checked boundary (crash or sandbox escape read).
judge.reasoning: Findings 3 and 4 match the GT chain: the new fcopysign rules use XmmMem operands, load sinking merges a scalar f32/f64 load into a 128-bit andps/andpd memory operand, and the read goes beyond the 4/8 bytes that were bounds-checked. The PR diff confirms the operands are not materialized into registers. The scanner understates the impact and adds an alignment angle, but it still states the over-read is real and reachable.

criteria: The trigger is f64x2.splat of a single-use f64 load on x86-64 when the movddup sinkable-load rule (gated on use_ssse3) does not apply.
The sink is the F64X2 splat rule 0 at lower.isle:4326, which passes src as XmmMem directly to x64_pshufd.
The missing guard: src is not forced into a register (no put_in_xmm), so load sinking folds the 8-byte load into the pshufd memory operand.
The impact is that pshufd (or movdqu widening, or vpshufd m128) reads 16 bytes, 8 bytes past the intended f64 load.
The causal chain is introduced by the PR diff (rule 0 change plus the new use_ssse3 gate on rule 5) and is not mitigated.
judge.findings_summary: Twelve findings. Findings 7 and 10 pinpoint the post-#6496 f64x2.splat pshufd fallback sinking an 8-byte load into a 16-byte read. Other findings cover adjacent over-reads (fcopysign, movlhps, roundss) and gating issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new F64X2 splat fallback rule passes src directly to pshufd. Load sinking folds an f64.load into the 128-bit operand, causing a 16-byte read instead of 8. Consequences: an out-of-sandbox read, a trap, or a host crash.
judge.reasoning: Findings 7 and 10 identify the exact chain: F64X2 splat rule 0 passes src to x64_pshufd, put_in_xmm_mem sinks the 8-byte f64 load, and the 16-byte read over-reads by 8 bytes once the use_ssse3-gated movddup rule is bypassed. Both recommend put_in_xmm. They label it 'Other' and argue Wasm reachability is limited, but they confirm the code behavior and do not call it fixed. Confidence is medium for that reason.

criteria: The libcalls table_fill_func_ref and table_fill_gc_ref now interpret their table_index argument as a DefinedTableIndex, resolved via get_defined_table.
Winch visit_table_fill still pushes the raw module-level TableIndex immediate onto the argument stack.
Winch does not use prepare_builtin_defined_table_arg (which visit_table_grow uses), so there is no conversion to the defined index or owning vmctx.
When a module imports tables, the index spaces differ, leading to an out-of-bounds defined-table lookup (host panic) or a write to the wrong table.
judge.findings_summary: One finding: Winch visit_table_fill passes a module-level TableIndex with the caller's vmctx to the table_fill libcalls, which now expect a DefinedTableIndex. This causes a host panic or wrong-table fill when tables are imported.
judge.ground_truth_summary: PR #11254 changed the table_fill libcalls to take DefinedTableIndex, but Winch visit_table_fill was not updated to use prepare_builtin_defined_table_arg. Imported tables then cause an out-of-bounds lookup panic or a wrong-table fill.
judge.reasoning: The scanner identifies the exact causal chain. Winch visit_table_fill pushes the raw module index while the libcalls now use DefinedTableIndex via get_defined_table. It contrasts this with visit_table_grow's use of prepare_builtin_defined_table_arg. It describes the host panic and wrong-table impacts, with a PoC using an imported table. The PR diff confirms the libcall change and no Winch update. Listing libcalls.rs as the file is acceptable because it is a must-cover role.

criteria: Location: amode_no_more_iconst rules 6/7 in aarch64 inst.isle
Incorrect guard: shift_masked_imm is called with the memory-access type ty instead of the ishl value's type (i64)
Trigger: narrow access type with a large shift amount (e.g. i32 with n=34) masks to the natural scale and falsely matches
Sink: a RegScaled amode is emitted whose address diverges from the CLIF shift, so the bounds-checked address differs from the accessed address
Vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR diff
judge.findings_summary: F1: rules 6/7 mask the shift by the access type, not the 64-bit ishl type, causing RegScaled miscompiles and a Wasmtime memory64 sandbox escape. F2: an adjacent F128 overflowing-shift panic.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The AArch64 amode rules 6/7 call shift_masked_imm with the load/store type instead of the ishl type. Narrow types then falsely match large shifts, emitting RegScaled addressing that diverges from CLIF semantics and escapes the sandbox.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the same lines, the same wrong-type mask (access ty instead of the 64-bit ishl type), and the same example (i32 load with n=34 giving x+4*y). It traces the same RegScaled miscompile and the bounds-check bypass under memory64. It notes the PR introduced the regression, and the diff confirms the vulnerable code is present.

criteria: StringPool map keys are &'static str obtained by transmuting borrows into the pool's own strings storage (insert)
StringPool::try_clone clones map and strings independently, field-wise
Map key clone copies the pointer shallowly, while the strings clone deep-copies into new allocations
Cloned map keys therefore point into the original pool's storage and dangle once the original is dropped
Lookups or rehashes on the clone read freed memory (use-after-free)
judge.findings_summary: Five findings. #1 is an exact StringPool::try_clone UAF from shallow-copied &'static str keys. #3 covers the enabling TryClone impl for &T. Others are an unrelated ZST double-drop and Stacked Borrows provenance issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: StringPool::try_clone copies HashMap keys that are transmuted &'static str borrows into the original pool's strings. The clone's keys dangle after the original drops, causing use-after-free on lookup. The fix re-interns strings into the clone.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 traces the exact GT chain in the PR's StringPool: the transmuted &'static keys from insert, field-wise try_clone, the shallow &T TryClone against deep-copied Box<str>, dangling keys after the original is dropped, and UAF in get_atom/insert/reserve. The PR snapshot contains this code unfixed. The finding calls the bug latent because there are no callers yet. It still asserts a present soundness UAF reachable through a safe API, so it is not a hypothetical future risk.

criteria: Location is MemoryImageSlot reset/instantiate logic in cow.rs, where protections are re-applied on slot reuse
Predicate is wrong: can_elide_bounds_check is used where can_use_virtual_memory (old Static semantics) is needed
Trigger condition: memory_guard_size == 0 with reservation < 4GiB (or other non-elidable but virtual-memory-reliant cases)
Consequence: set_protection is skipped, so stale previously-accessible pages stay RW for the next pooled instance
Impact: out-of-bounds accesses do not trap, breaking sandbox and memory semantics
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1-2 identify the wrong cow.rs reset predicate that leaves stale pooled pages RW when guard=0. Findings 3-6 are unrelated issues: MemoryCreator contract, panic, and shared-memory problems.
judge.ground_truth_summary: PR #9583 replaced the MemoryStyle::Static check with can_elide_bounds_check instead of can_use_virtual_memory. With guard=0 and reservation <4GiB, re-protection is skipped, so a pooled slot exposes prior pages to the next instance.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 points at cow.rs:437. It names the can_elide_bounds_check gate, explains why it is stricter than the old Static match, and gives the guard=0 with reservation <4GiB trigger. It traces the skipped re-protection to stale RW pages in a reused pool slot and recommends can_use_virtual_memory. The diff shows this predicate is still present, with no mitigation.

criteria: LoadKind::derive_operand_size/operand_size_for_vector maps VectorExtend kinds to the per-lane size (S8/S16/S32) instead of S64
Vector-extend loads (load8x8/16x4/32x2 s/u) actually read 8 bytes from linear memory
The derived undersized OperandSize is used for the heap bounds-check access size
Result: bounds check undercounts the access, so the load can read up to 4-7 bytes past the validated bound
judge.findings_summary: Five findings flag lane-size OperandSize for v128 extend loads causing undersized bounds checks versus 8-byte reads. The others are unrelated aarch64 issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: operand_size_for_vector returns S8/S16/S32 for 8-byte SIMD extend loads. This undersized size is used for bounds checking and emission, allowing out-of-bounds reads past linear memory.
judge.reasoning: Findings 1-5 identify the same root cause. operand_size_for_vector (masm.rs:304-314) returns lane sizes, and derive_operand_size feeds that size into emit_compute_heap_address for the bounds check. Meanwhile vpmovsx/zx reads an m64 operand, so the access can overread by up to 7 bytes. The PR diff confirms the mapping and the removal of the explicit S64. The suggested fix matches.

criteria: Trigger: the oneshot receiver errors because the sender was dropped without the guest calling response-outparam::set
Faulty assumption: a receiver error implies the spawned task returned Err
Sink: expect_err on the task.await result in handle_request in src/commands/serve.rs
Trigger case: the guest handle returns Ok(()) without calling set, so the task yields Ok(Ok(())) and the host panics
Impact: a guest-driven, remotely triggerable panic or DoS in wasmtime serve
judge.findings_summary: One finding: expect_err in serve.rs panics when the guest returns from handle without calling response-outparam::set. The scanner traces the full chain and suggests handling Ok(Ok(())) explicitly.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In handle_request, a receiver error is assumed to mean the task failed. When a guest returns Ok without calling set, expect_err panics, letting a guest crash the wasmtime serve host (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The scanner gives the exact causal chain. The receiver errors when the sender is dropped, the guest returns Ok without calling set, task.await yields Ok(Ok(())), and expect_err panics at line 461. The PR diff confirms the code is present and unmitigated. The scanner says tokio catches the panic and downplays the impact, but it confirms the panic is reachable and does not deny the root cause.

criteria: In DrcCompiler::alloc_array (drc.rs ~323-328), the code computes num_gc_refs for arrays whose elements are GC refs.
num_gc_refs is set to the `size` value from emit_array_size, which is the total byte size, instead of the array's element count (len).
That value is ORed into the GC header's reserved bits via emit_gc_raw_alloc and gc_alloc_raw.
The DRC collector's tracing (trace_gc_ref) uses num_gc_refs to bound the slice of outgoing edges, so it overruns the object when the array is dec-ref'd or collected.
Guest Wasm can trigger it by allocating an array of GC refs and letting it die.
judge.findings_summary: 13 findings. Finding 3 exactly identifies that alloc_array passes the array's byte size as num_gc_refs, which makes trace_gc_ref's slice exceed the object. Findings 4, 6 and 7 are related sinks. The other findings cover unrelated issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: DRC alloc_array uses the array byte size (`size`) instead of the element count as num_gc_refs for GC-ref arrays. The collector then traces past the object's reference slots, reading or dec-ref'ing out of bounds.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 names the same root cause at drc.rs:323-328: byte size is used instead of element count for GC-ref arrays. It traces the same chain through emit_gc_raw_alloc into the header and then to trace_gc_ref's over-long slice. The PR diff confirms the bug. The finding calls the effect a bounds-checked panic rather than a raw OOB read, but that only reframes the impact. It does not dispute the GT causal chain or call it fixed.

criteria: A module-supplied const expr (struct.new/struct.new_default) triggers GC struct allocation during eval
StructRef::_new can fail (e.g., GC heap OOM) and the error propagates out of eval via ?
A pre-existing caller (initialize_vmctx_globals) unconditionally .expect()s the eval result
Result: host panic instead of returning an instantiation error to the embedder
judge.findings_summary: 13 findings, mostly GC refcount use-after-free issues. Finding 5 says GC heap exhaustion in const-eval struct.new reaches .expect at instance.rs:1281 and panics the host during instantiation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Const-eval now allocates GC structs. StructRef::_new can fail, but initialize_vmctx_globals still calls expect on eval's result, so it panics instead of returning the error.
judge.reasoning: Finding 5 matches the full GT chain. StructRef::_new can return GcHeapOutOfMemory under AutoAssertNoGc, struct_new propagates it with ?, and initialize_vmctx_globals at instance.rs:1281-1283 calls .expect, so the host panics. The finding cites const_expr.rs:95 and the same .expect site. The PR diff shows the ? propagation, and the PR adds no change to the caller's expect.

criteria: Leak site is HostGraphExecutionContext::compute in crates/wasi-nn/src/wit.rs.
compute receives the input tensor Resource handles as owned values (Vec<NamedTensor> by value), so the guest gives up its handles.
Each input is fetched with table.get (a borrow plus clone), not removed with table.delete.
No other code path deletes these input resources, so ResourceTable entries and tensor data grow without bound on every compute call.
judge.findings_summary: Of 26 findings, most cover tensor length validation and backend panics. Finding 18 identifies the compute() resource leak: owned input tensor handles are fetched with get/clone and never deleted from the ResourceTable.
judge.ground_truth_summary: wit.rs compute() takes ownership of the input tensor resource handles but only borrows them with table.get. It never deletes them, so every compute call leaks ResourceTable entries and tensor memory.
judge.reasoning: Finding 18 matches every criterion. It places the bug in wit.rs compute at lines 252-258 and explains that the owned handles are consumed. It notes the code uses get plus clone and never calls delete, and recommends delete as the fix. The PR diff confirms this code is present with no cleanup. Calling the impact low-severity DoS does not deny that the bug is active.

criteria: Location is CompiledFunctionsTable::func_by_text_offset, in the sparse-kind branch of module_artifacts.rs
sparse_index is computed as a namespace-local offset (index - func_loc_starts[ns_idx])
That local offset is used as an absolute SparseIndex into the shared sparse_indices map without adding sparse_starts[ns_idx]
Impact: wrong FuncKey, or a downstream assert panic (e.g. BuiltinFunctionIndex bounds) for sparse namespaces after the first
Evaluated PR code still contains the unadjusted lookup
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports that func_by_text_offset omits sparse_starts[ns_idx] when indexing sparse_indices, giving wrong keys or a BuiltinFunctionIndex assert panic. The other findings cover unrelated shared-table and deserialization concerns.
judge.ground_truth_summary: func_by_text_offset uses a namespace-local offset as the absolute SparseIndex into shared sparse_indices without adding sparse_starts[ns_idx]. Sparse namespaces after the first get wrong keys or panic.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly: same function and lines (481-483), the same missing sparse_starts[ns_idx] base offset, and the same impact (wrong key, or a BuiltinFunctionIndex assert panic). The PR diff confirms the buggy code is present and adds no fix. The finding's note that reachability needs a profiler only qualifies one trigger path; it does not contradict the active bug.

criteria: A matching netrc 'default' entry carries neither a login nor a password.
parsenetrc() still returns NETRC_SUCCESS for that empty default match.
The success return sets conn->bits.netrc=TRUE in override_login().
Curl_http_output_auth()/Curl_auth_allowed_to_host() trust bits.netrc and resend credentials to a different host after a redirect.
No check excludes the login-less, password-less default case.
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: a NULL dereference in str_has_ctrl, wrong-login password returned, empty URL user treated as a specific login, a reversed-order password dropped, and stale our_login/found state. None covers an empty default being treated as success.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A netrc 'default' entry with no login or password still returned NETRC_SUCCESS. That set bits.netrc and allowed credentials from the first host to be resent to a different host after a redirect.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds 'else if(!login && !password) retcode = NETRC_FILE_MISSING;' at out:, so an empty default no longer yields success and bits.netrc is not set. The GT chain is broken. No scanner finding identifies an empty default returning success. Finding 2(3) concerns a default entry that does have a password, paired with a URL username, which is a different trigger. The other findings cover a NULL dereference, specific-login matching, ordering and stale-state issues.

criteria: ldap_set_option() is called with a NULL handle, which mutates the process-global LDAP context
The mutated options are TLS-critical (REQUIRE_CERT, CACERTFILE) or connection options, set before ldap_init()
Concurrent transfers in other threads share and observe the weakened global setting (data race / cross-transfer leakage)
The missing rule is per-connection handle scoping: ldap_init() should run first and its handle be passed to every ldap_set_option() call
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: verification hardcoded off, ldaps downgraded to cleartext without HAVE_LDAP_SSL, NULL deref in Novell builds, implicit ldapssl prototypes, and use_ssl ignored. None covers a global-context data race.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ldap_set_option(NULL, TLS options) before ldap_init() mutates the global OpenLDAP context, so concurrent threads inherit weakened certificate verification. The fix is to init the handle first and pass it to all option calls.
judge.reasoning: The PR moves ldap_init() before the option calls and passes the server handle to every OpenLDAP ldap_set_option() call, which removes the global-context race. No scanner finding describes global option mutation through a NULL handle shared across threads. Finding 1 covers hardcoded verify_cert=0, a different root cause. Finding 3 mentions a NULL handle only as a crash risk in Novell builds, not as a race.

criteria: Vulnerable code is the wolfSSL branch of Curl_vquic_tls_verify_peer in lib/vquic/vquic-tls.c
The guard makes the hostname/cert check conditional on SNI presence, i.e. `peer->sni && check`
When peer->sni is NULL (IP-literal host), the check is skipped entirely
The function falls through returning CURLE_OK, so the certificate is accepted unverified
The finding must say this skip-on-NULL-SNI logic is active in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicErrors in the same function: wolfSSL_check_domain_name is ineffective when called after the handshake, and comparing against SSL_FAILURE treats negative error codes as success (fail-open).
judge.ground_truth_summary: An inverted condition `if(peer->sni && check fails)` skips wolfSSL QUIC certificate/hostname verification when SNI is NULL (IP-literal hosts), so the function returns CURLE_OK without verifying.
