judge.reasoning: The evaluated diff uses `peer->sni ? peer->sni : peer->hostname` and always calls wolfSSL_check_domain_name, so no `peer->sni &&` guard skips the check. criteria: sanitize_cookie_path strips the lone '/' of path="/", leaving a zero-length sanitized path

criteria: Remote peer sends repeated PING frames while not reading from the connection.

criteria: url_match_auth_nego's final guard tests NTLM flags (want_ntlm_http/want_proxy_ntlm_http) instead of the Negotiate flags

criteria: verifystatus (OCSP stapling required) is enabled on the Apple SecTrust path in ossl_apple_verify

criteria: write_paused state drives cf_h2_update_local_win to shrink the stream receive window to zero

criteria: Cookie getlist returns live jar Cookie pointers rather than independent copies

criteria: tftp_state_timeout handles the already-expired overall timer branch (Curl_timeleft < 0)
That branch returns literal 0 instead of the negative timeout_ms

Result: the detected timeout is masked from the caller and the transfer is not promptly aborted

criteria: Shared SSL session cache peer->sessions list is protected by the scache lock
Curl_ssl_scache_take releases the lock via Curl_ssl_scache_unlock before trace logging
Trace logging reads peer->sessions via Curl_llist_count after the unlock
Concurrent mutation or freeing of the peer/sessions between unlock and read causes a data race or use-after-free
Scanner finding identifies this unlock-before-read ordering in Curl_ssl_scache_take
judge.findings_summary: Eight findings: ngtcp2 0-RTT logic issues (verification result returned as a byte count, connected-state timing, early-data limits, rejected 0-RTT handling, ALPN strcmp NULL dereference, session caching) and a quic_tp leak in vtls_scache.c. None concern the scache lock.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Curl_ssl_scache_take unlocks the scache before trace logging that calls Curl_llist_count(&peer->sessions). Another thread can mutate or free the peer in that window, causing a data race or possible use-after-free.

criteria: Session cache lookup in ossl_connect_step1 can resume a cached session even when verifystatus was requested
servercert skips verifystatus() because connssl->reused_session is TRUE
Missing guard: the session-reuse branch lacks a !conn_config->verifystatus check
Result: a resumed handshake bypasses the OCSP status check the user requested
The evaluated code must still lack the guard for the chain to hold

judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds 'ssl_config->primary.sessionid && !conn_config->verifystatus' in ossl_connect_step1. A cached session is therefore never resumed when status verification is requested, and the reused_session skip cannot bypass OCSP. criteria: Reuse path performs shallow struct copy of conn_to_host from old_conn to conn
Source conn_to_host.encalloc is not NULLed or zeroed after the copy, unlike host.encalloc
Both structures share the same encalloc heap pointer
Teardown of old_conn (conn_free/Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname) plus later teardown of conn frees encalloc twice
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: a cpool-lock data race in reuse_conn, a Curl_conn_free disconnect invariant concern, and a stale bits.ipv6_ip after host swap. None is the conn_to_host.encalloc double free.
judge.ground_truth_summary: reuse_conn shallow-copied conn_to_host but NULLed only rawalloc, not encalloc. The encalloc pointer was shared and freed twice on teardown of both connections.

criteria: pop3_perform() reads data->req.no_body to decide whether to set pop3->transfer = PPTRANSFER_INFO
pop3_perform_command() is the callee that recomputes data->req.no_body for the current command
The read happens before the recompute, so the transfer decision uses stale no_body from a prior request or reused handle state

criteria: Curl_get_line loops on fgets() in while(1)

criteria: common_init parses ch_layouts string and grows buf->channel_layouts via av_realloc_array
Realloc result stored in tmp is not assigned back to buf->channel_layouts

criteria: ff_thread_progress_report performs the atomic release-store of progress outside/before acquiring progress_mutex

criteria: Read-direction tile() parsing in cbs_apv_syntax_template.c

The Decoder outlives the codec context's buffer, so its pointer dangles
A consumer (e.g. enc_open copying dec->subtitle_header) reads the dangling pointer after the free, causing a use-after-free
No ownership transfer exists: no copy, no free in dec_free, no retain mechanism
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: uninitialized or NULL Decoder pointer in enc_open, av_assert0 abort, and a hypothetical subtitle_header_size+1 overflow. None describes a borrowed pointer or use-after-free.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dec_open stores a borrowed pointer to the AVCodecContext's subtitle_header in Decoder without copying it. When the codec context frees it, encoder consumers read freed memory (use-after-free).
judge.reasoning: The PR diff copies the header with av_mallocz plus memcpy and frees it in dec_free. This gives Decoder its own buffer and breaks the use-after-free chain. None of the scanner findings report a borrowed or dangling pointer. They report an uninitialized or NULL dec in enc_open, an assert-triggered abort, and a hypothetical integer overflow in size+1. These are adjacent issues, not the GT lifetime bug.

criteria: Search-or-allocate loop over c->heif_item[] matching item_id in mov_read_iloc/mov_read_infe
Loop can end without a match and without a free slot (j == nb_heif_item)
No post-loop check distinguishes the not-found case; only a !item ENOMEM check exists
The stale last-entry pointer is then used, overwriting an unrelated HEIFItem (item_id, extents, type, stream)
Results in corrupted demuxer state or an assertion failure downstream
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: a name leak on the new INVALIDDATA path, O(n^2) lookup DoS, duplicate infe ids creating orphan streams, is_idat_relative never being cleared, and iinf cleanup leaks plus compatibility rejection. All of them treat the not-found guard as present.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The HEIF item lookup loop lacks a not-found check (j == nb_heif_item). The stale last-entry pointer then overwrites an unrelated HEIFItem, corrupting state and triggering an assertion. The evaluated PR includes the fix.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds `if (j == c->nb_heif_item) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;` in mov_read_iloc and the matching check in mov_read_infe. This breaks the GT chain. No finding reports that an unrelated item gets overwritten. Findings 1 and 5 explicitly cite the new not-found guard as working. The other findings cover adjacent issues: leaks, quadratic lookup, duplicate-id handling, and a stale is_idat_relative flag.

criteria: get_freq_strides() output buffer is ld->freq_res (9 entries), aliased with the input stride selector
Writes of up to data_bands+1 (≤29) int16 entries overflow the 9-element freq_res array
Aliasing corrupts ld->freq_res[set_idx] and later loop indices into ld->last_data
Evaluated code still passes ld->freq_res as the output buffer to get_freq_strides
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings. One is an unclamped bsOttBandsPhase overflow, including into freq_stride_map. Others cover uninitialized time_pair, a decode_tsd overflow, logic errors, and an off-by-one in map_index_data. None covers freq_res aliasing.
judge.ground_truth_summary: get_freq_strides() wrote up to 29 entries into ld->freq_res[9], which was also its stride input. This caused an out-of-bounds write and corrupted indices into last_data. Fixed here by using a local freq_stride_map.
judge.reasoning: The PR already uses a dedicated local buffer, freq_stride_map[MPS_MAX_PARAM_BANDS+1], instead of ld->freq_res. That removes both the aliasing and the 9-entry overflow. Finding 1 reports a different trigger: an unclamped bsOttBandsPhase (29-31) overflowing freq_stride_map and other buffers. That is not the GT freq_res aliasing. No finding describes freq_res being used as get_freq_strides output.

criteria: huff_decode() mutates the caller's p_data[0]/p_data[1] pointers (data[i] += 1) in the time_pair/diff_freq path
ec_pair_dec() later passes the possibly-advanced p_data pointers to attach_lsb() instead of the base data_pair arrays
attach_lsb iterates the full nb_bands, up to 28, from the shifted pointer
Result is a one-element out-of-bounds stack read/write past the 28-element data_pair/data_diff arrays
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: freq_res=0 giving 255 bands and overflows, preroll config not rolled back, discarded 2D frequency-pair data, TSD integer truncation, and ignored map_index_data return values. None covers attach_lsb using shifted pointers.
judge.ground_truth_summary: huff_decode advances the caller's p_data pointers. ec_pair_dec then passes these shifted pointers to attach_lsb with the full nb_bands count, causing a one-element out-of-bounds stack read/write.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, attach_lsb() is called with data_pair[0] and data_pair[1] directly, not with the mutated p_data pointers. That breaks the GT chain. No scanner finding describes the pointer-advance mismatch. Finding 1 covers an unrelated freq_res=255 band-count overflow. Finding 3 is a data-discard logic bug in huff_decode, not an OOB access.

criteria: Source: bsOttBandsPhase and/or bsResidualBands read via get_bits(gb,5) in decode_usac_element_pair
Missing guard: no range check of these fields against numBands derived from bsFreqRes
Sink: unbounded otts_bands_phase/residual_bands used as nb_bands loop bound/index in ff_aac_ec_data_dec/parse_mps212 per-band arrays
Consequence: out-of-bounds read/write of fixed-size per-band buffers
Evaluated code must lack the numBands validation
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: uninitialized time_pair, swapped diff decode arguments, IPD mapping before the error check, stale param_sets, dropped pair_vec data, and the decode_tsd int cast. None address otts_bands_phase/residual_bands bounds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bsOttBandsPhase and bsResidualBands are parsed from the bitstream without validation against numBands for freq_res. They are later used as band counts in MPS212 decoding, causing OOB access.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already rejects the bad values. It returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA when freq_res is 0, when otts_bands_phase > numBands, or when residual_bands > numBands. That breaks the GT causal chain. None of the scanner findings target missing bounds validation of bsOttBandsPhase/bsResidualBands. They describe unrelated issues: uninitialized memory, swapped arguments, IPD error-check ordering, stale param_sets, and TSD truncation.

criteria: Vulnerable code is in h2645_sei_to_side_data in libavcodec/h2645_sei.c, in the ambient viewing environment branch
dst_env is wrapped in an AVBufferRef and passed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext, which may take ownership of or free the buffer
dst_env fields are written AFTER that ownership-transferring call
The resulting write to possibly freed or already-published memory is identified as the use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicError findings in pthread_frame.c init_thread. One says global side data reaches only the first worker thread's frames. The other says avcodec_open2 frees user-set decoded_side_data.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Use-after-free in h2645_sei_to_side_data. AmbientViewingEnvironment fields are written after the buffer is passed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext, which may free or take ownership of it. This is fixed in the evaluated PR.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the dst_env fields are set before ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext is called, so the GT ordering bug is fixed. Neither scanner finding covers this ordering. Both concern pthread_frame.c: one is about frame-thread propagation of global side data, the other about freeing user-supplied decoded_side_data. These are unrelated issues.

criteria: Vulnerable code is the boundary index mirroring in vif_filter1d (vertical ii and horizontal jj passes)
The mirroring is a single-step reflection that is only valid when overshoot is no larger than the image dimension
Trigger is image dimensions smaller than filt_w/2, such as a 1x1 input
The sink is an out-of-bounds read of src[ii*src_stride+j] or temp[jj] with an index still outside [0,dim-1]
judge.findings_summary: One TypeConfusion finding: config_input_ref is said to lack a pixel-format equality check, causing an 8-bit vs 16-bit mismatch and an OOB read in the offset functions. The PR code already contains this check.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Single-step index reflection in vif_filter1d fails when image dimensions are smaller than filt_w/2, so ii/jj stay out of range and src/temp are read out of bounds.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR replaces the single-step reflection with avpriv_mirror(), which handles repeated folding, so the GT causal chain is broken. The scanner instead reports a missing pixel-format equality check in config_input_ref. That is a different root cause in a different function, and the PR code actually contains that format check. No finding addresses the mirroring logic in vif_filter1d.

criteria: Energy array en sized too small (2 elements) for up to 3 TNS filters
Loop over g up to n_filt=3 indexes en[g] / en[!g] with g=2
Out-of-bounds stack read past en array end
Triggered for non-LOW profile long windows (order==TNS_MAX_ORDER)
judge.findings_summary: Five LogicError findings: NaN gain bypasses the threshold, an always-true order/length ternary, wrong window band indexing in the energy loop, a wrong coef_start stride, and the coefficient compression/3-bit mismatch. None is the en[] overflow.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The en[2] energy array is read at en[2] when n_filt=3 (AAC Main long windows) via en[g] < en[!g], a stack buffer over-read in ff_aac_search_for_tns.
judge.reasoning: In the PR, en is now float[4], with en[2] or en[3] set to en[0], and the comparison is en[g] < en[g+1]. At most en[3] is read, which stays in bounds. So the GT overflow is fixed in this snapshot. No scanner finding reports an en out-of-bounds access. All five findings are unrelated logic or correctness issues, and finding 3 explicitly says it is not a memory-safety bug.

criteria: avformat_free_context guards the ff_flush_packet_queue call behind s->iformat
The guard skips freeing si->packet_buffer, which lives on FFFormatContext
Muxers fill packet_buffer via ff_interleave_add_packet, so queued packets leak on free
No separate unconditional free of packet_buffer exists in avformat_free_context
judge.findings_summary: Two TypeConfusion findings: demuxing union fields alias muxer state, reachable via avformat_flush/ff_flush_packet_queue and avformat_queue_attached_pictures on output contexts.
judge.ground_truth_summary: An overly broad if (s->iformat) guard around ff_flush_packet_queue in avformat_free_context skips freeing muxer packet_buffer, leaking interleave-queue packets.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds an unconditional avpriv_packet_list_free(&si->packet_buffer) before the guarded flush, so muxer packet_buffer is freed and the GT leak is absent. Neither scanner finding reports a packet_buffer leak. Both instead describe union aliasing type confusion through avformat_flush and avformat_queue_attached_pictures on output contexts. That is a different trigger and sink, and finding 1 even suggests the iformat guard as its fix.

criteria: Error path is the new subblock-duration validation in param_parse (total_duration != duration)
param is allocated earlier via av_iamf_param_definition_alloc and owned locally
That error path returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA without calling av_free(param)
Result is a memory leak of param on malformed IAMF input
Finding must identify the missing free/leak, not other validation weaknesses
judge.findings_summary: Two reports of unsigned wraparound bypassing the new duration checks in param_parse and parameter_block_obu, and one report that zero subblock_duration is accepted. No memory leak is reported.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new subblock-duration check in param_parse returned without av_free(param), leaking the allocated param definition on malformed input.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the new check in param_parse calls av_free(param) before returning, so the GT leak is fixed. None of the scanner findings mention a leak. Findings 1 and 2 report 32-bit wraparound in total_duration that bypasses the check. Finding 3 reports that zero subblock durations are accepted. Finding 2 also states that the error path is memory-safe. These are adjacent validation issues, not the GT leak.

criteria: Trigger is a non-NULL empty exprs string ("") supplied to the filter
The validation only checks for a NULL pointer, not an empty string, so the empty string passes
No tokens are parsed, so last_expr stays NULL/unset and nb_channels stays 0
With expected_nb_channels > 0, ADD_EXPRESSION(last_expr) passes NULL to av_expr_parse, and strlen() dereferences it
The chain is still active in the evaluated code because no empty-string guard exists
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings: OOB read in val(), unset last_expr with '|'-only exprs, outlink/inlink channel-count mismatch, uninitialized ret, channel_values leak, layout ref leak, and an unused out_channel_layout field.
judge.ground_truth_summary: An empty exprs string passes a NULL-only check. Zero tokens are parsed, so a NULL last_expr is passed to av_expr_parse and strlen(NULL) crashes. This PR already includes the empty-string check.
judge.reasoning: The PR code checks `!eval->exprs || !*eval->exprs`, which rejects the empty string, so the GT chain is broken. Finding 2 reaches the same sink (last_expr passed to av_expr_parse) but uses a different trigger: a delimiter-only string such as "|". It explicitly notes that this input passes the emptiness check. That makes it an adjacent bug with a different trigger, not the GT. No other finding targets this chain.

criteria: prepareForSwap copies dynamic elements only when the buffer is physically inside the nursery (ChunkPtrIsInsideNursery), ignoring buffer-allocator ownership metadata
A tenured object can end up holding a buffer marked nursery-owned after swapping with a nursery object
A later nursery collection frees that nursery-owned buffer, so the tenured object's elements_ dangles (UAF)
The copy ignores shifted elements: memmove starts from the shifted header and the new elements pointer is not adjusted by numShifted
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: unguarded MarkTenuredAlloc in scan_obj, unguarded GetAllocSize in addSizeOfExcludingThis, and small nursery-owned buffers created by prepareForSwap and realloc. None identifies the swap ownership UAF or the shifted-element copy bug.
judge.ground_truth_summary: prepareForSwap copied buffers only when physically in the nursery, so a tenured object could keep a nursery-owned buffer that a minor GC later frees (UAF). The copy also ignored shifted elements.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR copies elements whenever IsInsideNursery(this) != IsInsideNursery(other). It allocates with ownership matching other, copies from getUnshiftedElementsHeader, and adds numShifted. This breaks both GT chains. The scanner findings cover scan_obj marking guards, GetAllocSize misuse, and small nursery-owned allocations. Each one treats prepareForSwap as maintaining the invariant, or describes only future or adjacent risks. None identifies the GT ownership mismatch or the shifted-copy bug as active.

criteria: ServiceWorkerContainer is exposed on worker threads (WorkerNavigator.serviceWorker)
DispatchMessage was relaxed to run off the main thread (MOZ_ASSERT(NS_IsMainThread()) removed)
EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch unconditionally uses NS_DispatchToMainThread for a container that may live on a worker
Result: the worker's JS runtime/global is touched from the main thread, a cross-thread race
judge.findings_summary: Two null-deref findings (GetRegistration, ClientSource::PostMessage), one WorkerNavigator CC/Invalidate gap, and one PrincipalInfoToPrincipal off-main-thread data race. None reports main-thread dispatch of worker messages.
judge.ground_truth_summary: After ServiceWorkerContainer was exposed to workers, EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch still used NS_DispatchToMainThread, so DispatchMessage ran on the main thread against the worker's JS runtime. That is a race condition.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch already uses NS_DispatchToCurrentThread, which breaks the GT chain. Finding 4 explicitly notes this NS_DispatchToCurrentThread change and raises an unrelated principal/eTLD thread-contract concern. No finding identifies dispatching to the main thread as the vulnerability. The other findings cover null derefs and a cycle-collection gap, which are adjacent issues.

criteria: PipeWireNode cleanup (destructor/deleter) destroys proxy via pw_proxy_destroy before spa_hook_remove on node_listener_
Hook registered on proxy via pw_node_add_listener ties hook to proxy's listener_list lifetime
spa_hook_remove accesses freed proxy listener_list after proxy destruction (UAF)
Triggered by node destruction e.g. OnRegistryGlobalRemove erasing nodes
Evaluated code must still have the incorrect destroy-then-remove order
judge.findings_summary: Eight findings: uninitialized stream_, memcpy OOB read, nodes_ data race, null meta deref, null session, framerate divide-by-zero, callback race, and unchecked pw_registry_bind. None cover hook/proxy cleanup order.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The PipeWireNode cleanup calls pw_proxy_destroy before spa_hook_remove. This frees the proxy listener_list that the hook references, causing a UAF during node removal. The benign snapshot has the correct order.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated code's ~PipeWireNode calls spa_hook_remove before pw_proxy_destroy, which is the correct order, so the GT chain is broken. No scanner finding describes the wrong cleanup order. Finding 3 covers data races on nodes_ and finding 8 covers a null proxy; both are adjacent bugs, not the GT root cause.

criteria: emitGuardIsNumber passes Int32/Float32 through without converting them to Double
An MSign is created with Int32 input and Double output (the Int32->Double type-mismatch case)
LIRGenerator::visitSign's mismatch branch assumes Double->Int32 and selects LSignDI for that case
The wrong LIR choice causes a wrong-register write or stale float data (type confusion)
No LSignID path exists to handle the Int32->Double case
judge.findings_summary: One finding: IsNumberType includes Int64, so emitGuardIsNumber and emitLoadDoubleResult could accept untagged Int64 values. The scanner calls this latent and unreachable and gives no concrete path.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Removing the Double conversion in emitGuardIsNumber lets MSign receive Int32 input with Double output. visitSign wrongly picks LSignDI, writes the wrong register, and causes type confusion. The PR adds LSignID, which fixes this.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds an LSignID branch in visitSign that handles Int32 input with Double output, which breaks the GT causal chain. The scanner instead reports a different issue: IsNumberType accepting the Int64 MIR type. It does not identify the visitSign/LSignDI mis-selection. It also admits it has no reachable path and calls the issue a latent hazard. This is an adjacent, hypothetical concern, not the GT bug.

criteria: Caller (SelectionNodeCache::MaybeCollect) invokes iterator Init(range) without checking its nsresult
Iterator pointer members (mCurNode, mFirst, mLast, mClosestCommonInclusiveAncestor) are not default-initialized, so they stay indeterminate when Init fails
IsDone()/Next()/GetCurrentNode() are then used on the failed iterator, reading uninitialized pointers
Path is reachable via nsINode::IsSelected / LookUpSelection cache paths
Finding must identify use of uninitialized iterator state as the sink
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: MaybeCollect iterates the range's default boundaries but excludes containers based on cross-shadow boundaries. With a stale cross-shadow sub-range, unselected nodes get cached as fully selected, causing wrong highlighting and debug assertion crashes.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The unchecked iter.Init(range) in MaybeCollect plus non-default-initialized ContentIteratorBase pointer members let IsDone()/Next() read uninitialized pointers after Init fails.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already contains the fix. MaybeCollect checks NS_FAILED(rv) and continues. The iterator members are default-initialized to nullptr, and Init is marked [[nodiscard]]. The scanner reports a different issue: a logic mismatch between default and cross-shadow range boundaries that caches wrong nodes as selected. It explicitly says there is no memory corruption. It does not identify an unchecked Init or uninitialized members.

criteria: Error.captureStackTrace passes a startAt/constructorOpt function into SavedStacks::insertFrames
Frames are not pushed to stackChain until startAt has been seen, so stackChain can be empty
Async-stack reparenting block is entered while startAt has not been seen and stackChain is empty
Unchecked stackChain[stackChain.length()-1] access causes an out-of-bounds read/write
No guard tied to seenStartAt or stackChain emptiness prevents entry to the reparenting block
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: empty-stackChain OOB in reparenting when startAt is the bottom frame of an async activation (seenStartAt flips late). Finding 2: wrong realm principals for filtering. Finding 3: live-cache fast path bypasses startAt censoring.
judge.ground_truth_summary: startAt delays pushes to stackChain. When startAt is never seen, async reparenting still indexes stackChain[length-1] on an empty vector, an out-of-bounds read. The PR's seenStartAt guard fixes this case.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds a `&& seenStartAt` guard, which breaks the GT chain: reparenting with startAt never seen. Finding 1 targets the same sink, but by a different trigger. seenStartAt flips right after the matching startAt frame is skipped, so the chain can be empty on that iteration. This may be a real residual off-by-one bug. Under the rubric it is a same-sink, different-trigger near match, not the GT chain. Findings 2 and 3 are unrelated.

criteria: mStylesheetDocument is a strong RefPtr that the processor registers itself on via AddMutationObserver(this) in ImportStylesheet
The cycle-collection Unlink path, via the auto-generated NS_IMPL_CYCLE_COLLECTION_WRAPPERCACHE macro, clears mStylesheetDocument
Unlink clears the reference without first calling RemoveMutationObserver(this)
The document keeps a dangling observer pointer to the freed processor, and its later destruction or notification (NodeWillBeDestroyed / LastRelease) causes a UAF
The evaluated code still auto-unlinks mStylesheetDocument with no custom Unlink
judge.findings_summary: Reports that the strong mStylesheetDocument is missing from the CC traverse/unlink macros, causing a document memory leak. It notes that adding it without a custom Unlink would cause a UAF, framed as a hypothetical.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The CC macro auto-unlinks the strong mStylesheetDocument without calling RemoveMutationObserver. The document keeps a dangling pointer to the freed processor, causing a UAF when the document is later destroyed.
judge.reasoning: This is a benign snapshot with the fix applied. The scanner itself reports that the CC macro does not include mStylesheetDocument, so no auto-unlink happens without RemoveMutationObserver. Its main finding is a different bug: an uncollectable-cycle memory leak. It mentions the GT UAF only as a hypothetical risk of a future fix, not as an active vulnerability. The GT causal chain is therefore not supported.

criteria: EnsureLocale writes the shared mLocale with no idempotency guard, so a repeated call can reallocate the string.
Multiple main-thread callers (AllowedForWindowInternal, GetLoadInfo, ExecWorkerOnMainThread) can trigger repeated writes after workers already exist.
Worker threads read mLocale through GetLocale (e.g. from OpenInternal) without synchronization while those writes happen.
The evaluated code must still lack an idempotency or synchronization guard that prevents rewrites after initialization.
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: untrusted IPC locale reaching the parent, a null manager dereference in GetLocale, an empty-locale logic issue, and a DataRace on mLocale that the scanner itself calls safe because of the idempotency flag and ordering.
judge.ground_truth_summary: EnsureLocale lacked idempotency or synchronization, so repeated main-thread calls could rewrite mLocale while worker threads read it via GetLocale. This PR's mLocaleInitialized guard fixes that.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds the mLocaleInitialized early return, guarded by the main-thread capability, so mLocale is written only once. That breaks the GT chain of repeated writes racing with worker reads. Scanner finding 4 names the right race but says the ordering is safe by construction, that mLocaleInitialized suppresses later writes, and that it is not a demonstrated race. That is a future-risk concern, not an active vulnerability. The other findings cover different bugs.

criteria: AlertNotification::GetAction returns an nsIAlertAction from mActions via an out-param (nsIAlertAction**)
The out-param is assigned a raw pointer without AddRef/forget, so ownership is not transferred
Callers using getter_AddRefs (OnActivate, CreateToastXmlDocument) later release a reference they never gained
The refcount underflows, freeing the action while mActions still holds it (use-after-free)
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: an action-lookup fail-open treated as a body click, a latent null dereference of mAlertNotification, removed alerterror signal handling, and dead settings/snooze comparisons. None are refcount or use-after-free issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: GetAction assigned a raw pointer from mActions to the XPIDL out-param without AddRef. Callers releasing it via getter_AddRefs underflow the refcount, causing use-after-free. The fix, RefPtr copy plus forget, is already applied in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff uses RefPtr<nsIAlertAction> match = action; match.forget(aAlertAction), which transfers ownership correctly, so the GT use-after-free is absent from the evaluated code. None of the scanner findings mention a missing AddRef, refcount mismatch, or use-after-free in GetAction. They cover logic errors, a latent null dereference, and alerterror handling instead.

criteria: nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1/OnStartRequest on the main thread reads the transaction conn info via unlocked GetConnInfo() to feed ProcessAltService
nsHttpTransaction::GetConnInfo reads mConnInfo without mLock
DisableHttp3 on the socket thread concurrently swaps mConnInfo without synchronization
No lock-protected snapshot replaces the main-thread read in the nsHttpChannel path
judge.findings_summary: Two alt-svc logic bugs: aDontValidate leaking across mappings, and no TTL refresh on existing mappings. One data race: TRRServiceChannel calls unlocked GetConnInfo while the socket thread mutates mConnInfo; it notes nsHttpChannel is safe.
judge.ground_truth_summary: nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1 calls mTransaction->GetConnInfo() on the main thread without a lock. This races with DisableHttp3's mConnInfo.swap on the socket thread, a TSan-detected data race.
judge.reasoning: In this PR, nsHttpChannel gets its conn info from TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo. That call returns mFinalizedConnInfo under mLock, which breaks the GT chain in ContinueProcessResponse1. Scanner finding 2 does describe an unlocked GetConnInfo race, but its trigger is TRRServiceChannel::OnStartRequest, a different call site. It explicitly says nsHttpChannel uses the safe pattern. That makes it a same-sink, different-trigger near match. The other findings are unrelated alt-svc logic issues.

criteria: Location is Code::createManyLazyEntryStubs in WasmCode.cpp
Base for calleePtr comes from tierCodeBlock.segment->base() instead of tierCodeBlock.base()
Offsets are CodeBlock-relative, so adding them to the segment base gives a wrong pointer when codeBase != segment base
The bad calleePtr is embedded in the generated entry stub, which then calls the wrong code address
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: the MOZ_ASSERT bounds checks in CodeBlock::disassemble still compare CodeBlock-relative offsets against the segment length. It also notes dead code (FuncExport::offsetBy) and a stale comment.
judge.ground_truth_summary: createManyLazyEntryStubs computed calleePtr from segment->base() rather than CodeBlock::base() after offsets became CodeBlock-relative. This produces a wild callee pointer in the lazy entry stubs.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already changes createManyLazyEntryStubs to use tierCodeBlock.base() for calleePtr, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner's only finding is about stale debug assertions in CodeBlock::disassemble comparing against segment->lengthBytes(). That is a different function, sink and bug class. It does not cover the calleePtr base mismatch.

criteria: readAllocSiteIndex records the pre-append vector length as the index for the new element
masm.append() result is not checked, or the index is not abandoned on OOM, so the index points one past the end
Caller continues and loadAllocSiteInstanceData indexes allocSitesPatches()[allocSiteIndex] with that stale index
setPatchOffset writes out of bounds on the missing element
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: 32-bit overflow of sizeof(AllocSite)*count in Instance::init, reachable via dead-code alloc sites that skip the overflow guard, and per-instance memory amplification from dead-code alloc ops.
judge.ground_truth_summary: readAllocSiteIndex ignores an OOM in masm.append, so the returned index is past the vector end. loadAllocSiteInstanceData then calls setPatchOffset on a nonexistent element, an out-of-bounds write.
judge.reasoning: The PR's readAllocSiteIndex returns !masm.oom(), and every caller returns false on failure. The stale index is therefore never used, which breaks the GT chain. The scanner instead reports an integer overflow in the Instance::init allocation size caused by dead-code alloc sites, plus memory amplification. Those are a different trigger and a different sink. Neither finding describes the OOM append index going out of bounds.

criteria: CachedBAxisMeasurement pointer is obtained from frame properties and held in a local before the reflow call in MeasuringReflow
parent->ReflowChild() triggers MarkIntrinsicISizesDirty -> MarkCachedGridMeasurementsDirty, which removes and deletes the property
The stale pointer is dereferenced after ReflowChild (cachedMeasurement->Update write) without being re-fetched
The evaluated code still uses the pre-reflow pointer after ReflowChild
judge.findings_summary: Reports a possible UAF on the cache-hit path after FinishReflowChild/DidReflow. Acknowledges the re-fetch after ReflowChild is correct and that no confirmed trigger exists.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A stale CachedBAxisMeasurement pointer is held across ReflowChild, which can delete the property via MarkIntrinsicISizesDirty. The later Update() call then writes to freed heap memory.
judge.reasoning: The PR scopes the hit-path pointer inside the if-statement and re-fetches the pointer after ReflowChild before calling Update, which breaks the GT chain. The scanner explicitly says the miss path is handled correctly. Instead it reports a different trigger: dereferences after FinishReflowChild/DidReflow on the hit path. It also says it found no invalidating path, so the report is a latent pattern rather than the GT bug.

criteria: Location: TenuringTracer::promoteString, dependent-string promotion path
Root base from rootBaseDuringMinorGC() may differ from the dependent string's direct d.s.u3.base
Branch where root base is NOT in the collected nursery region only forwards the string and omits setBase()
Result: promoted dependent string keeps a stale base pointer, giving UAF when the base chain is later traced

criteria: Set_High_Precision applies 12-bit precision (precision_scale=64) with no check on target bitmap size

criteria: The dists allocation in sdf_generate_bounding_box uses FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, rows, width), treating width as a raw byte item_size

criteria: Ins_SHZ loop limit for the glyph zone (gep2==1) comes from font-controlled contours[n_contours-1]+1

criteria: Writer in ossl_synchronize_rcu publishes the retire-in-order signal (next_to_retire++, prior_signal broadcast, prior_lock unlock) before the qp->users drain loop completes

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, both pthread and win versions take prior_lock and wait for their turn, then run the users drain loop, and only afterwards increment next_to_retire and broadcast. criteria: ossl_quic_get_peer_token calls ossl_quic_build_new_token(peer, NULL, 0) to build a lookup key

criteria: FTS3/4 is marked SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS, making it usable from untrusted schemas

No i64 or sqlite3_malloc64 widening breaks the chain

criteria: Type-disjointness predicate used to fold reference equality (===) to constant false

NodeType lattice allows types with no shared bits but a common concrete subtype (e.g., kAnyHeapObject vs kNumber, both containing kHeapNumber)

criteria: Shared process-wide import wrapper cache whose lookup paths (MaybeGet/CompileWasmImportCallWrapper/FindWrapper) return cached WasmCode pointers

criteria: Lookup functions LookupStruct, LookupArray and LookupFunctionSignature in canonical-types.cc are involved

criteria: On 64-bit builds, the TryParseArrayIndex accumulator is a 32-bit type, so `10 * index` wraps for 10-digit strings.

criteria: Trigger: JSON.stringify fast path receives a JSObject/JSArray whose meta-map is the context-less read-only meta_map root (e.g., detached global)

criteria: Vulnerability is in NodeProperties::InferMapsUnsafe, in the kTransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap case

criteria: DecodeAsmJsOpcode asserts the 0xfa prefix with V8_ASSUME/DCHECK instead of checking it at runtime

Attacker-crafted bytes (0xfa plus a multi-byte LEB index) reach DECODE(AsmJs) and then DecodeAsmJsOpcode

Finding 1 raises a different concern: the check is not wrapped in VALIDATE, so DecodeError can reach a V8_ASSUME(false) path under NoValidationTag. criteria: Location is ResumeJSObject in src/json/json-stringifier.cc.

Only kWithMapCache uses descriptor_idx, so the GT chain is broken. Finding 4 questions the kWithMapCache assumption as speculative and admits it is not demonstrated. criteria: Lazy new-space page allocation removes the invariant that an allocation failure implies the space is at target capacity
SemiSpaceNewSpaceAllocatorPolicy::EnsureAllocation slow path lacks a ReachedTargetCapacity guard before calling AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity
AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity is reached while current_capacity_ < target_capacity_, e.g. after an OOM or virtual-memory failure
Available() equals the full target capacity (Capacity = max(current, target), Size ≈ 0), so DCHECK_LT(Available(), size_in_bytes) fails
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: Shrink/RewindPages UAF on over-target to-space, epilogue DCHECK violation, stale current_capacity_ after rewind, null deref in FillCurrentPageForTesting, and a false DCHECK in MakeUnusedPagesInToSpaceIterable.
judge.ground_truth_summary: EnsureAllocation lacks a ReachedTargetCapacity guard, so AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity runs below target capacity and its Available()<size DCHECK fails. The evaluated PR already applies this fix.

The scanner findings cover adjacent problems: over-target shrink/UAF, the epilogue DCHECK, RewindPages accounting, and null deref in testing helpers. criteria: Regular wasm functions (WASM_FUNCTION) emit SetStackPointer to switch to the central stack around Fast API calls
The ARM64 SlotToMemOperand FP-to-SP offset conversion optimization stays enabled for that code
The guard disabling SP-relative operands (FPRelativeOnly / invalidates_sp) misses regular wasm function code
Result: SP-relative slot accesses hit the central stack instead of the secondary stack, causing memory corruption or heap CHECK failure
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the new CHECK(IsOnCentralStack) in Isolate::Throw crashes CAPI host functions called on a JSPI secondary stack. Finding 2: the WellKnown_FastApi fallback executes Unreachable after the slow call.

Neither scanner finding concerns SP-relative operand conversion. One finding covers the new CHECK in Isolate::Throw and the CAPI wrapper. The other covers an Unreachable in the WellKnown_FastApi fallback. Both are adjacent issues, not the GT bug.

criteria: Fast-iterable state is cached on a shared DescriptorArray rather than per-invocation/per-map
Promotion from kUnknown to kJsonFast happens at the end of ResumeJSObject
Promotion has no guard checking nof_descriptors (map->NumberOfOwnDescriptors) against descriptors->number_of_descriptors()
A partial prefix validation is therefore treated as full validation of the shared array
A later stringify of an object with more own properties sharing the array takes the kJsonFast path over unvalidated tail descriptors (DCHECK at field_index / wrong property reads)
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: kJsonFast relies on a DCHECK-only field-index compactness invariant, acknowledged as holding today and guarded at 2871. Finding 2: discarded key_result in ResumeFrom is a maintenance risk. Both are hypothetical.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ResumeJSObject promoted a shared DescriptorArray to kJsonFast after validating only the first NumberOfOwnDescriptors entries. Later objects with more properties then skipped validation of the tail descriptors. The PR's nof_descriptors guard fixes this.

Finding 1 explicitly cites this guard, says the invariants hold, and frames its concern as hypothetical future-regression hardening. Finding 2 is an unrelated ordering-invariant concern in ResumeFrom. Neither reports an active partial-validation bug.

criteria: kArchCallCFunction (and/or a WithFrameState variant) is placed outside the IsCallWithDescriptorFlags opcode range, after kArchCallBuiltinPointer
MiscField of CFunction opcodes holds GP/FP parameter counts instead of CallDescriptor flags
VisitCall therefore cannot encode kHasExceptionHandler for fast API C calls
Code generators skip registering an exception handler at fast API call sites, so a throwing fast call traps

It also moves the parameter counts into an immediate input, encodes the flags with EncodeCallDescriptorFlags, and registers handlers in the code generators. criteria: KnownMapsMerger::IntersectWithKnownNodeAspects sets node_type_ to EmptyNodeType when the intersect set is empty

The known-maps-subset 'done' branch intersects to the empty type and returns without emitting a deopt

criteria: Vulnerable site is MaglevGraphBuilder::TryBuildStoreField's double-field path with a transition map

Sink: BuildStoreTaggedField/CanElideWriteBarrier reaches a type contradiction or DCHECK

criteria: Vulnerable operation is the final store of the match count in RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern

Caller pre-populates number_of_matches from cache TryGet on a cache hit, so the in-out contract is broken

criteria: Uint8ArrayToBase64 obtains raw backing-store pointer inside a DisallowGarbageCollection scope

criteria: Type guard in VisitSpeculativeAdditiveOp is narrowed to Signed32 and no longer accepts Unsigned32 inputs
Nodes whose inputs are Unsigned32 fall through to a different lowering path than intended
The PROPAGATE and LOWER phases then assign different UseInfo values to the same input edge

judge.findings_summary: Reports UNREACHABLE crash when SpeculativeNumberAdd/Subtract enters new Integral32 branch without opcode/hint check, triggered via escape analysis narrowing input types.

judge.ground_truth_summary: fd_renumber leaves an fd in both used and free (identity renumber, or a `to` already freed). A later push() pops it and the insert assert panics the host.
judge.reasoning: The task is benign: the PR already carries the fix, and free is a BTreeSet with the duplicate-FD handling applied. No scanner finding describes free-list/used duplication or the push() assert panic. Finding 1 covers resource leaks and orphaning a live resource in fd_renumber. That is the same function but a different sink and mechanism, so it is only a near match. It cites the CVE in RELEASES.md only in passing.

criteria: Trigger: a caller passes a shared MemoryType (MemoryType::shared) to Memory::new / Memory::new_async
Missing guard: Memory::_new has no ty.is_shared() rejection
Sink: the resulting wasmtime::Memory exposes safe unsynchronized APIs (e.g. Memory::data returning &[u8]) over shared linear memory
Impact: data race in safe Rust when another thread writes through SharedMemory concurrently
Related: WasmCoreDump::new collects shared memories as Memory without filtering them out
judge.findings_summary: Ten findings: import shared-flag mismatch, limiter bypass, assert and todo panics, stale base pointer, MemoryCreator bypass, vmimport unwrap, and bulk-memory races. None targets the Memory::new shared-type guard.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Memory::new/_new accepted shared MemoryType without rejection. Safe Memory::data slices over concurrently mutated shared memory cause data races. The coredump path also exposed shared memories through Memory.
judge.reasoning: This is a benign task, and the fix is stated as already applied. No finding names the missing is_shared check in Memory::_new or the coredump path. Finding 1 wraps a shared memory in wasmtime::Memory, but through import type matching, and its sink is a panic in grow, not a safe-API data race. Finding 10 is a data race in bulk-memory libcalls, an adjacent bug. Neither is the same causal chain.

criteria: Vulnerable site is the x64 ISLE lowering rule for fcopysign (F32/F64)
fcopysign operands are not forced into XMM registers before the vector AND/ANDN operations
Load-sinking folds a scalar memory load into the ANDPS/ANDPD memory operand
That folded operand becomes a 128-bit read, going 8 bytes past the checked bound (OOB read, guard-page fault or out-of-sandbox read)
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicError findings: no non-SSE4.1 fallback for vector ceil/floor/nearest/trunc, and libcall_1 panicking via expect on emit_vm_call failure.
judge.ground_truth_summary: x64 fcopysign ISLE rules let a scalar load sink into ANDPS/ANDPD, widening it to a 128-bit read past the bound (OOB read/DoS). The fix forces operands into registers, and that fix is present here.
judge.reasoning: The PR already forces a and b into Xmm registers before x64_andps/andpd, so load-sinking cannot fold the scalar load and the causal chain is broken. Neither scanner finding addresses fcopysign or load widening. Both cover other issues: a missing non-SSE4.1 vector rounding fallback and the expect() panic in libcall_1.

criteria: The F64X2 splat fallback rule (rule 0) passes src directly to x64_pshufd, so load sinking can fold the load into the instruction.
The sunk memory operand is read by the 128-bit pshufd, which reads 16 bytes where the f64 load should read 8.
The result is an out-of-bounds read past the intended address, which can cause a sandbox read or a host crash.
No put_in_xmm or other guard prevents the load from being sunk into pshufd.
judge.findings_summary: The single finding is a LogicError: the movddup sinkable-load rule is gated on SSSE3 instead of SSE3. It argues this could cause a compiler panic or SIGILL under unusual flag settings. The finding calls the core pshufd change correct.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The f64x2.splat fallback passed src directly to pshufd, letting a sunk 8-byte f64 load become a 16-byte memory read. This is an out-of-bounds read on hosts without SSE3.
judge.reasoning: In this PR, the F64X2 rule 0 now uses (put_in_xmm src), which forces the value into a register and prevents load sinking into pshufd. The scanner's only finding is a different issue: rule 5 is gated on use_ssse3 when movddup needs SSE3. The scanner also states that put_in_xmm yields register operands only, which confirms the GT bug is fixed.

criteria: Libcalls table_fill_func_ref/gc_ref expect DefinedTableIndex after the PR
Winch visit_table_fill passes the raw module-level TableIndex instead of converting it via prepare_builtin_defined_table_arg
Imported tables make the TableIndex and DefinedTableIndex spaces diverge
The mismatched index leads to an out-of-bounds get_defined_table panic or access to the wrong table
Evaluated code must still show Winch inserting the raw table index
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the table.fill libcalls trust the compiler-emitted (vmctx, defined index) pair, and a hypothetical element-type disagreement could hit unreachable!/panic. The finding states pre-PR behavior was equivalent and confidence is low.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Winch visit_table_fill was not updated to pass a DefinedTableIndex after the libcalls switched to one. With imported tables this caused an out-of-bounds get_defined_table panic or access to the wrong table.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated diff, Winch visit_table_fill now uses prepare_builtin_defined_table_arg, so the GT chain is fixed. The scanner reports a different, hypothetical problem: a mismatch between the declared element type and the runtime element type that would reach unreachable!(). It never says Winch passes a TableIndex where a DefinedTableIndex is expected. It also states that the compiler passes the correct pair and labels its own issue low-confidence.

criteria: Shift-mask predicate in amode_no_more_iconst rules 6/7 uses the memory access type instead of the ishl value type
The mismatched bit-width (e.g. i32 load, i64 index) causes a false match of ty_bytes == 1 << masked_shift
The resulting RegScaled amode encodes shift log2(ty_bytes), which differs from the CLIF shift amount
The divergence lets the address bypass bounds checks and escape the sandbox (64-bit Wasm memory)
judge.findings_summary: One finding: u64_shl can panic when the masked shift amount is >= 64 for I128-typed ishl in amode rules 6/7. It calls the masking itself correct.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Rules 6/7 masked the shift amount using the load type instead of the ishl type. This false-matched RegScaled with the wrong shift, letting the computed address diverge from CLIF semantics and escape the sandbox.
judge.reasoning: The PR passes shift_ty, the type of the ishl value, to shift_masked_imm, which removes the type confusion. The scanner explicitly calls the mask semantically correct. It instead reports a separate I128 u64_shl panic, which is a DoS from malformed CLIF. That is a different trigger and impact from the GT miscompilation and sandbox escape.

criteria: StringPool stores &'static str keys in its map via a transmute; the keys borrow from the pool's own strings field
StringPool::try_clone clones the map directly, copying the raw key pointers unchanged
The cloned map's keys still point into the original pool's strings allocation, not the clone's
Dropping the original pool, then doing a lookup or insert through the clone, reads freed memory
There is no re-interning through the new pool's insert() during the clone
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: a latent self-referential-transmute UAF hazard that acknowledges the re-interning fix, cross-pool Atom confusion, panics in Atom conversions, an expect panic in insert, and a Box<str> layout/leak concern.
judge.ground_truth_summary: StringPool::try_clone cloned the map directly, copying &'static str keys that pointed into the original pool's strings. After the original pool was dropped, lookups through the clone read freed memory.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, try_clone builds a fresh pool and re-interns every string via insert(), so the cloned map's keys point into the clone's own storage. That breaks the GT causal chain. Scanner finding 1 explicitly says the PR's TryClone was fixed by re-interning. It only describes a latent, hypothetical hazard if someone later calls map.try_clone(). The other findings cover unrelated issues.

criteria: Finding located in cow.rs MemoryImageSlot::assign_init_image protection-reset logic
Identifies wrong predicate (can_elide_bounds_check instead of can_use_virtual_memory) gating set_protection on shrink
Trigger: guard_size==0, reservation<4GiB, compiler assumes VM semantics
Consequence: stale pages left accessible, leaking prior instance memory in pooling allocator
Vulnerable predicate must be present in evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: One finding: MemoryCreatorProxy::new_memory in trampoline/memory.rs always passes Some(memory_reservation), which violates the documented MemoryCreator safety contract.
judge.ground_truth_summary: cow.rs assign_init_image used can_elide_bounds_check instead of can_use_virtual_memory, so protections were not reset on shrink and prior instance data stayed readable.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already uses ty.can_use_virtual_memory in assign_init_image, so the GT bug is fixed. The scanner's only finding is in a different file and function: MemoryCreatorProxy passing Some(memory_reservation) to custom MemoryCreator implementations. That is a different trigger, sink, and contract, so it does not match the GT.

criteria: LoadKind::derive_operand_size maps VectorExtend loads to an OperandSize smaller than 8 bytes
That undersized OperandSize flows into the Wasm linear-memory bounds check / heap access sizing
SIMD load8x8/16x4/32x2 extend loads actually read 8 bytes from memory
The mismatch lets the load read past the validated bound near the end of linear memory
judge.findings_summary: One finding: the x64 wasm_load Splat arm gates AVX2-only vpbroadcastb/w/d on has_avx() only, causing SIGILL on AVX1-only hosts.
judge.ground_truth_summary: derive_operand_size gave vector-extend loads a per-lane size (S8/S16/S32) instead of 8 bytes, undersizing the bounds check and allowing out-of-bounds reads.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, derive_operand_size maps VectorExtend(_) to OperandSize::S64, which is the correct 8-byte width. The GT undersized bounds chain is therefore absent. The scanner reports a different bug: Splat loads are gated only on AVX while emitting AVX2-only vpbroadcast instructions, causing SIGILL. That is a different trigger, sink, and guard, so it does not match the GT.

criteria: Receiver (oneshot) error branch in handle_request awaits the spawned task result
Code panics on the task result (expect_err or similar) assuming receiver error implies task error
Trigger: guest returns Ok(()) without calling response-outparam::set
Impact: host process panic/crash (DoS) driven by guest code
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reports that task.await in the receiver-error branch can hang indefinitely if the guest drops the outparam and keeps running. This is a DoS via hang, not a panic.
judge.ground_truth_summary: expect_err on the task result panics when the guest returns Ok without calling response-outparam::set. This crashes the wasmtime serve host.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR handles the Ok(Ok(())) case explicitly with bail!, so there is no expect_err panic. The GT panic chain does not exist in this code. The scanner reports a different issue, an unbounded task.await hang after the guest drops the outparam early. That is a different sink and impact, not the panic.

criteria: DRC alloc_array computes num_gc_refs for GC-ref element arrays
num_gc_refs is set to the byte size (size) rather than the element count (len)
The oversized count is packed into the GC header reserved bits via emit_gc_raw_alloc
Collector tracing uses num_gc_refs to slice outgoing edges, so it over-reads past the object's ref slots
Triggered by allocating and then collecting an array of GC refs
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: num_gc_refs=len overflows the reserved kind bits, causing a panic or truncation. Finding 2: array_new_data retry passes byte_len as the element count, leaving elements uninitialized.
judge.ground_truth_summary: DRC alloc_array passed the array byte size instead of the element count as num_gc_refs. Tracing then over-reads past the array's GC-ref slots and dec-refs arbitrary heap data.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, num_gc_refs = len, not size, so the GT size-vs-len bug is fixed. Finding 1 is a different issue: a large len overflows the 27 reserved bits, causing a panic or under-tracing, which is the opposite of the GT over-read. Finding 2 concerns array_new_data. Neither finding matches the GT chain, and the code shows the fix.

criteria: Const-expr evaluation gains a new fallible GC allocation path (struct.new/struct.new_default via StructRef::_new)
Module-supplied global initializer can trigger the allocation failure
Caller (initialize_vmctx_globals) unconditionally expects/unwraps the eval result
Panic occurs instead of propagating the allocation error to the embedder
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reports a DRC refcount UAF from the non-owning raw returned by _to_raw, a refcount leak from global.get fields, and an element-segment ownership mismatch. It reports no unchecked expect or panic.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A new fallible GC struct allocation in const-expr eval reaches initialize_vmctx_globals' unconditional expect(), causing a panic instead of returning an error. This PR already propagates the error with ?.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff changes initialize_vmctx_globals to return Result and replaces the .expect() with ?, so the GT panic chain is fixed. The scanner reports no unchecked-expect or panic problem. Its findings cover other issues: refcount ownership causing a use-after-free, a refcount leak, and element-segment ownership. These are adjacent bugs, not the GT root cause.

criteria: compute() receives Vec<NamedTensor> holding Resource<Tensor> handles by value
Tensors are fetched via non-consuming table.get instead of table.delete
Consumed handles are never removed from the ResourceTable
Each compute() call leaks table entries, giving unbounded memory growth
Location: crates/wasi-nn/src/wit.rs HostGraphExecutionContext::compute
judge.findings_summary: Six findings on backend input validation: PyTorch/OpenVINO length mismatches, ONNX chunk/unimplemented panics, WinML unimplemented panic and a no-op alignment check. None covers resource-table leaks.
judge.ground_truth_summary: wit.rs compute() takes tensor resources by value but uses table.get rather than delete, leaking ResourceTable entries on every call. The fix is already applied in this benign snapshot.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already uses inputs.into_iter() with self.table.delete(tensor_resopurce), so tensor handles are removed from the table and the leak chain is broken. No scanner finding addresses resource-table cleanup in wit.rs compute(). All findings are adjacent backend panics or data-validation issues, such as length mismatch, unimplemented types, and alignment.

criteria: Reverse PC-to-FuncKey lookup in CompiledFunctionsTable::func_by_text_offset for sparse namespaces
Sparse index computed as a namespace-local offset (index - func_loc_start)
Missing addition of the per-namespace base sparse_starts[ns_idx] before indexing the shared sparse_indices map
Consequence: wrong FuncKey or out-of-range index/panic for sparse namespaces that do not start at 0
Vulnerable code must still be present in the evaluated snapshot
judge.findings_summary: Scanner reports that CompiledModule::func_by_text_offset resolves functions of other static modules through the shared component table, causing a debug_assert panic or wrong profiler names.
judge.ground_truth_summary: func_by_text_offset uses a namespace-local sparse offset as an absolute SparseIndex without adding sparse_starts[ns_idx]. This yields a wrong FuncKey or a panic for sparse namespaces after the first.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already adds sparse_start to sparse_offset and debug-asserts that the result is within the namespace range, so the GT bug is fixed. The scanner reports a different issue: cross-module resolution in CompiledModule::func_by_text_offset that affects profiling. It does not mention the missing sparse base offset. The GT chain is absent and the finding does not match it.

criteria: A matching .netrc 'default' stanza with neither login nor password still makes parsenetrc() return NETRC_SUCCESS
The out: fixup only substitutes a blank password when our_login is set, and never excludes the no-login/no-password default case
override_login() treats NETRC_SUCCESS as trusted netrc credentials and sets conn->bits.netrc = TRUE
bits.netrc makes the HTTP auth logic (Curl_auth_allowed_to_host) resend credentials after a redirect to a different host
Impact is leakage of the first host's credentials to an unrelated host
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: a NULL dereference in str_has_ctrl when netrc success has missing login/password, missing our_login and keyword resets on machine/default, unconditional password storage, and an empty URL username treated as a specific login.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A netrc 'default' entry without login or password still yields NETRC_SUCCESS. That sets bits.netrc, which allows credentials to be resent on a redirect to a different host, leaking them.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 shares the trigger: parsenetrc() returns success with NULL or no credentials, including for 'default'. Its sink is different, though: a NULL dereference in str_has_ctrl() causing a crash. No finding links the empty success to conn->bits.netrc or to resending credentials across a redirect to another host. The other findings describe adjacent state-reset and password-selection bugs. This is a near match with the same trigger but a different sink.

criteria: LDAP TLS options (REQUIRE_CERT / CACERTFILE) are set via ldap_set_option with a NULL handle
The NULL handle targets the process-global LDAP option context, not a per-connection handle
The options are set before ldap_init(), so no per-session handle exists yet
Concurrent transfers or threads can observe or race on the weakened global TLS verification setting
Evaluated PR code still contains these NULL-handle TLS option calls with no per-handle setting or locking
judge.findings_summary: Five findings. A Windows NULL check is missing, verification is hardcoded off, and global NULL-handle TLS options race across threads (the GT match). Two build and include issues are also reported.
judge.ground_truth_summary: OpenLDAP TLS options are set through a NULL (global) handle before ldap_init(). Concurrent ldap transfers race on the shared settings and can inherit disabled certificate verification.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 matches the GT root cause. It names ldap_set_option(NULL, LDAP_OPT_X_TLS_REQUIRE_CERT/CACERTFILE), plus the timeout and protocol calls, as writes to global state made before ldap_init(). It describes the unsynchronized data race and the cross-thread weakening of verification, and gives the correct fix of setting options on the per-session handle. The PR diff adds exactly these calls with no lock and no per-handle use.

criteria: Location is the wolfSSL branch of Curl_vquic_tls_verify_peer in lib/vquic/vquic-tls.c
The guard changed from fail-closed (!peer->sni || check fails) to fail-open (peer->sni && check fails)
The trigger is peer->sni being NULL, as with IP-literal targets
When SNI is missing, the host/cert identity check is skipped and the function returns CURLE_OK
Impact is that QUIC/HTTP3 wolfSSL connections accept any server identity, enabling MITM
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 identifies the inverted !peer->sni|| to peer->sni&& guard causing fail-open verification for IP-literal hosts. Finding 2 reports the post-handshake domain check as a no-op. Finding 3 is an unrelated rustls dead-code issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The wolfSSL QUIC verify_peer guard was inverted, so a NULL SNI (IP-literal hosts) skips certificate/hostname verification. The function returns CURLE_OK, allowing MITM on HTTP/3 connections.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the same function and identifies the inverted SNI guard as the root cause. The trigger is the same: NULL sni for IP literals. It describes the same fail-open return of CURLE_OK and the same MITM impact. The PR diff shows the vulnerable condition is introduced and nothing else in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Source is sanitize_cookie_path() handling a cookie path of exactly "/"
Trailing-slash strip decrements len to 0 for the lone leading '/'
Curl_memdup0(cookie_path, len) allocates exactly len+1 (1 byte), unlike old strdup-sized buffer
Sink is replace_existing()'s strchr(clist->spath + 1, '/') reading past the 1-byte allocation
Reached via secure cookie with path "/" followed by same-name non-secure cookie from insecure origin
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a heap OOB read in replace_existing caused by the 1-byte spath for path "/" after the sanitize_cookie_path rewrite. Three other findings cover parsing logic regressions.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactored sanitize_cookie_path strips the lone '/' and uses Curl_memdup0(len=0), giving a 1-byte spath. replace_existing's strchr(spath+1) then reads out of bounds.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain. It names sanitize_cookie_path() stripping the lone '/' and Curl_memdup0 then allocating 1 byte, in contrast to the old strdup's 2 bytes. It identifies the sink as strchr(clist->spath+1) in replace_existing and gives the secure/insecure overlay trigger. The PR diff shows this new allocation with no guard. No fix appears.

criteria: Trigger: the remote peer keeps sending PING frames while not reading from the connection, and auto-PONG is enabled.
Incorrect guard: ws_enc_add_cntrl only checks ws->enc.payload_remain==0, not whether earlier bytes in ws->sendbuf were actually transmitted.
Sink: every PING appends a new encoded PONG frame to ws->sendbuf.
ws->sendbuf uses BUFQ_OPT_SOFT_LIMIT, so writes never fail on capacity and the buffer grows without bound.
Impact: unbounded memory growth leading to memory exhaustion (DoS).
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: a sendbuf_payload underflow causing an OOB read in ws_enc_send, a non-atomic failure path in ws_enc_add_pending that truncates the PONG, and pending state not reset in Curl_ws_accept.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Auto-PONG appends to a soft-limit sendbuf whenever payload_remain==0, without checking that prior bytes were sent. A peer that sends PINGs but never reads causes unbounded memory growth.
judge.reasoning: The PR code supports the GT chain: an eager PONG append guarded only by payload_remain, into a soft-limit sendbuf. No finding describes unbounded sendbuf growth or memory exhaustion. Finding 1 covers stale sendbuf_payload causing an underflow and out-of-bounds read. Finding 2 covers a non-atomic header/payload write that leaves a truncated frame, a different sink. Finding 3 covers stale state on re-accept. These are adjacent issues in the same code, not the GT.

criteria: Vulnerable function is url_match_auth_nego in lib/url.c (the Negotiate analogue of url_match_auth_ntlm)
Guard checks NTLM flags (want_ntlm_http/want_proxy_ntlm_http) instead of Negotiate flags
As a result, the block that sets m->found, sets m->force_reuse, and returns FALSE to keep searching is unreachable for Negotiate requests
The function then falls through to return TRUE for any Negotiate connection that passes the credential check, bypassing the negotiation-state selection
Impact: wrong connection reuse, including a connection already authenticated with another Negotiate/Kerberos context
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError at lib/url.c:1226 in url_match_auth_nego. The Negotiate force-reuse block is gated on NTLM flags, making it dead code. The function always returns TRUE, causing wrong reuse of Negotiate connections.
judge.ground_truth_summary: url_match_auth_nego checks the NTLM want-flags instead of the Negotiate flags. The block that enforces selection of fully negotiated connections never runs, so Negotiate connections can be wrongly reused across users or credentials.
judge.reasoning: The scanner flags the same copy-paste guard in url_match_auth_nego: NTLM flags are checked instead of Negotiate flags. It shows the found/force_reuse/keep-searching block is dead code, so the function returns TRUE regardless of Negotiate state and the wrong connection can be reused. The PR diff contains this bug and nothing in it mitigates the problem.

criteria: smb_parse_url_path sets req->path to a pointer inside connection-owned smbc->share instead of a private copy
Lifetime mismatch: req->path has request/easy-handle lifetime, but smbc->share has connection lifetime
The connection, and its share via the conn dtor/disconnect, is freed while the smb_request still holds req->path
req->path is later dereferenced (tree-connect/open message building, easy dtor), causing a use-after-free read
The finding asserts an active UAF, not a latent or hypothetical one
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports req->path pointing into connection-owned share memory, framed as a leak plus latent dangling pointer and explicitly not a live UAF. Finding 2 reports a stale share on connection reuse (wrong resource accessed).
judge.ground_truth_summary: req->path is set into the middle of connection-owned smbc->share. When the connection is freed before the easy handle, req->path dangles, and later accesses in tree-connect, open or the easy dtor read freed heap memory.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT root cause: req->path borrows connection-owned share memory, and it proposes a strdup fix. However, it explicitly says this is 'currently a latent dangling-pointer hazard plus a leak rather than a live UAF'. It frames the UAF as arising only after 'any future code change'. That contradicts the GT's active UAF, so strict rules require false. Finding 2 is a different stale-share logic bug.

criteria: Location is the NTLM connection-reuse fallback for mismatched credentials (url_match_auth_ntlm / ConnectionExists in lib/url.c)
The only guard is http_ntlm_state == NTLMSTATE_NONE
There is no check that http_negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE
A connection already authenticated with Negotiate/SPNEGO keeps NTLM state NONE, so it passes the guard
A request with different credentials reuses that connection and runs under the previous user's identity
judge.findings_summary: Four LogicError findings on the new NTLM reuse fallback: an HTTP/2 mid-handshake race, a proxy-NTLM check bypass, the missing Negotiate state check (finding 3), and chosen overwriting a better match.
judge.ground_truth_summary: url_match_auth_ntlm lets an NTLM-wanting request with mismatched credentials reuse a connection when http_ntlm_state is NONE. It does not check http_negotiate_state, so Negotiate-authenticated connections get reused by another user.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 matches the GT root cause. The PR adds a fallback that sets chosen = check whenever http_ntlm_state is NONE, with no Negotiate state check. A Negotiate-authenticated connection never touches NTLM state, so it is reused for a different user's credentials and the request runs as the old user. The PR diff shows this chain is active and adds no mitigation.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: In Curl_auth_gsasl_is_supported, a gsasl_client_start() failure triggers gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx).
gsasl->ctx is not set to NULL after that free, so the persistent struct keeps a stale pointer.
Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup later calls gsasl_done(gsasl->ctx) with no already-freed check.
The result is an actual double free of the same GSASL context, presented as an active, reachable defect.
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: challenge-buffer leak, gsasl ctx/session leak on mechanism fallback, dangling ctx after gsasl_done (called latent), undeclared 'result', undeclared 'serverdata', and unchecked strdup/base64 results.
judge.ground_truth_summary: When gsasl_client_start fails, Curl_auth_gsasl_is_supported calls gsasl_done(ctx) but leaves ctx non-NULL. Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup later calls gsasl_done on the same pointer again: a double free.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 names the exact location: gsasl_done on client_start failure without nulling ctx, with a possible double free via Curl_auth_gsasl_cleanup. But it calls this a 'latent UAF rather than an immediately reachable one'. It says the stale pointer is overwritten by the SHA-1 probe and the risk comes only from future guards. That is the excluded hypothetical/future-risk framing, not an asserted active double free.

criteria: Location is the CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD handler in Curl_vsetopt (lib/setopt.c)
Trigger is passing NULL (the conventional clear signal), which leaves the temporaries u/p NULL
Free/overwrite of the stored proxy username/password is gated behind the 'if(!result && u)' / 'if(!result && p)' guards
Consequence: old STRING_PROXYUSERNAME/PROXYPASSWORD values are not cleared and persist across easy-handle reuse
Impact: stale credentials are sent to later proxies (credential leak)
judge.findings_summary: Two findings. One is a memory leak because Curl_urldecode overwrites without freeing. The other is that a NULL or colon-less CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD no longer clears stale proxy credentials because of the u/p non-NULL guards.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactored CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD handler only frees and sets the proxy user and password when the parsed u/p are non-NULL. Passing NULL therefore fails to clear the old proxy credentials, which then leak to later transfers.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT exactly. It names the NULL input to CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD, the u/p temporaries, the non-NULL guards that skip clearing, the retained STRING_PROXYUSERNAME/PASSWORD values, and stale credentials sent to a new proxy. The PR diff shows these guards are present and nothing in the PR clears the old values. Finding 1, a memory leak, is an adjacent issue and does not affect the verdict.

criteria: The trigger is the application setting CURLOPT_REFERER to NULL after a referer was previously set on a reused handle.
The refactor removed the unconditional Curl_bufref_set in setopt.c CURLOPT_REFERER handling.
Curl_pretransfer only updates state.referer when STRING_SET_REFERER is non-NULL and has no else branch to clear it.
The stale state.referer is reused as the Referer header on a later request, leaking the old referer.
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: clearing CURLOPT_REFERER leaves state.referer stale or dangling because Curl_pretransfer guards are skipped, so the old Referer is sent (framed as UAF). Finding 2: a stale auto-referer persists when AUTOREFERER is disabled.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Moving the referer bufref update into Curl_pretransfer guarded by a non-NULL check omitted clearing it when CURLOPT_REFERER is set to NULL. The previous referer stays cached and is sent on later requests.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain. CURLOPT_REFERER is set to NULL with autoreferer off, both guards in Curl_pretransfer are skipped, state.referer is never cleared, and the stale value is emitted as the Referer header. The finding labels it UAF because the bufref is non-owning, but the trigger, missing else-clear, and sink are identical to the GT. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code and adds no fix.

criteria: mqtt_doing captures mq->sendleftovers in a local pointer and frees it after the retry mqtt_send
mqtt_send hits an allocation failure (Curl_memdup OOM) and returns an error without updating mq->sendleftovers
mq->sendleftovers is left dangling and still owns the freed pointer
the newly added mqtt_done frees mq->sendleftovers again, causing a double free
the PR does not detach or clear the remainder before the retry
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings: a NULL dereference in mqtt_done, the GT double free on OOM in the leftover resend (findings 2 and 6), an OOB read when Curl_write fails, and a leak from leftovers being overwritten.
judge.ground_truth_summary: mqtt_doing frees a captured sendleftovers pointer after the retry mqtt_send fails on allocation, while mq->sendleftovers still holds it. The new mqtt_done then frees the same pointer again.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the exact GT chain. On the leftover resend in mqtt_doing, Curl_memdup fails and mqtt_send returns OOM without touching mq->sendleftovers. mqtt_doing then frees ptr, which leaves sendleftovers dangling. The new mqtt_done frees it a second time. The PR diff adds mqtt_done but has no detach or clear step before the retry, so the bug is present.

criteria: Trigger is the new write_paused state making cf_h2_update_local_win shrink the HTTP/2 stream receive window to zero
On unpause (http2_data_pause or h2_xfer_write_resp), the updater calls nghttp2_submit_window_update without first setting nghttp2's local window size
Consequence: a stream whose window reached zero cannot restore its receive window and stays blocked/stalled
Location is lib/http2.c cf_h2_update_local_win / http2_data_pause
judge.findings_summary: Four cw-pause.c issues: unbounded pause buffer causing HTTP/3 DoS, premature or duplicated EOS on partial flush, swallowed EOS write error, and a zero-length bufq DEBUGASSERT. None concerns HTTP/2 window restoration.
judge.ground_truth_summary: write_paused shrinks the HTTP/2 receive window to zero. On unpause, cf_h2_update_local_win submits a WINDOW_UPDATE without setting nghttp2's local window size, so the stream can remain blocked.
judge.reasoning: All four scanner findings target lib/cw-pause.c: unbounded buffering affecting HTTP/3, premature EOS during flush, a swallowed EOS write error, and a zero-size bufq assert. Finding 1 mentions the h2 window shrink only as a mitigation that bounds memory. None identifies the missing nghttp2 local-window setter on unpause or the resulting stuck HTTP/2 stream. The GT bug is still present in the PR code, but the scanner does not cover it.

criteria: Trigger: PEM body between BEGIN/END PUBLIC KEY markers is empty or only '\n'/'\r' characters
Lazily allocated dynbuf (pbuf) never has Curl_dyn_addn called, so its internal buffer stays NULL
Curl_dyn_ptr(&pbuf) returns NULL with no NULL/empty check before use
NULL passed to Curl_base64_decode, which dereferences it (strlen) in pubkey_pem_to_der, lib/vtls/vtls.c ~988
Regression from the fixed malloc(+1) NUL-terminated buffer to dynbuf in this PR
judge.findings_summary: One NullPointerDereference finding in pubkey_pem_to_der at vtls.c:988. An empty or whitespace-only PEM body leaves the dynbuf unallocated, so Curl_dyn_ptr returns NULL and Curl_base64_decode calls strlen(NULL). Reachable via CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The dynbuf conversion of pubkey_pem_to_der lets Curl_dyn_ptr return NULL when no bytes are appended (empty or newline-only PEM body). The NULL pointer is passed unchecked to Curl_base64_decode and dereferenced.
judge.reasoning: The scanner identifies the same trigger (an empty or newline-only PEM body), the same state (dynbuf never allocated), the same missing guard (no NULL check on Curl_dyn_ptr), and the same sink (strlen in Curl_base64_decode). Location and function also match. The PR diff confirms the unconditional Curl_dyn_ptr call with no fallback. Nothing in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Buffer obtained from curl's overridable/tracked allocator (Curl_base64_decode) in init_config_builder_ech
Buffer released with raw libc free() in the cleanup path
Root cause: rustls.c lacks curl_memory.h/memdebug.h, so free() is not redirected to curl's matching deallocator
Consequence: allocator/deallocator mismatch causing invalid free under memory overrides or memdebug builds
