No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Lookup indices come from HarfBuzz via hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups/hb_set_next
Each index is used directly to subscript globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[]
No check of the index against the array's allocated length (lookupCount)
The out-of-bounds offset is then passed to af_map_lookup, which reads from gsub+offset
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: coverage iterator wrap at glyph 0xFFFF, unbounded recursion in add_substitute, uninitialized gsub_lookup_count on the parse-fail path, two NULL dereferences, and an Offset32 pointer wrap on 32-bit builds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: HarfBuzz-collected GSUB lookup indices index gsub_lookups_single_alternate[] without a bounds check against lookupCount, causing an out-of-bounds heap read that also feeds af_map_lookup.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds gsub_lookup_count, sets it in af_parse_gsub, and checks idx < gsub_lookup_count in both the trace loop and the main loop. That breaks the GT chain. Finding 3 calls this check the fix and reports a different issue: the count may be uninitialized when GSUB parsing fails. That is a different root cause, so the GT vulnerability is not detected.

criteria: Pool-size computation for peak_coords omits the sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier
The other four sub-buffers correctly include sizeof, so only peak_coords is undersized
Writes over 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values to peak_coords/im_start/im_end overflow into adjacent pool memory or past the heap block
Trigger is a crafted variable font gvar table applied in TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas
judge.findings_summary: One finding: FT_UInt integer overflow/wrap in the gvar pool_size computation that could undersize the allocation, mainly on 16-bit int platforms. It also flags the lost FT_NEW_ARRAY overflow guards.
judge.ground_truth_summary: peak_coords_size omitted the sizeof(FT_Fixed) factor in the shared gvar pool, undersizing it about 4x and causing a heap overflow when peak/intermediate coords are written.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, peak_coords_size already includes sizeof(*peak_coords), so the GT undersizing is fixed. The scanner instead reports FT_UInt integer wrap in the pool-size arithmetic, mainly on 16-bit configurations, and admits it is not practical on 32/64-bit. That is a different root cause and a speculative concern, not the missing-sizeof bug.

criteria: Untrusted PKCS#12 PBMAC1 PBKDF2 params parsed in PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC (p12_mutl.c)
keylength used without existence/bounds check (<=EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE)
PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC writes keylen bytes into fixed key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] stack buffer in pkcs12_gen_mac
salt accessed as octet_string without verifying ASN.1 type in library path
Missing validation present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: (1) NULL dereference on non-OCTET-STRING salt in the apps/pkcs12.c -info printer; (2) PBMAC1 PBKDF2 ignores the libctx/propq. Neither reports a keylength buffer overflow.
judge.ground_truth_summary: An unvalidated PBKDF2 keylength in PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC overflows the stack buffer key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] in pkcs12_gen_mac. A missing salt type check also allows an invalid dereference. Both are fixed in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR already validates salt type and requires 0<keylen<=EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE, so the GT chain is broken. Finding 1 is a different sink: apps/pkcs12.c, the CLI info printer, with a NULL dereference. It explicitly says the library path correctly rejects bad salt. Finding 2 is a libctx/FIPS logic issue. Neither finding reports an active keylength stack overflow.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled IV OCTET STRING length in ASN.1 AEAD (GCMParameters) params during CMS decrypt
Sink: copy of IV into fixed stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH] in evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params
Missing guard: no upper-bound check i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH before/at copy (two-step length query then copy with unchecked length)
Evaluated code must still lack this bound (copy size not capped)
judge.findings_summary: Eight findings: GCM tag length ignored, authAttrs ASN.1 tags, missing AAD, NULL derefs, uninitialized IV, encrypt-side ivlen overflow, and a generic helper memcpy concern. None reports an active decrypt IV stack overflow.
judge.ground_truth_summary: evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params copies an attacker-controlled IV length into the stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH] after checking only i<=0, causing a stack overflow when parsing CMS AuthEnvelopedData.
judge.reasoning: The PR code passes EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH as the max copy length and checks `i > EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH`, so the GT overflow is fixed. No finding reports an active decrypt-side IV overflow. Finding 7 covers an encrypt-side ivlen issue in cms_enc.c, which is a different trigger. Finding 8 covers a generic helper concern and says the CMS caller is safe. Finding 1 is about tag length. Nothing matches the GT chain.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Input to one-shot signing/verification is buffered via a size-limited read helper (bio_to_mem, 16MB cap)
When the cap is reached, the helper stops reading and returns success with partial data instead of an error
The caller accepts that partial buffer as success, e.g. only checking for buflen <= 0
Signing or verification therefore runs on truncated data, leaving trailing bytes unauthenticated
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: uninitialized BUF_MEM if BIO_get_mem_ptr fails, print_out size_t-to-int cast and ignored BIO_write result, and a 4KB allocation overshoot past maxlen before the error return. None reports silent truncation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bio_to_mem silently stopped reading at the 16MB limit and returned success, so dgst one-shot signing (Ed25519/Ed448/ML-DSA) covered only the first 16MB. The trailing data was left unauthenticated.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, bio_to_mem returns 0 when sz exceeds a non-zero maxlen, and do_fp_oneshot_sign treats that as a read error. Oversized input is now rejected, so the silent-truncation chain is broken. Scanner finding 3 discusses the maxlen check but says it is a bounded allocation overshoot, explicitly 'not a returned-data truncation'. The other findings cover an unchecked BIO_get_mem_ptr call and print_out write failures, which are unrelated.

criteria: In x509_main, the OPT_ADDREJECT handler pushes the parsed object onto the wrong stack ('trust' instead of 'reject')
The cause is a copy-paste error from the OPT_ADDTRUST case during the sk_*_push return-check refactor
As a result, -addreject marks the certificate as trusted for that purpose, inverting the intended security policy
The evaluated code must still contain sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(trust, objtmp) inside the OPT_ADDREJECT case
judge.findings_summary: Four findings, all memory or reference leaks on new push-failure paths (crl2pkcs7, e_capi, engine, x509 objtmp). None addresses the reject entry being pushed onto the trust stack.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A copy-paste error made the -addreject handler in apps/x509.c push to the trust stack instead of the reject stack, so rejected purposes became trusted. The evaluated PR already uses the reject stack.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the OPT_ADDREJECT case calls sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(reject, objtmp), which is the correct stack, so the GT causal chain is not present. The only finding in apps/x509.c (finding 4) describes an ASN1_OBJECT memory leak when the push fails. That is an adjacent bug in the same function, not the wrong-stack trust inversion. No finding identifies the GT root cause.

criteria: Trigger: hardware-accelerated ctx->stream path taken with len not a multiple of 16
Stream path processes full blocks but does not advance in/out pointers
Tail-handling code uses bare in/out pointers, assuming they were already advanced
Result: partial tail is read/written at buffer start, so real trailing bytes are left unencrypted/unauthenticated
Affects both CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt and CRYPTO_ocb128_decrypt
judge.findings_summary: One finding: in-place OCB encryption of a partial last block XORs ciphertext into the checksum instead of plaintext, giving a wrong tag. Fail-closed. Different trigger and root cause from the GT.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The OCB ctx->stream path does not advance in/out pointers, while tail handling assumes they were advanced. Trailing 1-15 bytes are processed at the wrong offset and left unencrypted/unauthenticated. Fixed in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds pointer advancement (in/out += num_blocks*16) in both stream branches, which breaks the GT chain. The scanner reports a different bug in the same function: in-place partial-block encryption computes the checksum from ciphertext. That finding involves a different trigger (in==out aliasing), a different flaw (wrong checksum order), and fails closed. It never mentions the stream path or missing pointer advancement.

criteria: bmp_to_utf8 passes remaining UTF-16 source length as UTF8_putc destination capacity
UTF8_putc returns -1 for 3-byte BMP char when only 2 source bytes remain
OPENSSL_uni2utf8 second (writing) pass does not check negative return
Negative j added to asclen makes it negative
NUL write at asctmp[asclen] writes before the heap buffer
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings. #1 flags len-as-capacity confusion in bmp_to_utf8 causing a spurious NULL return. Others cover negative lengths, a password leak, utf82uni loop checks, surrogate handling and overflow.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bmp_to_utf8 misuses source length as UTF8_putc capacity, returning -1. The unchecked second pass of OPENSSL_uni2utf8 makes asclen negative, so the NUL terminator is written before the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: In the PR code, the second loop in OPENSSL_uni2utf8 checks `if (j < 0)`, then frees the buffer and returns NULL. That breaks the chain to the negative-index write. Finding 1 does flag the len/capacity confusion, but it says the outcome is a NULL return (fail-closed), not heap corruption. So it describes the fixed state, not the GT overflow. Other findings cover unrelated bugs.

criteria: Attacker-controlled signed attribute (signingCertificate / signingCertificateV2) is retrieved as an ASN1_TYPE from SignerInfo
Code reads attr->value.sequence without checking attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE
A non-SEQUENCE attribute type causes type confusion, leading to an invalid or NULL pointer dereference (DoS)
Affects ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get, reached from timestamp response verification
The missing type check is present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: CAdES attribute added after signing, unchecked i2d length, unchecked X509_digest, CAdES attribute never verified, NULL hash_alg dereference, CADES|NOATTR. None concern ASN1_TYPE type confusion.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ESS_SIGNING_CERT(_V2)_get reads attr->value.sequence without validating that attr->type is V_ASN1_SEQUENCE. A malformed TS response then causes type confusion and a crash. The evaluated PR already includes the fix.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get both check attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE before reading the union member, so the GT causal chain is broken. None of the scanner findings mention the missing union type check in these getters. The findings instead cover CAdES signing order, i2d length checks, an unchecked X509_digest, missing verification, a NULL hash_alg, and NOATTR handling.

criteria: Vulnerability is in kek_unwrap_key in crypto/cms/cms_pwri.c
Length check against tmp[0] is incorrect (inverted, or underflows as tmp[0]-4)
Incorrect check lets memcpy(out, tmp+4, tmp[0]) read past tmp and write past out
Attacker controls tmp[0] via crafted CMS PWRI encryptedKey
Evaluated code must still contain the flawed check (inlen < tmp[0]-4)
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: NULL derefs on keyDerivationAlgorithm and ec, a short-input check-byte OOB read in kek_unwrap_key, a double-free of the password, and a kek_wrap_key header OOB read. None cover the tmp[0] memcpy bounds check.
judge.ground_truth_summary: kek_unwrap_key's check `inlen < tmp[0]-4` is wrong and can underflow, allowing memcpy of tmp[0] bytes to read and write out of bounds. Fixed here as `inlen < 4 + tmp[0]`.
judge.reasoning: The PR code uses the corrected check `inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0]`, so the GT causal chain is broken. Scanner finding 2 does target kek_unwrap_key, but it describes a different trigger and sink: short input with blocklen 1, leading to tmp[4..6] check-byte reads. It does not identify the tmp[0] length-check flaw or the memcpy overflow. No finding matches the GT.

criteria: Server host enclosed in brackets is copied into a stack buffer 'host' via strncpy of exactly sl bytes
No NUL terminator is written after the strncpy copy
The unterminated 'host' is then used as a C string (strstr(no_proxy, server)), reading past buffer bounds
Out-of-bounds read originates in the 'host' buffer, not in the no_proxy haystack
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: an empty-'[]' host causing an empty strstr needle, an infinite loop and an over-read past no_proxy; and bracketed no_proxy IPv6 entries no longer matching, allowing proxy bypass.
judge.ground_truth_summary: use_proxy strips IPv6 brackets with strncpy(host, server+1, sl) without NUL-terminating host. A later strstr(no_proxy, host) reads beyond the host buffer (out-of-bounds read, DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR writes host[sl] = '\0' right after strncpy, which breaks the GT chain. Finding 1 describes a different trigger (an empty '[]' host producing an empty strstr needle) and a different over-read location (past the end of no_proxy). It does not report the missing terminator. Finding 2 is a no_proxy matching logic regression. Neither finding matches the GT root cause.

criteria: Partial first-block pre-processing path in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc/dec
vmovdqu8 loads of iv (%r11) and input ($inp) lack the {%k1}{z} mask
Unmasked loads read a full 16 bytes when only $left (1-15) bytes are valid
Over-read past the buffer end can cross into an unmapped page, causing a crash/DoS
judge.findings_summary: One finding: ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_eligible omits the AVX512VL check, so EVEX xmm instructions may raise #UD and crash the process.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unmasked vmovdqu8 loads in CFB partial-block pre-processing read 16 bytes regardless of valid length, an out-of-bounds read causing DoS at page boundaries.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the pre-processing loads in both enc and dec already use {%k1}{z} masks, so the GT over-read is fixed. The scanner's only finding concerns a missing AVX512VL check in the eligibility function, which could cause #UD. That is a different root cause, sink and guard, not the unmasked-load OOB read.

criteria: Trigger is a crafted delta CRL that has the Delta CRL Indicator (base_crl_number) but lacks the CRL Number extension (crl_number)
check_delta_base reaches ASN1_INTEGER_cmp(delta->crl_number, base->crl_number)
No NULL check on delta->crl_number before that comparison
Crash (NULL dereference) on the X509_V_FLAG_USE_DELTAS verification path
The missing guard must still be absent in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Ten LogicError findings on CRL/delta handling: break vs continue, the lastpos=0 search, delta-as-base, expired deltas, the IGNORE_CRITICAL path, infinite loop risk, and missed store deltas. None reports a NULL dereference of delta->crl_number.
judge.ground_truth_summary: check_delta_base passes delta->crl_number to ASN1_INTEGER_cmp without a NULL check. A delta CRL that has base_crl_number but no CRL Number extension causes a NULL dereference. The PR fixes this.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds `if (delta->crl_number == NULL) return 0;` before ASN1_INTEGER_cmp in check_delta_base, which breaks the GT causal chain. No scanner finding reports a NULL dereference of delta->crl_number. Finding 8 (a delta accepted as base) is in the same function but is a different logic bug. Finding 7 concerns ignored decode errors, an adjacent issue. Neither is the GT bug.

criteria: Source: CMS KeyAgreeRecipientInfo keyEncryptionAlgorithm whose optional parameters field is absent, so alg->parameter is NULL
Sink: direct dereference of alg->parameter->type or ->value in dh/ecdh_cms_set_shared_info
Missing guard: no NULL check on alg->parameter before the dereference
Reachable via CMS_decrypt on untrusted input, causing a crash (DoS)
Evaluated code must still dereference alg->parameter directly
judge.findings_summary: 11 findings: uninitialized public_key and dukmlen, AUTOARGLEN overflow, inverted parameter check, NPDs on DHparams_dup, malloc and kdf_md, pkey_dh_copy bugs, no peer key validation, fail-open derive, negative UKM length. None covers the alg->parameter NULL dereference.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The DH/ECDH CMS set_shared_info functions dereference alg->parameter without a NULL check. The optional parameters field can be absent in a crafted KeyAgreeRecipientInfo, which crashes CMS_decrypt (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR's dh_cms_set_shared_info and ecdh_cms_set_shared_info read the parameter through X509_ALGOR_get0. That call reports an absent parameter as atype V_ASN1_UNDEF, and the code then fails the check atype != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE, so the NULL dereference is gone. No scanner finding reports dereferencing a NULL alg->parameter. The NPD findings it does make concern a different trigger and sink: a failed DHparams_dup, an unchecked malloc, and a NULL kdf_md.

criteria: Allocation size for hex output is computed as buflen*3 or 1+buflen*2 in openssl_buf2hexstr_sep
No overflow check before the multiplication, so size_t wraps on 32-bit platforms
OPENSSL_malloc allocates the undersized wrapped length
buf2hexstr_sep then writes the full hex expansion past the allocation (heap overflow)
Code path is reachable with large attacker-controlled input such as an X.509 SKID/AKID OCTET STRING
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: a write before the buffer when buflen is 0, an EBCDIC off-by-one length, and an unsigned long truncation in the str_n check on Win64. None covers the unchecked multiplication feeding malloc.
judge.ground_truth_summary: openssl_buf2hexstr_sep computes buflen*3 or 1+buflen*2 without an overflow check. On 32-bit platforms this wraps, so malloc allocates an undersized buffer and the hex conversion overflows the heap.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds SIZE_MAX/3 and (SIZE_MAX-1)/2 guards in both openssl_buf2hexstr_sep and buf2hexstr_sep, which breaks the GT chain. Finding 3 is an adjacent integer issue: an unsigned long truncation in a caller-supplied-buffer check on Win64. It even states that the allocating wrapper is safe, which contradicts the GT sink. Findings 1 and 2 cover a zero-length underflow and an EBCDIC off-by-one, so neither matches the GT.

criteria: Fires in port_default_packet_handler when validate_addr==0, after qrx_src=qrx; qrx=NULL already ran
Trigger: an Initial packet carrying a token for which port_validate_token fails
Second qrx_src=qrx reassignment runs without a qrx!=NULL guard, overwriting the saved qrx_src with NULL
Salvage loop then calls ossl_qrx_read_pkt(qrx_src==NULL), a NULL dereference that crashes the server
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: UAF because an injected RXE keeps its pkt->qrx pointer to the freed qrx_src. Finding 2: NULL deref when port_bind_channel gets qrx=NULL on the tserver dummy-channel path.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A second, unguarded qrx_src=qrx in the token-failure path, with validate_addr==0, nulls the saved QRX. ossl_qrx_read_pkt(NULL) then crashes the server, triggered remotely by an Initial packet with an invalid token.
judge.reasoning: The PR guards the second reassignment with 'if (qrx != NULL)', so qrx_src keeps the saved QRX and the GT chain is broken. Neither scanner finding matches it. Finding 1 is a UAF from packets being injected into another QRX. Finding 2 is a NULL deref in port_bind_channel on the tserver path, a different sink and trigger, and it admits the path is not reachable today.

criteria: CMS ktri decrypt (cms_RecipientInfo_ktri_decrypt) or PKCS7 pkcs7_decrypt_rinfo explicitly sets rsa_pkcs1_implicit_rejection=0 for RSA recipient keys
Disabling happens inside the CMS/PKCS7 recipient-info decryption path, not via a generic API or engine flag
Result: distinguishable RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decrypt success vs. failure reaches CMS_decrypt/PKCS7_decrypt callers, creating a Bleichenbacher oracle
Root cause is CMS/PKCS7 control flow relying on decrypt success to match recipients, instead of keeping implicit rejection on
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: a public RSA_PKCS1_NO_IMPLICIT_REJECT_PADDING constant that bypasses the toggle, KDK secrets left on the stack, and EXT_PKEY keys forced to no implicit rejection. None concerns CMS or PKCS7 decryption.
judge.ground_truth_summary: cms_RecipientInfo_ktri_decrypt and pkcs7_decrypt_rinfo explicitly disable RSA implicit rejection for RSA keys. This restores a Bleichenbacher padding oracle in multi-recipient CMS/PKCS7 decryption.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR only adds the implicit-rejection option, and it defaults to enabled. It does not change cms_env.c or pk7_doit.c, so CMS/PKCS7 never disables implicit rejection; the docs even describe it as in use. The scanner's findings are adjacent: the public padding-mode-8 constant, an uncleared KDK, and the EXT_PKEY fallback. None of them names the CMS/PKCS7 ctrl_str disablement. The GT chain is absent in this snapshot.

criteria: The bug is in selfsigned_verify_cb(), the custom verify callback used when validating a rootCaKeyUpdate self-signed cert.
After check_issued() matches a trust-store issuer, the callback appends 'cert' (the target/self) instead of 'issuer' to the chain.
Because of that chain, the signature check effectively runs against the cert itself, so no cryptographic link to the old root is established.
The result is that an attacker-supplied newWithOld/newWithNew is accepted as a trusted root CA.
The evaluated code must still contain the wrong X509_add_cert argument.
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: newWithNew is not required to be self-signed or the same CA; dangling output pointers; selfsigned_verify_cb overwrites cert and appends untrusted certs; mock server NULL dereference.
judge.ground_truth_summary: selfsigned_verify_cb added 'cert' instead of 'issuer' to the verification chain, so the self-signature check was ineffective. This let RA-level attackers install a forged root CA via rootCaKeyUpdate.
judge.reasoning: The PR code calls X509_add_cert(chain, issuer, ...), so the GT typo is fixed. Finding 3 targets the same callback but describes a different problem: the 'cert' loop variable is overwritten while appending untrusted certs, and there is no target/key identity check. Finding 1 is a missing self-signed/same-CA policy check. Neither finding identifies the cert-vs-issuer argument error. Both are adjacent findings, not the GT causal chain.

criteria: Vulnerable code is validate_email_name() in crypto/x509/x509_vpm.c
Local-part length is computed wrongly as len - (at - name) instead of at - name
The 64-octet local-part bound check uses that wrong length
The full email len, not the local-part length, is passed to validate_local_part, causing an out-of-bounds read
Reachable via the X509_VERIFY_PARAM email APIs or S/MIME From: parsing
judge.findings_summary: Seven findings: UAF on stack push failure, several NULL dereferences, identity lists cleared before validation, hostflags applied to email checks, and lost NUL terminator in buffer_copy. None concern the validate_email_name local-part length.
judge.ground_truth_summary: validate_email_name computes the local-part length wrongly and passes the full len to validate_local_part. The local-part limit is never really enforced, and the read can run out of bounds.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already has the fix. It sets local_len = at - name, checks local_len > 64, and calls validate_local_part(name, local_len, ...), so the GT chain is broken. No scanner finding targets validate_email_name's length arithmetic. The one OOB finding (#7) is a different bug: buffer_copy drops the NUL terminator.

criteria: Writer in ossl_synchronize_rcu publishes the retire-in-order signal (next_to_retire++, broadcast, unlock prior_lock)
That signal is published before the loop that waits for the current qp's reader count to reach zero
The next writer can therefore proceed and retire or reuse a qp before readers have drained
The result is a use-after-free or double-retire race on recycled rcu_qp slots (more than 3 QPs)
In the evaluated code, the signal is still ordered before the zero-reader wait
judge.findings_summary: Two UAF findings on memory-ordering weakening: a RELAXED reader_idx store in update_qp, and ACQUIRE/RELAXED atomics in get_hold_current_qp. No finding addresses the next_to_retire ordering relative to the reader drain.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ossl_synchronize_rcu signaled next_to_retire before waiting for zero readers, so the next writer could retire or reuse a qp prematurely. The evaluated PR places the signal after the wait, so the bug is not present.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the next_to_retire increment, broadcast and unlock come after the reader-count-zero wait in both pthread and win, so the GT ordering bug is fixed. The scanner reports different issues: a relaxed store of reader_idx and weakened atomics in the reader handshake. Neither describes the retire-signal-before-drain ordering. This is an adjacent bug, not the GT bug.

criteria: Trigger: ossl_quic_wire_peek_frame_header() fails inside log_frame()
Missing guard: log_frame returns 0 on that failure without setting *need_skip
Caller log_frames loops while PACKET_remaining()>0 with no cursor advance and need_skip==0
Effect: infinite loop / DoS on the same packet position
Code evidence must show the peek-failure path still leaves need_skip unset
judge.findings_summary: Reports an infinite loop from non-minimal PADDING (0x40 0x00) that decodes without advancing, plus ILP32 truncation of STREAM frame length in need_skip.
judge.ground_truth_summary: log_frame returns 0 on peek_frame_header failure without setting need_skip. log_frames then loops forever on the unchanged packet position, causing a DoS. This PR already fixes it.
judge.reasoning: The PR already sets *need_skip = SIZE_MAX when peek_frame_header fails, so the GT causal chain is broken. Scanner finding 1 describes a different trigger: non-minimal PADDING that returns success without advancing. That is the same sink and loop with a different root cause. Finding 2 is ILP32 truncation of the STREAM length. Neither finding identifies the peek-failure path with need_skip left unset.

criteria: Vulnerable function is final_maxfragmentlen in ssl/statem/extensions.c
s->session is dereferenced (ext.max_fragment_len_mode) before any NULL check
s->session can be NULL at function entry on some handshake path
Finding identifies NULL pointer dereference / crash as the impact
Evaluated code lacks a NULL guard ahead of the first dereference
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: removed missing-MFL-on-resumption check leads to an unsolicited extension (logic error). Finding 2: TLS 1.2 resumption writes MFL into a shared cached session (data race). Neither is a NULL dereference.
judge.ground_truth_summary: final_maxfragmentlen dereferences s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode before the existing NULL check, causing a remote NULL-dereference DoS. This benign PR places the NULL check first.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated diff adds 'if (s->session == NULL) return 1;' before any dereference of s->session, so the GT NULL-dereference chain is broken. Neither scanner finding mentions a NULL dereference. Finding 1 is about a removed resumption-MFL consistency check (a logic error), and finding 2 is a data race on a shared session. Both are adjacent issues, not the GT.

criteria: ossl_quic_get_peer_token builds a lookup key via ossl_quic_build_new_token
ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL when BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on an unset peer address
Return value is not NULL-checked before use
NULL key is passed to lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve, which dereferences it and segfaults
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: unbounded token cache, leak on failed insert, use-after-free from an ignored CRYPTO_UP_REF failure, and IPv6 scope or AF_UNIX key collisions. None concern a NULL key from build_new_token.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ossl_quic_get_peer_token passes a possibly-NULL key from ossl_quic_build_new_token (unset peer address) to lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve without checking it, causing a segfault. This is fixed in the evaluated PR.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR diff checks the key for NULL after ossl_quic_build_new_token and returns 0, so the GT NULL-dereference chain is broken. None of the scanner findings mention a missing NULL check or an unset peer address causing a NULL key. The findings cover unbounded cache growth, insert-failure leaks, an ignored UP_REF result, and key collisions, which are adjacent issues.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: OSSL_HASH.hashValue is declared OPTIONAL (ASN1_OPT), so decoding can leave it NULL
i2r_HASH reaches hashValue->data/length while printing the attributeDescriptor extension
No NULL check on hash->hashValue before the dereference
Crafted cert/CRL that omits hashValue triggers a NULL dereference crash during printing
Evaluated code must still lack the guard
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: unsanitized control characters in output, IMPLICIT vs EXPLICIT tagging (noting a missing hashValue only gives partial output), OID truncation in an 80-byte buffer, and an ILP32 hex-encoding overflow.
judge.ground_truth_summary: i2r_HASH dereferences the optional hashValue without a NULL check, so a crafted CRL/cert crashes extension printing. The benign PR already includes the fix.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR has 'if (hash->hashValue == NULL) return 0;' before the dereference, which breaks the GT chain. Finding 2 notes that hashValue is optional but says i2r_HASH returns 0, which is the fixed behavior, not a crash. Finding 4 is an ILP32 overflow, a different bug. No finding describes an active NULL dereference.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Source: untrusted certificate notAfter ASN1_STRING data from ASN1_STRING_get0_data()
Sink: strcmp() (or another NUL-terminator-dependent comparison) on that buffer
Missing guard: the explicit ASN1_STRING length is not checked before the comparison
Impact: heap out-of-bounds read past a short, non-NUL-terminated buffer
Location: ossl_x509_check_cert_time in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: the sentinel match skips the ASN.1 type check and time validation, so a 15-byte UTCTime is accepted. It also notes *error is left unset and the literal is not EBCDIC-portable.
judge.ground_truth_summary: strcmp() on non-NUL-terminated ASN1_STRING notAfter data without a length check, causing a heap out-of-bounds read in ossl_x509_check_cert_time.
judge.reasoning: The PR code first checks notafter->length == 15 and then uses memcmp with a length of 15, so the strcmp out-of-bounds read is not present. The scanner reports a different bug: the sentinel check accepts a UTCTime-typed value, a semantic validation bypass. That finding implicitly relies on the bounded length+memcmp comparison. It does not identify a strcmp or NUL-termination over-read.

criteria: BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg RETURN callback invocation passes NULL as processed pointer
Same invocation passes a potentially positive inret (real ret)
bio_call_callback legacy shim dereferences *processed when inret>0 for BIO_CB_RETURN non-CTRL ops

criteria: Source: column index iCol decoded from a corrupt FTS3 doclist in fts3auxNextMethod

criteria: Trigger: the remote peer keeps sending PING frames while not reading from the connection

Finding 1 says sendbuf fills up and the payload write returns AGAIN, which assumes writes do fail on capacity and contradicts the GT soft-limit growth premise. criteria: Location is lib/http2.c cf_h2_update_local_win, reached via the new write_paused state (h2_xfer_write_resp / http2_data_pause)

On unpause, nghttp2_submit_window_update is sent without first setting nghttp2's internal local window size

criteria: Sink is strcmp(per->uploadfile, ".") in tool_read_cb (src/tool_cb_rea.c ~line 95)

criteria: Curl_cookie_getlist returns live jar Cookie pointers instead of independent copies

criteria: tftp_state_timeout detects expiry via Curl_timeleft() returning negative timeout_ms

criteria: servercert gates verifystatus() on !connssl->reused_session, skipping the OCSP status check when a session is reused

Result: a connection requiring CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYSTATUS completes without any status check (fail-open)
Correct guard is to disable session reuse when verifystatus is set, forcing a full handshake and status check
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicError findings in servercert. OCSP verification is skipped when a session is set or resumed. Recommends refusing session reuse when verifystatus is enabled.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The reused_session flag suppresses verifystatus() in servercert while ossl_connect_step1 still reuses cached sessions under verifystatus, bypassing the OCSP check. Fix: gate the session lookup on !verifystatus.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT causal chain. Session reuse sets reused_session, servercert then skips verifystatus, and VERIFYSTATUS is bypassed on resumed connections. It also proposes the GT fix: refuse session reuse when verifystatus is set. The PR diff shows the cache lookup is still ungated by verifystatus, so the vulnerability is active. Finding 1 is a related variant with the same sink and guard.

criteria: Vulnerable site is reuse_conn() in lib/url.c, where hostname structs are shallow-copied from old_conn to conn
host.rawalloc and host.encalloc are NULLed on the source, but conn_to_host.encalloc is not
After the copy, conn and old_conn share the same conn_to_host.encalloc heap pointer
Freeing old_conn (conn_free calling Curl_free_idnconverted_hostname) releases the shared buffer
A later teardown or reset of conn->conn_to_host frees the same buffer again (double free / UAF)
judge.findings_summary: One DoubleFree finding: reuse_conn NULLs host.encalloc but not conn_to_host.encalloc. conn_free(old_conn) frees the shared IDN buffer, causing UAF and a later double free.
judge.ground_truth_summary: reuse_conn shallow-copies conn_to_host without NULLing old_conn->conn_to_host.encalloc. Freeing old_conn and later conn frees the same encalloc twice.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds a conn_free(old_conn) call and NULLs only conn_to_host.rawalloc, leaving encalloc shared. The scanner names the same function, the same missed encalloc NULLing, the same conn_free sink and the same later double free on teardown. It also adds the UAF consequence and a CONNECT_TO IDN trigger. It writes &conn->conn_to_host where old_conn is meant, a minor typo that does not change the match.

criteria: pop3_perform() reads data->req.no_body to decide pop3->transfer (PPTRANSFER_INFO vs body)
That read happens before pop3_perform_command() recomputes no_body via !pop3_is_multiline(command)
Result: pop3->transfer reflects a stale or previous no_body value, not the current command's value
Consequence: the transfer state machine mishandles whether a body is expected (wrong setup or data handling, worse on handle reuse)
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: UIDL classification ignores URL-path args; LIST-with-args table entry is wrong; stale no_body snapshot in pop3_perform leaves transfer=BODY, causing unread socket data on reuse.
judge.ground_truth_summary: pop3_perform() reads data->req.no_body to set pop3->transfer before pop3_perform_command() recomputes it from multiline detection. The transfer state is therefore based on a stale value.
judge.reasoning: Finding 3 states the GT ordering directly: the no_body override happens after pop3_perform() snapshots the flag, so pop3->transfer stays PPTRANSFER_BODY. The PR diff confirms no_body is set only at the end of pop3_perform_command(), and nothing reorders it. The described impact (unread data on reused connections) is a plausible downstream effect of the same stale-state chain. Findings 1 and 2 are adjacent classification bugs and do not match.

criteria: RTMP* allocated in rtmp_setup_connection is registered in the connection meta hash with the rtmp_conn_dtor destructor before RTMP_SetupURL
The RTMP_SetupURL failure path (malformed URL) still calls RTMP_Free(r) manually
The pointer is never removed from the meta hash before that manual free
Later connection teardown (disconnect/meta_remove or hash destroy) runs rtmp_conn_dtor, which calls RTMP_Close and RTMP_Free on the already-freed pointer, causing a double-free
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a double-free of the RTMP handle on RTMP_SetupURL failure, with the meta dtor freeing it again at teardown. Finding 2 is an adjacent issue: RTMP_Close on an uninitialized handle when meta_set fails.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The RTMP* is registered in the conn meta hash with a destructor, but the URL-parse failure path still frees it manually. Connection teardown then frees it again: a double-free in rtmp_setup_connection.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff keeps RTMP_Free(r) on the SetupURL failure path after Curl_conn_meta_set registers the destructor. Scanner finding 1 identifies the same trigger (malformed URL), the same sink (the dtor's second RTMP_Free via meta remove or hash destroy), and the same ownership/lifetime flaw. Nothing in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Curl_get_line's while(1) loop retries fgets() after it returns NULL
Loop exit relies only on feof() (*eof), a trailing newline, or a dynbuf append failure
Missing ferror() check: an I/O error leaves feof false, so no exit condition is met
Result is an infinite CPU-spinning loop (DoS) when parsing cookie/HSTS/alt-svc/netrc files
Regression: the PR removed the old NULL-with-empty-buffer break
judge.findings_summary: Three LogicError findings. #1 is an infinite loop on fgets error because ferror is never checked. #2 is a synthetic empty line at EOF. #3 is a NUL-prefixed line no longer stopping the parse.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Rewritten Curl_get_line only exits on feof, a newline, or an append error. A persistent fgets I/O error leaves feof false and spins the loop forever, a DoS regression.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the same location (lib/curl_get_line.c:47, Curl_get_line), the same trigger (fgets NULL from a read error with feof clear), and the same missing guard (no ferror check, exit only on eof). It describes the same infinite busy-loop DoS and the regression from removing the old break. The PR diff confirms this code is present and that nothing in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Vulnerable function is ipv4_normalize in lib/urlapi.c, specifically the new lenient rc-handling branch added by the PR
Trigger: a final component that is the '0x' hex prefix with no following hex digits
curlx_str_hex returns STRE_NO_NUM and leaves the cursor at end-of-string, so the 'n && rc==STRE_NO_NUM && !*c' check passes
Missing guard: the hex-prefix branch is not excluded from the trailing-dot leniency, so n is decremented
Impact: a malformed host such as '127.1.0x' is classified and normalized as a valid IPv4 address instead of HOST_NAME
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding in ipv4_normalize: a trailing '0x' with no digits hits the STRE_NO_NUM trailing-dot path, so hosts like 127.1.0x parse as IPv4 (an SSRF / host-confusion risk).
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new trailing-dot leniency in ipv4_normalize also accepts an empty '0x' hex component at end-of-string, so inputs like '127.1.0x' are wrongly normalized as valid IPv4.
judge.reasoning: The scanner identifies the same function and the same new STRE_NO_NUM leniency. It names the same trigger (a trailing '0x' with no digits, cursor at '\0'), the same missing hex-prefix exclusion, and the same misclassification as IPv4, giving the '127.1.0x' -> 127.0.0.1 example. The PR diff shows the flawed condition, and nothing in the diff mitigates it.

criteria: Trigger: parsing the deprecated ch_layouts option string in common_init of buffersink.c
av_realloc_array result stored only in local tmp, never assigned back to buf->channel_layouts
Subsequent memset/writes dereference the stale pointer (NULL on first iteration, dangling after a moved realloc)
Result is a NULL write crash or use-after-free (memory corruption)
Vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR diff with no fix
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: missing realloc assignment in common_init leads to a NULL write in memset and a leak, plus possible use-after-free. Finding 2: separate logic bug where deprecated sample_fmts and sample_rates are dropped in query_formats.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In common_init, av_realloc_array result in tmp is never assigned to buf->channel_layouts. The memset then dereferences a NULL or dangling pointer, causing a crash. The memset also clears only one element instead of two.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the same trigger (parsing the ch_layouts string in common_init), the same missing assignment of tmp back to buf->channel_layouts, and the same sink (memset on the NULL pointer). It also notes the possible use-after-free on later iterations. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code with no fix. The scanner does not mention the secondary memset-size issue, but that is not needed for the match.

criteria: Source: num_parameters read via ffio_read_leb in audio_element_obu from untrusted input
Missing guard: no upper bound (<=2) on num_parameters for Channel-based audio elements (only Scene forced to 0)
Trigger: duplicate DEMIXING/RECON_GAIN param types parsed repeatedly via param_parse
Sink: element->demixing_info/recon_gain_info pointer overwritten by new av_iamf_param_definition_alloc, leaking prior allocation (memory exhaustion DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Nine findings: substream heap overflow, OOB reads of the sound_system_map and ipcm sample_fmt tables, NULL deref in free helpers, uninitialized header padding, obu_size underflow, AAC put_bits negative count, read_close leak, ambisonics sqrt UB. None covers the num_parameters bound.
judge.ground_truth_summary: audio_element_obu has no upper bound on num_parameters for Channel elements. Repeated DEMIXING/RECON_GAIN params make param_parse overwrite demixing_info/recon_gain_info pointers, leaking memory (CVE-2025-1816).
judge.reasoning: None of the scanner findings covers num_parameters in audio_element_obu or the leak from duplicate demixing/recon_gain parameters overwriting earlier allocations. Finding 8 is a memory leak, but it comes from iamf_read_close nulling ownership pointers on header failure. That is a different trigger and a different sink. The other findings are unrelated overflows, out-of-bounds reads and undefined behavior. The diff is truncated, so the GT code cannot be confirmed.

criteria: The source is the fps option, changed to an unbounded VIDEO_RATE (count may also be small), and the rate % (fps*count) divisibility check was removed.
step = sample_rate/(fps*count) can exceed fft_len = 2^ceil(log2(sample_rate*timeclamp)), and nothing validates step against fft_len.
In filter_frame, remaining_fill is set to step after a plot, so j = fft_len - remaining_fill goes negative.
The sink is a write to fft_data[j+m] at negative offsets, a heap buffer underflow/overflow.
The vulnerable chain is present in the evaluated PR code.
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a heap overflow in filter_frame when step exceeds fft_len (negative j writes to fft_data). The other findings cover a zero-step hang, an uninitialized ret, an fft_bits range problem, and a freetype divide-by-zero.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The showcqt rewrite made fps an unbounded VIDEO_RATE and dropped the divisibility check. As a result step can exceed fft_len, j = fft_len - remaining_fill goes negative, and filter_frame writes to fft_data at negative offsets.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the unbounded rational fps and the missing step-vs-fft_len check. It explains that remaining_fill=step makes j=fft_len-remaining_fill negative, and that filter_frame then writes to fft_data[j+m]. It gives a concrete trigger (48kHz, fps=5, count=1). The PR diff shows fps as VIDEO_RATE with no bounds and the divisibility check removed. No mitigation is present.

criteria: Sink is the ff_copy_bits() call that copies A53 closed-caption side data in ff_mpeg1_encode_picture_header
Length argument is side_data->size, a byte count
ff_copy_bits expects its length in bits, so the units do not match
Result is that only about 1/8 of the caption payload is written, which corrupts or truncates the CC output
Introduced by replacing the per-byte put_bits loop during the refactor
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: the A53 CC payload length is passed to ff_copy_bits in bytes, not bits, truncating and misaligning the captions. It warns that simply multiplying by 8 would over-read the unpadded buffer.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactor replaced the per-byte put_bits loop with ff_copy_bits(pb, data, side_data->size), passing bytes where bits are expected, which corrupts closed captions. Multiplying by 8 alone risks over-reading unpadded side data.
judge.reasoning: The scanner points to the exact ff_copy_bits call, says side_data->size is passed as bytes while the function expects bits, and explains the truncated and corrupted caption output. It also flags the padding over-read risk if the fix only multiplies by 8, matching the GT. The PR diff confirms the buggy line is present, and nothing in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Location: hls_pcm_sample in libavcodec/hevc.c
Trigger: monochrome SPS (chroma_format_idc == 0), where hshift/vshift for chroma are 0
Faulty operation: the PCM length calculation still adds chroma sample terms
Missing guard: the length is not gated on chroma_format_idc, although the put_pcm chroma calls are
Consequence: an inflated length makes skip_bytes over-skip, desynchronizing bitstream/CABAC parsing
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: PCM length includes chroma for monochrome (exact GT match); verify_md5 OOB read on the GRAY8 palette; chroma_format_idc no longer range-checked; stale SAO chroma flags.
judge.ground_truth_summary: For YUV400, the hls_pcm_sample length still counts two full-size chroma planes because only put_pcm was guarded. This inflates skip_bytes and desynchronizes parsing.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names hls_pcm_sample, the monochrome trigger with zero hshift/vshift, the ungated chroma term in the length, and the skip_bytes over-skip that desynchronizes CABAC. The PR diff guards only the put_pcm chroma calls and leaves the length unchanged, so the vulnerability is present in the evaluated code. The finding treats it as an active bug.

criteria: get_eia608_packet assumes a c608 sample holds a single atom: one 8-byte header followed by caption byte pairs
Only the first atom header is skipped (avio_skip(pb, 8)); later cdat/cdt2 headers are read as caption data
Hardcoded 0xFC cc_type cannot tell CC field 1 (cdat) from field 2 (cdt2)
Output size ((size-8)/2)*3 ignores multiple atom headers, so packets are corrupted or wrongly sized
Reached from mov_read_packet for AV_CODEC_ID_EIA_608 samples
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: signed integer overflow in the new_size calculation, leading to heap overflow. Finding 2: the EIA-608 path bypasses ffio_limit, allowing large allocations and DoS from an untrusted sample size.
judge.ground_truth_summary: LogicError: get_eia608_packet skips only the first 8-byte atom header, so later cdat/cdt2 headers are treated as caption pairs. The hardcoded 0xFC mislabels field 2 and the output sizing is wrong.
judge.reasoning: The PR code does have the multi-atom misparse. Neither finding identifies it: there is no mention of later cdat/cdt2 headers being read as caption data, or of field 1/2 being misidentified via the hardcoded 0xFC. Finding 1 covers only the secondary integer-overflow note in the GT, which is a different sink and mechanism. Finding 2 is an adjacent DoS from the missing ffio_limit. Both are near matches in the same function.

criteria: ff_thread_progress_report does the release-store of progress before taking progress_mutex, outside the critical section
ff_thread_progress_await slow path reads progress with memory_order_relaxed while holding the mutex
A relaxed load that sees the release-store does not synchronize-with it, and the mutex gives no happens-before because the reporter has not locked or unlocked it yet
The waiter can then read non-atomic payload data written before report() without ordering, which is a data race
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR with no fix
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: DataRace, progress is release-stored outside the mutex while the await slow path uses a relaxed load, so payload reads lack happens-before. Finding 2: non-atomic check-then-store can move progress backwards.
judge.ground_truth_summary: report() release-stores progress before locking the mutex, while await() slow path loads it relaxed under the mutex. No acquire-release or mutex happens-before results, so payload data such as VP9 MVs is read racily.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the release-store before the mutex in report() and the relaxed load inside the mutex in await(), and explains why neither acquire-release nor mutex ordering is established. It gives the same interleaving and the same consequence, unsynchronized payload reads. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code unchanged. Finding 2 is an adjacent issue and does not affect the verdict.

criteria: PR adds av_freep(&cblk->lengthinc), which sets the pointer to NULL
nb_lengthinc counter is not reset to 0 after the free, leaving stale state
Guard `!nb_terminationsinc && !lengthinc` is bypassed when nb_terminationsinc != 0
Loop bounded by stale nb_lengthinc dereferences NULL lengthinc[cwsno] in jpeg2000_decode_packet
Triggered on a later decode_packet call for the same code block via crafted JPEG2000 input
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a uint16 length wrap, which is unrelated. Finding 2 reports a NULL dereference of lengthinc after av_freep with stale nb_lengthinc and a guard bypassed by nonzero nb_terminationsinc.
judge.ground_truth_summary: av_freep(&cblk->lengthinc) runs without resetting nb_lengthinc. A later call with nonzero nb_terminationsinc bypasses the guard, and the loop dereferences the NULL lengthinc pointer (CVE-2025-22921).
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the exact GT chain. It notes that av_freep leaves nb_lengthinc stale, that the guard is bypassed when nb_terminationsinc is nonzero, and that lengthinc[cwsno] is then read through a NULL pointer, causing DoS. The PR diff shows the free without a counter reset, and the guard is as described. The PR adds no mitigation. The UAF remark about av_free is only an aside; the NULL dereference is presented as an active bug.

criteria: ff_dovi_configure round-trips avctx through a temporary AVCodecParameters via from_context/to_context
avcodec_parameters_to_context frees and replaces avctx->coded_side_data (av_packet_side_data_free)
A caller (libaomenc aom_init) holds a pointer into coded_side_data (cpb_props from ff_encode_add_cpb_side_data) across the ff_dovi_configure call
The caller later writes through the dangling pointer, causing a heap use-after-free
The PR adds no fix that preserves existing side-data pointers
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: UAF in libaom, where cpb_props dangles after avcodec_parameters_to_context frees coded_side_data inside ff_dovi_configure. Finding 2: PPS overflow and divide-by-zero.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ff_dovi_configure's new codecpar round-trip calls avcodec_parameters_to_context, freeing avctx->coded_side_data. libaomenc's cpb_props pointer dangles and is then written to, causing a heap UAF.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain exactly. The PR adds the round-trip in ff_dovi_configure, and avcodec_parameters_to_context frees avctx->coded_side_data. libaomenc keeps cpb_props from earlier and writes through it after the call. The finding names the same trigger, sink and lifetime violation, and nothing in the diff mitigates it. Finding 2 is an unrelated integer-overflow issue.

criteria: submit_packet() no longer returns early for no-delay codecs (vp3/theora) when draining on an empty packet
Guard skips only update_context_from_thread() but still sets fctx->prev_thread to a thread that never decoded and has no VLC state
ff_thread_flush() copies context from that VLC-less prev_thread into thread[0] via update_context_from_thread()/vp3_update_thread_context(), nulling coeff_vlc
After flush and restart, vp3 unpack_dct_coeffs() dereferences the NULL coeff_vlc
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: an OOM on next_pkt allocation causing an assert abort or NULL threads dereference during teardown, and unbounded frame buffering in frame_worker_thread. Both are unrelated to the prev_thread/VLC draining chain.
judge.ground_truth_summary: During draining, submit_packet sets prev_thread to a VLC-less thread for no-delay codecs. ff_thread_flush copies that state to thread[0], setting coeff_vlc to NULL, and vp3 unpack_dct_coeffs dereferences it after flush.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff still contains the GT chain: the early return was removed, the new guard only skips the context update, prev_thread is still set, and flush still copies from prev_thread. Neither scanner finding matches it. One reports an OOM teardown abort in ff_frame_thread_init. The other reports unbounded frame buffering in the worker. Neither covers prev_thread/VLC state during draining, the flush copy, or the vp3 NULL dereference.

criteria: TaskItem 'task' is pushed onto tf_model->task_queue via ff_queue_push_back, which transfers ownership to the queue
PR adds av_freep(&task) in error branches after the successful push (extract_lltask_from_task failure and request_queue pop failure)
Task is not removed from task_queue before being freed
dnn_free_model_tf teardown walks task_queue and av_freep's each item, freeing the same TaskItem a second time
Location: ff_dnn_execute_model_tf in libavfilter/dnn/dnn_backend_tf.c around lines 1159-1177
judge.findings_summary: Two findings. One reports that execute_model_tf frees the live model on error (UAF/double-free). The other reports a TaskItem freed in ff_dnn_execute_model_tf after it was queued, then freed again in teardown (double-free).
judge.ground_truth_summary: The leak fix adds av_freep(&task) in error paths after ff_queue_push_back already gave the task to task_queue. dnn_free_model_tf later frees it again, a double free.
judge.reasoning: Scanner finding 2 matches the GT. It names both post-push av_freep(&task) sites in ff_dnn_execute_model_tf. It notes the task is still owned by task_queue and shows the teardown loop that av_freep's queued items, causing a double free. The PR diff adds these frees and adds no dequeue step. The UseAfterFree label is acceptable because the title states double-free.

criteria: Vulnerable code is in dump_stream_group for the TILE_GRID group type in libavformat/dump.c
The loop bound is tile_grid->nb_tiles and the subscript is tile_grid->offsets[i].idx, both taken from untrusted parsed container metadata
No check enforces offsets[i].idx < stg->nb_streams before indexing stg->streams[]
The sink is an out-of-bounds read of stg->streams[] followed by dereferencing an invalid AVStream pointer
The flawed loop is present in the evaluated PR code and is not mitigated
judge.findings_summary: Unchecked tile_grid->offsets[i].idx indexes stg->streams[] at dump.c:785, causing an OOB read and garbage-pointer deref. Reachable via HEIF grid/iovl idx inconsistencies.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dump_stream_group loops over nb_tiles and indexes stg->streams[] with untrusted offsets[i].idx without validating it against nb_streams, causing an out-of-bounds read and invalid-pointer dereference.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds the loop that indexes stg->streams[tile_grid->offsets[i].idx] up to nb_tiles with no bounds check. The scanner flags this exact line and names the missing idx < nb_streams check. It also gives a reachable HEIF trigger and describes the OOB read and the dereference of the bad pointer. Its label is BufferOverflow, but the root cause, trigger and sink all match the GT, and the PR adds nothing that blocks this path.

criteria: Source/trigger: attacker-controlled 32-bit seek_back read from the file after a 'dhav' tag in get_duration()
end_pos is computed as end_buffer_pos + offset - seek_back + 8, so it can fall below the buffer base
The bounds check rejects only end_pos < 0 plus an upper bound; it lacks an end_pos >= end_buffer_pos lower-bound check
Sink: AV_RL32(end_buffer + (end_pos - end_buffer_pos) + 16) reads before the heap allocation
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR snapshot with no lower-bound fix
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: (1) heap OOB read from the missing lower bound on end_pos plus an upper-bound off-by-4; (2) end_buffer memory leak; (3) unchecked avio_read result.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In dhav get_duration, an attacker-controlled seek_back can push end_pos below end_buffer_pos. The check covers only end_pos<0 and the upper bound, so AV_RL32 reads before the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the ground truth exactly. It names the attacker-controlled seek_back as the trigger, the end_pos computation, the missing lower bound against end_buffer_pos, and the AV_RL32 out-of-bounds sink in get_duration. The PR diff introduces this exact code and adds no mitigation. The extra upper-bound off-by-4 point is additional and does not weaken the match.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled uint32 decoded_size read from the codec48 bitstream header
Sink: rle_decode(ctx, dst, decoded_size) writing into frame buffer ctx->frm0 in the compr==2 path
Missing guard: decoded_size is never checked against the destination buffer size (buf_size or frame allocation)
Impact: heap out-of-bounds write past the frame buffer
Evaluated PR code contains the unchecked compr==2 call with no added clamp
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: heap overflow from unchecked decoded_size passed to rle_decode in old_codec48 compr 2. Also reported: OOB reads from codec48 motion vectors and unaligned uint16 stores.
judge.ground_truth_summary: old_codec48 passes the attacker-controlled decoded_size to rle_decode without checking it against the destination buffer size, causing a heap buffer overflow when writing to frm0.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the same source (decoded_size from the bitstream), the same sink (rle_decode into ctx->frm0 for compr==2), and the same missing bound against the frame allocation, at old_codec48 line 1187. The PR diff shows case 2 calling rle_decode with no size check, so the vulnerability is active in the evaluated code. The note that values above INT_MAX become negative does not weaken the match.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled rle_raw_size read from the DWA header in dwa_uncompress
Sink: the alpha copy loop reads ai0/ai1 from rle_raw_data, with ai1 offset by rle_raw_size/2, across ysize*xsize
Missing guard: no check that rle_raw_size >= 2*xsize*ysize; the buffer is allocated with exactly rle_raw_size bytes
Result: heap out-of-bounds read past rle_raw_data that leaks into decoded pixel data
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR without mitigation
judge.findings_summary: Seven DWA/EXR issues. Finding 4 is an OOB read in the alpha loop of rle_raw_data because rle_raw_size is not checked against 2*xsize*ysize. Others cover DC/AC buffer handling, write overflow, zlib overread and int64 sizes.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dwa_uncompress trusts rle_raw_size without checking it covers 2*xsize*ysize or capping it, so the ai0/ai1 alpha reads overrun the rle_raw_data heap buffer (OOB read).
judge.reasoning: Finding 4 matches the GT. It names the attacker-controlled rle_raw_size header field and the ai0/ai1 reads at the rle_raw_size/2 offset. It states the missing requirement that rle_raw_size >= 2*ysize*xsize, given only a >0 check, and concludes the loop reads past the allocation. The PR diff contains this exact code with no guard.

criteria: Attacker-controlled index metadata from the MXF file (IndexStartPosition/IndexDuration) feeds the new clamp in mxf_edit_unit_absolute_offset
The clamp FFMAX(FFMIN(edit_unit, index_end), first_segment->index_start_position) can leave edit_unit hugely negative, near INT64_MIN
No sign or range validation of edit_unit after the clamp
The negative edit_unit then reaches a signed 64-bit multiplication by 2 (or nb_segments) that overflows (UB)
The vulnerable code was introduced by this PR and is not mitigated within it
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: an infinite loop on gapped segments, a uint64/int64 clamp yielding a negative edit_unit that overflows nb_segments*edit_unit, and offsets precomputed before zero durations are repaired.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new clamp uses file-controlled index_start_position and does not ensure edit_unit is non-negative. A near-INT64_MIN edit_unit later overflows a signed multiplication by 2 (UBSan).
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 identifies the GT root cause: the clamp at line 1917 lets a crafted start position produce edit_unit near INT64_MIN. It also notes the missing negative check, since the INT64_MAX/n guard still passes. The scanner's sink is nb_segments*edit_unit, not GT's index*=2. With nb_segments=2, though, it matches the UBSan operand order '2 * -4962…'. No fix appears in the PR. The differing sink lowers confidence.

criteria: Source: untrusted 32-bit stts sample_duration/sample_count fields from a crafted MOV/MP4 file
State: current_dts and corrected_dts int64 accumulators grow independently across entries, with no saturation or range check
Trigger: a large negative delta_magnitude cast drives corrected_dts strongly negative while current_dts stays large or positive
Sink: unchecked signed subtraction (current_dts - corrected_dts) in the drift computation overflows int64 (UB)
Missing guard: no validation that the operands stay in a range where the subtraction is safe
judge.findings_summary: Three IntegerOverflow findings in mov_read_stts. One: signed overflow of the current_dts - corrected_dts drift computation via negative corrected_dts accumulation. Two: unsigned underflow when duration is 0. Three: 32-bit count*duration wrap.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The max_stts_delta PR adds int64 current_dts and corrected_dts accumulators driven by untrusted stts fields. The unchecked signed subtraction current_dts - corrected_dts in the drift computation overflows int64 (UB).
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the same chain: attacker-controlled stts entries, negative int32 delta_magnitude accumulated into corrected_dts with no saturation, then the (current_dts - corrected_dts) drift subtraction overflowing int64 as UB. It needs no non-default options. The PR diff adds this exact code with no guard. The trigger differs slightly from GT (corrected_dts pushed alone toward INT64_MIN), but the source, sink, and missing guard all match.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled bits_per_coded_sample and nb_channels parsed from the W64 fmt chunk via ff_get_wav_header
Sink: 32-bit signed int multiplication ((bits_per_coded_sample+7)/8)*nb_channels in the w64_read_header block_align sanity check
Missing guard: no check that the product fits in int before computing it
Consequence: signed overflow UB yielding a corrupted value compared with and possibly assigned to codecpar->block_align
Code is present in the evaluated PR snapshot with no mitigation
judge.findings_summary: Signed int overflow in the new w64_read_header block_align repair: file-controlled bps and channels are multiplied, and the wrapped result can be stored in block_align. Also reports a huge-allocation bypass.
judge.ground_truth_summary: w64_read_header multiplies file-derived ((bits_per_coded_sample+7)/8) by nb_channels in signed int without an overflow check. The UB corrupts the block_align sanity check and the stored value.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds the unchecked int product ((bps+7)/8)*nb_channels in w64_read_header. The scanner names this exact expression, says both inputs come from the file, and describes signed overflow with the wrapped value written back to block_align. That matches the GT source, sink and missing guard. It also mentions an INT_MAX+7 variant and a huge-allocation issue, but the core product overflow matches. No mitigation is present.

criteria: Vulnerable function is set_pict_type in libavcodec/vvc/refs.c, reached from ff_vvc_set_new_ref
Loop over CBS fragment units with unit->type <= VVC_RSV_IRAP_11 treats them as slice units
unit->content_ref is cast to H266RawSliceHeader* and dereferenced via IS_I/IS_B
No NULL check on content_ref, which can be NULL for units CBS did not parse (malformed or crafted input)
Trigger path: non-IRAP picture with ph_inter_slice_allowed_flag set, from untrusted bitstream
judge.findings_summary: NULL dereference in set_pict_type. Reserved VCL NAL units (4/5/6/11) stay in the fragment with NULL content_ref, which IS_I/IS_B then dereference without a check.
judge.ground_truth_summary: set_pict_type dereferences unit->content_ref as H266RawSliceHeader for slice-type units without a NULL check. Malformed bitstreams leave it NULL, causing a crash.
judge.reasoning: The scanner points to the same function, the same loop and the same missing NULL check on content_ref before the IS_I/IS_B dereference. It gives a concrete trigger: reserved VCL NAL types left unparsed with content_ref NULL. That matches the GT's malformed-bitstream cause. The PR diff contains the vulnerable code and adds no guard.

criteria: Source/trigger: 16-bit start and count values read from the attacker-controlled bitstream in mm_decode_pal
Sink: write to s->palette[start+i] inside a count-bounded loop
Missing guard: no clamp, mask, or bounds check keeping start+i below 256 (AVPALETTE_COUNT)
Introduced by the PR's replacement of the fixed 128-iteration loop
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR snapshot with no mitigation
judge.findings_summary: One BufferOverflow finding in mm_decode_pal: attacker-controlled start and count (0..65535) drive writes to s->palette[start+i] with no check against AVPALETTE_COUNT (256), overflowing MmContext on the heap.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The refactor reads the start offset and count from the stream but never checks that start+i stays within the 256-entry palette, allowing an out-of-bounds write in mm_decode_pal.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows unchecked le16 start and count values indexing s->palette[start+i]. It adds no bounds check. The scanner names the same function and the same attacker-controlled start/count source. It also names the same out-of-bounds palette write sink and the same missing check against 256 entries. It describes the issue as active and exploitable, so it matches the ground-truth causal chain exactly.

criteria: Attacker-controlled block size and `space` field are read from the MLV file in read_packet
`size` is decremented by 12, 8 and `space` without a remaining-size check, so the unsigned value can underflow
The unchecked `size` reaches get_packet_lj92, where `av_new_packet(size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE)` overflows or truncates
A mismatched allocation followed by writes (TIFF header or avio_read) causes a heap-buffer-overflow
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: unchecked size and space subtractions in read_packet underflow. Finding 2: size+MAX_HEADER_SIZE truncation in get_packet_lj92 leads to a heap overflow. Finding 3: uninitialized bytes left in the packet.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unchecked attacker-controlled size and space underflow in read_packet, then size+MAX_HEADER_SIZE overflows in get_packet_lj92's allocation, causing a heap-buffer-overflow during the writes and the avio_read copy.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 follows the exact GT chain: an attacker-controlled block size or space underflows `size` in read_packet, then `size+2048` in get_packet_lj92's av_new_packet overflows or truncates, and the writes that follow overflow the heap. Finding 1 covers the subtraction underflow. The PR diff shows no guard on either path. The scanner names the header write rather than avio_read as the overflowing store, but the source, missing check and allocation sink all match.

criteria: Source/trigger: the bitstream-controlled noise.offset (noise_offset = offset - 16) is applied during noise filling
The PR moves that offset from the dequantized float sf onto the raw integer sfo in apply_noise_fill
No clamp or bounds check is applied to sfo after adding noise_offset
Sink: the unclamped sfo is used as an index into ff_aac_pow2sf_tab in dequant_scalefactors
Impact: an out-of-bounds read of the lookup table
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: a rate_idx table overflow, a FAC kv overflow, the reset_state ch index bug, dequant running on stale LPD state, and a negative skip_bits. None identifies the unclamped noise_offset on sfo causing an OOB read of pow2sf_tab.
judge.ground_truth_summary: apply_noise_fill now adds the bitstream-controlled noise_offset to the integer sfo without clamping. dequant_scalefactors then indexes ff_aac_pow2sf_tab with that sfo, causing an out-of-bounds read.
judge.reasoning: The vulnerable chain is present in the PR: sfo += noise_offset is unclamped, and the delayed dequant uses sfo as a pow2sf table index. Finding 4 comes closest, noting that sfo is newly treated as a table index. However, it frames the bug as a logic error from stale LPD state, says sfo 'usually will not accumulate', and never claims a missing clamp causes a pow2sf_tab OOB read. The other findings are unrelated bugs.

criteria: Vulnerable code is the bilinear chroma interpolation branch (uvalpha>0) in yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template / yuv2rgba64_1_c_template
Sink is the U/V weighted sum ubuf0*uvalpha1 + ubuf1*uvalpha - (128<<23) computed in signed int
Trigger: large-magnitude 32-bit chroma samples multiplied by 12-bit weights exceed the int range, causing signed overflow UB
Missing guard: U/V are declared plain int, not the overflow-tolerant SUINT/unsigned type, with no clamping
Introduced by this PR replacing the old sum/average with a weighted multiply
judge.findings_summary: One IntegerOverflow finding in the yuv2rgba64_1/full_1 templates. The signed 32-bit U/V weighted chroma interpolation overflows with large or negative 19-bit samples times 12-bit weights. Introduced by this PR.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The PR changed bilinear chroma interpolation to a weighted multiply but left U/V as signed int instead of SUINT. Large chroma samples times uvalpha weights overflow, which is signed-overflow UB in yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template.
judge.reasoning: The scanner flags signed overflow in the new U/V weighted-multiply expression. It explicitly names both yuv2rgba64_1_c_template and yuv2rgba64_full_1_c_template. It covers the negative-sample overflow mode that matches the UBSan report (-293650*16525). It notes the old averaging path had more headroom and that unsigned multiplies are used elsewhere. The PR diff shows the vulnerable code present and unmitigated, since av_assert2 only bounds uvalpha.

criteria: Trigger: ANIMv0/1 input with subversion < 2 reaches process_frame_obj
Code hard-codes the internal buffer to 384x242, sets have_dimensions=1, and sizes buffers to that
No check that the FOBJ w/h/left/top fit within 384x242; only the loose 800x600 sanity check applies
Decode routines then access the small buffer using the larger attacker-controlled w/h, causing out-of-bounds access
Causal chain is present in the PR diff and not mitigated (the clamp exists only in the else branch)
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: subversion<2 locks the buffer at 384x242 while codecs 37/47/48 decode up to 800x600, causing a heap overflow. Finding 2: negative left/top bypasses the oversized-frame clamp.
judge.ground_truth_summary: For subversion<2 the buffer is fixed at 384x242 and have_dimensions is set, but FOBJ w/h are only checked against 800x600. This allows out-of-bounds access on the small buffer.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. Subversion<2 locks the buffer at 384x242 and sets have_dimensions, with no check of FOBJ w/h, which the bound check allows up to 800x600. The decoders then use the larger w/h on the small buffer. The diff confirms the clamp exists only in the else branch, so it is skipped for this first FOBJ. Calling the bug an overflow rather than an OOB read is the same root cause.

criteria: Vulnerable location is mov_parse_heif_items() in libavformat/mov.c, where the strict guard (sample_count==1 && chunk_count==1) is replaced by sanity_checks()
sanity_checks() accepts the state sample_size!=0 with sample_count==0, because the (!sample_size && !sample_count) clause is false
Crafted HEIF/stsz input can reach this zero-count state while still passing validation
The sink is the subsequent write to sc->sample_sizes[0] (or the mov_build_index use) on an empty or NULL sample table, giving a NULL pointer dereference
The PR does not add any guard that restores the sample_count>0 invariant
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: NULL write to sample_sizes[0] after the weakened sanity_checks() in mov_parse_heif_items. Finding 2: huge index allocation from a large sample_count. Finding 3: signed overflow when computing the chunk offset.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The strict check sample_count==1/chunk_count==1 in mov_parse_heif_items was replaced by sanity_checks(), which allows sample_count==0 when sample_size!=0. This leads to a NULL dereference on the sample_sizes/index arrays.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the ground truth exactly. It names the replaced guard and explains that sanity_checks() passes when sample_size!=0 and sample_count==0. It gives a crafted-stsz path that frees sample_sizes, ending in a NULL write to sc->sample_sizes[0] in mov_parse_heif_items. The PR diff shows the weakened check still in place, with no mitigation.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled tile_data_size[c] parsed from the APV tile_header
Read-direction tile() sets tile_data[c] via align_get_bits and calls skip_bits_long(8*comp_size)
Missing guard: no check of comp_size against get_bits_left before the skip (the write path has a put_bytes_left check)
Consequence: tile_data pointer is paired with an oversized length, so downstream consumers read past the buffer
The PR snapshot contains no remaining-bits validation in the READ branch
judge.findings_summary: Six findings. Finding 2 identifies the unchecked skip_bits_long of tile_data_size in tile() and the resulting overread via tile_data with an oversized length. The other findings cover unrelated issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The APV CBS tile() read path skips 8*tile_data_size bits without checking get_bits_left. A crafted, oversized tile_data_size then causes heap out-of-bounds reads when tile_data is used downstream.
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT. It names the same function and line, the same attacker-controlled tile_data_size, the same skip_bits_long sink, and the same missing remaining-bits check. It also describes the downstream overread through tile_data/size. The PR diff confirms that the READ branch has no get_bits_left guard while the write branch has put_bytes_left. No mitigation is present.

criteria: Bitstream buffer is grown via av_fast_realloc in shorten_decode_frame after header parse
Zeroing is bounded by requested max_framesize values, not the actual allocated_bitstream_size
av_fast_realloc over-allocates slack that stays unzeroed
Later bitstream parsing (GetBitContext) reads those uninitialized bytes
judge.findings_summary: Flags uninitialized-heap reads in shorten_decode_frame. Cites the dropped padding memset and the new memset clearing only up to the requested max_framesize, which leaves av_fast_realloc slack unzeroed for GetBitContext to read.
judge.ground_truth_summary: After av_fast_realloc, the memset clears between old and new requested max_framesize instead of the actual allocated_bitstream_size delta. Over-allocated bytes stay uninitialized and are read during bitstream parsing.
judge.reasoning: The scanner's headline is the removed per-packet padding memset, but its causal chain says av_fast_realloc over-allocates slack and the new memset stops at the requested max_framesize+64. That leaves the growth tail uninitialized, and later reads hit it. This matches the GT mechanism of using requested sizes instead of allocated_bitstream_size. The PR code shows this flawed memset is still present, with no fix.

criteria: Padded buffer allocated via av_image_alloc (non-zeroed) for non-16-aligned width in dxv_encode
av_image_copy2 copies only width*bpp bytes per row
Right-edge memset boundary uses frame->linesize[0] (source stride) instead of true pixel data width
Bytes between width*bpp and frame->linesize/safe_linesize remain uninitialized
Uninitialized pad bytes are consumed by ff_texturedsp_exec_compress_threads and encoded into output
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: heap overflow from a negative memset length. Finding 2: memset uses frame stride instead of data width, so right-pad bytes stay uninitialized and are compressed into the packet.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dxv_encode clears horizontal padding using frame->linesize as the data/pad boundary instead of real pixel width, leaving freshly allocated bytes uninitialized that are then read by the DXT compressor (MSan).
judge.reasoning: Finding 2 matches the GT root cause. It names the non-zeroed av_image_alloc buffer and the memset that starts at frame->linesize[0] instead of width*4. It explains that this leaves the right padding uninitialized, and that the compressor reads those bytes over the aligned width. The PR diff contains this exact code, with no guard or fix.

criteria: Sink is the U8P sample-format conversion in osq_decode_block: av_clip_uint8(src[n] + 0x80)
Overflow happens in the 32-bit signed bias addition src[n] + 0x80 before the clamp runs
Trigger: decoded int32 samples near INT32_MAX coming from a malformed bitstream
Missing guard: no widening (int64 or unsigned) before the bias add, and no bound on src[n] before the addition
Must point to the output conversion path, not to the reconstruction or prediction arithmetic
judge.findings_summary: Reports unbounded rice_k OOB read, INT_MIN negation in get_srice, and int32 overflow in prediction and downsample in do_decode. None covers the U8P +0x80 bias addition.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In the U8P conversion, src[n] + 0x80 is computed in signed 32-bit int before av_clip_uint8, so values near INT32_MAX overflow (UB).
judge.reasoning: The PR code still contains av_clip_uint8(src[n] + 0x80) with no widening, so the GT bug is present. No scanner finding names this sink. Finding 3 covers signed overflow in the prediction and downsample code in do_decode, and mentions S32P/S16P output, not the U8P bias add. Finding 2 covers the negation in get_srice. Both are adjacent integer overflows in the same file with different sinks.

criteria: Source: ff_vvc_palette_escape_val made failable, returning negative AVERROR on malformed escape value
Sink: signed multiplication coeff * scale in palette_subblock_data (ctu.c ~2056)
