Missing guard: no upper bound or sanity cap is applied to ISIZE before the allocation
judge.findings_summary: One finding: TT SVG branch is missing the x/y ppem validation present in CFF, leading to possible wrong advance metrics via FT_MulDiv.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new SVG glyph-load call reaches tt_face_load_svg_doc, which trusts the gzip ISIZE trailer and passes it uncapped to FT_QALLOC, allowing huge allocations.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports that the TT SVG path lacks the ppem check that the CFF path has, and that FT_MulDiv can produce bad metrics. It never mentions tt_face_load_svg_doc's gzip ISIZE, the FT_QALLOC allocation, or the missing size cap. The finding is in the same function and the same SVG branch, but it describes a different sink and a different missing guard, so it is an adjacent issue rather than a match.

criteria: The new tag == 1 table-directory branch in tt_face_load_any is the vulnerable path
face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF is used directly as an index into face->ttc_header.offsets[]
No bounds check against ttc_header.count exists before the dereference
face_index can hold values that are not valid TTC subfont indices, causing an out-of-bounds read of offsets[]
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR snapshot and is not mitigated
judge.findings_summary: Reports an OOB heap read in tt_face_load_any (tag == 1): offsets[] is indexed by face_index & 0xFFFF without a ttc_header.count check. The example trigger is a negative face_index, and the finding notes that non-TTC faces have only one offset entry.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The tag == 1 table-directory access indexes ttc_header.offsets by face_index without a bounds check. face_index also enumerates non-TTC containers such as Mac Resource files, so the index can exceed the array and cause an OOB read.
judge.reasoning: The scanner flags the same sink, ttc_header.offsets[face_index & 0xFFFF] in the tag == 1 branch. It names the same missing guard (index < ttc_header.count) and the same fix. Its example trigger is a negative face_index, not the GT's Mac Resource container, but both are cases where face_index is not a valid TTC index. The PR diff shows the unchecked access and no mitigation.

criteria: Vulnerable operation is the multiplication (p->y - min_y) * target_height in af_latin_stretch_tilde's scaling loop
Bug class is signed integer overflow of FT_Pos (UB), not division by zero
Trigger is large or fuzzed glyph coordinates that make the product exceed the long range
Missing guard is the absence of bounds validation or a safe multiply (MUL_LONG/FT_MulDiv); the comment wrongly assumes the operands are small
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: division by zero in stretch_tilde when height==0, a broken edge_next circular list in segment removal, and a NULL dereference from af_find_highest_contour callers.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Signed overflow in (p->y - min_y) * target_height in af_latin_stretch_tilde. Fuzzed large coordinates overflow FT_Pos, and the code has no bounds check and does not use MUL_LONG.
judge.reasoning: The unguarded multiplication is present in the PR code. Scanner finding 1 targets the same scaling statement, but it describes division by zero when height==0. That is a different sink and a different trigger. No finding mentions overflow of the multiplication or large coordinates, and none questions the 'small numbers' assumption. The other findings cover a linked-list invariant break and a NULL dereference. This is a near match only.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Allocation of dists in sdf_generate_bounding_box uses FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, rows, width)
item_size argument is a raw byte count (width) instead of sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance)
Resulting buffer is rows*width bytes, undersized by a factor of sizeof(*dists)
Subsequent writes or reads of dists[index] for index < rows*width overflow the heap buffer
(Secondary) Code relies on dists being zero-initialized for its sign==0 sentinel check
judge.findings_summary: One IntegerOverflow finding at ftsdf.c:3284. It calls the FT_ALLOC_MULT change a correct, complete fix for the old rows*width overflow and states no new vulnerabilities exist.
judge.ground_truth_summary: FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, rows, width) allocates rows*width bytes, ignoring sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance). This produces an undersized heap buffer, so later dists[index] accesses cause a heap buffer overflow.
judge.reasoning: The vulnerable FT_ALLOC_MULT call is present in the PR. The scanner looked at this exact line but treated it as a correct integer-overflow fix and said no new vulnerabilities were introduced. It never noticed that width is passed as the item byte size instead of sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance). That missing element size is the actual root cause of the undersized allocation and overflow.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: a font-controlled last contour end index (zp2.contours[n_contours-1]) in the gep2==1 normal-zone branch of Ins_SHZ
The PR removes the BOUNDS check on the contour-derived value against zp2.n_points and replaces it with an unchecked limit = contours[last]+1
Sink: the loop for(i<limit) calls MOVE_Zp2_Point on zp2.cur/tags with indices that can reach or exceed n_points
Impact: an out-of-bounds heap read/write (buffer overflow), not just extra iterations or a defense-in-depth gap
No validation added elsewhere in the PR bounds limit to n_points
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: the removed BOUNDS check in Ins_SHZ gep2==1 is a defense-in-depth regression. It claims the buffer is large enough, so the impact is DoS amplification or future risk, not memory corruption.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Ins_SHZ derives limit from an unchecked font-controlled contours[last]+1 after the PR removed the BOUNDS check. The limit can exceed the point arrays, so MOVE_Zp2_Point overflows the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: The scanner points at the right place: the removed BOUNDS check and the unchecked contour-derived limit in Ins_SHZ. However, it classifies this as a LogicError and a defense-in-depth regression. It says the check is typically redundant and that the buffer is large enough to absorb the extra iterations. It frames the risk as DoS or future loader regressions. That explicitly denies the active out-of-bounds overflow in the ground truth.

criteria: Ins_SHZ computes the loop limit for the glyph zone (gep2 != 0) as exc->zp2.n_points - 4U
Unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge value when n_points < 4
The PR removed the prior guard (n_contours > 0 / last-contour limit, else 0)
The loop i < limit then drives out-of-bounds access to zp2.cur/tags via Move_Zp2_Point
judge.findings_summary: Unsigned underflow of n_points - 4U in Ins_SHZ for the glyph zone, giving a huge limit and an out-of-bounds read/write loop via Move_Zp2_Point. The finding notes the original n_contours guard was removed.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Commit 1803559c replaced the n_contours-based limit in Ins_SHZ with an unchecked n_points - 4U. This underflows when n_points < 4, so the loop overruns the zp2 arrays.
judge.reasoning: The scanner finding names the same trigger (n_points < 4 in the glyph zone), the same operation (n_points - 4U wrapping), the removed n_contours guard, and the same sink (the loop calling Move_Zp2_Point out of bounds). The PR diff shows the vulnerable code was added and that no new guard was introduced. The extra note about ttgload.c does not weaken the match.

criteria: Source: lookup indices come from hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups()/hb_set_next() and are not validated by HarfBuzz at collection time
Sink: those indices directly subscript globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[idx] in af_reverse_character_map_new
Missing guard: no bounds check against the allocated lookupCount, which AF_FaceGlobals does not track
Impact: an out-of-bounds heap read, and the garbage offset is then passed to af_map_lookup for further deref
judge.findings_summary: One finding: unbounded recursion in add_substitute() through long acyclic GSUB substitution chains, causing a stack overflow and denial of service.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Out-of-bounds read of gsub_lookups_single_alternate[] using unvalidated HarfBuzz lookup indices in af_reverse_character_map_new, with no tracked array length or bounds check.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff still contains the unchecked access globals->gsub_lookups_single_alternate[idx], so the GT bug is present. The scanner reports only unbounded recursion in add_substitute, which can cause a stack overflow. That finding has a different sink, a different trigger and a different bug class. It never mentions indexing by HarfBuzz lookup indices or the missing array-length bounds check, so it does not match the GT.

criteria: Location is TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas in src/truetype/ttgxvar.c, in the pooled allocation refactor
peak_coords_size = ALIGN_SIZE(3*num_axis) omits the sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier
The other pool sub-buffers do include their element sizes, so peak_coords is the only undersized region
Writes to peak_coords/im_start_coords/im_end_coords over 3*num_axis FT_Fixed elements overflow into adjacent pool regions or past the heap allocation
The vulnerable code is present in the evaluated PR diff with no fix
judge.findings_summary: One BufferOverflow finding: peak_coords_size is missing sizeof(FT_Fixed) in the pool computation of TT_Vary_Apply_Glyph_Deltas, causing heap overflow into later sub-buffers and beyond the pool.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The gvar pool refactor drops sizeof(FT_Fixed) from peak_coords_size, undersizing the first sub-buffer. Writes to the 3*num_axis coordinate arrays then overflow adjacent pool memory and the heap.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows peak_coords_size computed without sizeof(FT_Fixed) while the other four sizes include their element sizes. The scanner names this exact omission, the same function and line, and the same overflow chain: writes through peak_coords, im_start_coords and im_end_coords corrupt adjacent pool regions or overrun the heap buffer. Nothing in the PR mitigates it.

criteria: Source/trigger: attacker-controlled PBKDF2PARAM keylength parsed from an untrusted PKCS#12 PBMAC1 MAC structure
No check that keylength exists or is bounded (<= EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE) in PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC
Sink: PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC writes keylen bytes into the fixed key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] stack buffer in pkcs12_gen_mac
Reachable via PKCS12_verify_mac -> pkcs12_gen_mac -> PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC
Secondary: salt is used as an OCTET STRING without checking its ASN.1 type
judge.findings_summary: 7 findings. The keylength stack overflow and the salt type confusion match the GT. The rest cover adjacent issues: NULL prf, NULL hmac_md, iteration count, and app-level issues.
judge.ground_truth_summary: PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC trusts the parsed keylength and salt type. An oversized keylength overflows key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] in pkcs12_gen_mac via PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC. A salt that is not an OCTET STRING causes an invalid dereference.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain exactly: the unvalidated keylength flows into PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC and overflows the 64-byte key stack buffer in pkcs12_gen_mac. It also gives the correct verify path. Finding 4 covers the missing salt type check. The PR diff shows no bounds or type validation, so the vulnerability is active in the evaluated code.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled IV octet-string length from ASN.1 AEAD params (crafted CMS AuthEnvelopedData)
Two-step extraction: first asn1_type_get_octetstring_int call with NULL buffer returns length i
Missing guard: only i<=0 is checked, no check that i<=EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH
Sink: second call copies i bytes into stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH], i used as max_len, overflowing it
Location: evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params in crypto/evp/evp_lib.c, reachable before authentication
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a stack overflow in evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params because the attacker-controlled IV length is used as max_len for the second copy. Finding 5 raises a related IV-length issue. The other findings concern unrelated CMS NULL dereferences and a memory leak.
judge.ground_truth_summary: evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params gets the IV length via a NULL-buffer call and checks only i<=0. It then copies i bytes into the stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH], so a crafted CMS message overflows the stack.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows the root cause directly. After the length probe, the only check is i<=0, then asn1_type_get_octetstring_int(type,&tl,iv,i) copies i bytes into the 16-byte stack iv. Scanner finding 1 identifies this same source, the attacker-controlled length used as max_len in the second call, the same stack-buffer sink, and the same missing bound. It also gives the CMS_decrypt reachability path. No fix appears in the PR.

criteria: Vulnerable function is ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char in ssl/quic/quic_impl.c
Source: ssl3_get_cipher_by_char(p) can return NULL for unknown/unsupported cipher IDs
Sink: unconditional dereference ciph->algorithm2 on the returned pointer
Missing guard: no NULL check before the dereference
Trigger reachable via SSL_CIPHER_find on a QUIC SSL object with an unknown cipher ID, causing a crash (DoS)
judge.findings_summary: One NullPointerDereference finding in ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char. It reports that ssl3_get_cipher_by_char can return NULL and that ciph->algorithm2 is then dereferenced unchecked. The trigger is SSL_CIPHER_find with a QUIC object.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new QUIC function ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char dereferences the result of ssl3_get_cipher_by_char without a NULL check. Unknown cipher IDs from SSL_CIPHER_find therefore crash the process (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char, which dereferences ciph->algorithm2 without a NULL check. The scanner finding matches every part of the GT chain: the same source (NULL from ssl3_get_cipher_by_char for unmatched IDs), the same sink, the same missing guard, and the same trigger via SSL_CIPHER_find on QUIC. The line offset (3538 vs 3542) falls inside the same function. The PR adds no mitigation.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Location is apps/x509.c x509_main, in the OPT_ADDREJECT option handler
The handler pushes the parsed ASN1 object to the 'trust' stack instead of the 'reject' stack
The cause is a copy-paste error from OPT_ADDTRUST introduced by the sk_*_push return-check refactor
Impact: -addreject marks the certificate as trusted rather than rejected for the given purpose, inverting security policy
The flaw is present in the evaluated PR diff with no fix
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 correctly identifies the -addreject handler pushing to the trust stack, which inverts semantics. Finding 2 is an unrelated NULL dereference in a test file.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A copy-paste error in the x509 -addreject handler pushes rejected objects onto the trust stack, so certificates become trusted instead of rejected for that use.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the exact PR-introduced change: sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(reject, ...) became sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(trust, ...) in the OPT_ADDREJECT case. It traces the downstream X509_add1_trust_object effect and the inverted trust semantics. The diff confirms the bug and shows no fix. The line number differs slightly (460 vs 468), but the function and handler are the same.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: bmp_to_utf8 passes remaining UTF-16 source length (len, capped at 4) as UTF8_putc destination capacity
UTF8_putc returns -1 for BMP chars needing more UTF-8 bytes than remaining source bytes (e.g., >=U+0800 with 2 bytes left)
First (sizing) pass with NULL str succeeds/checks j<0, but second (writing) pass in OPENSSL_uni2utf8 lacks j<0 check
Negative j added to asclen, making it negative
NUL terminator write asctmp[asclen] writes before the heap buffer (underflow)
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: heap underflow in OPENSSL_uni2utf8 from missing bmp_to_utf8 failure check in second loop, giving asctmp[-1] write. Finding 2: unrelated memory leak in PKCS12_key_gen_utf8.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bmp_to_utf8 passes source length as UTF8_putc capacity, so it returns -1 for 3-byte BMP chars. The unchecked second pass in OPENSSL_uni2utf8 makes asclen negative, and the NUL write lands before the buffer.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT chain exactly. It identifies len misused as capacity (unilen-i capped at 4), the UTF8_putc failure for 3-byte BMP chars, and the missing j<0 check in the second loop. It also covers the negative asclen and the asctmp[-1] write, with a concrete U+4E2D example. The PR diff shows this code with no guard, so the vulnerability is present.

criteria: Source: attacker-controlled signed attribute (signingCertificate/V2) taken from a PKCS7/TS signer info
Sink: attr->value.sequence dereferenced in ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get / ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get
Missing guard: no check that attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE before reading the union member
Impact: type confusion leads to an invalid/NULL pointer dereference and a DoS crash during TS response verification
judge.findings_summary: The scanner reported two issues: freeing an uninitialized pp in the CMS_add1_signing_cert* functions, and an uninitialized digest buffer in ESS_CERT_ID_new_init. Neither involves ASN1_TYPE type validation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get access the ASN1_TYPE union member value.sequence without checking type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE. A malformed TS response can exploit this type confusion to crash the process.
judge.reasoning: The PR code still has the vulnerability: ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get read attr->value.sequence without checking the type. Neither scanner finding covers this. One reports freeing an uninitialized pointer in cms_ess.c. The other reports an unchecked X509_digest result in ESS_CERT_ID_new_init. Both are different bugs on different code paths, so the GT is not detected.

criteria: Vulnerability is in kek_unwrap_key in crypto/cms/cms_pwri.c
Length byte tmp[0] comes from decrypted attacker-influenced wrapped key data
Bounds check `inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0] - 4)` is incorrect (wrong arithmetic/direction, should require inlen >= 4 + tmp[0])
memcpy(out, tmp + 4, tmp[0]) then reads past the end of tmp and/or writes past the end of out
No guard in the PR code corrects the bound before the memcpy
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: heap OOB read/write in kek_unwrap_key from the wrong tmp[0] bound before memcpy. Also reported: NULL derefs in pwri_crypt and a double-free on push failure.
judge.ground_truth_summary: kek_unwrap_key's bound `inlen < tmp[0]-4` is wrong and can underflow. The memcpy of tmp[0] bytes from tmp+4 then reads past tmp and writes past out.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT root cause. It names the flawed check `inlen < (size_t)(tmp[0]-4)`, the correct requirement `inlen >= 4+tmp[0]`, and the memcpy sink. It also gives the same impact: up to 8 bytes of out-of-bounds read on tmp and 4 bytes of out-of-bounds write on out. The PR code still contains the flaw, with no fix. Findings 2 and 3 are unrelated but do not detract.

criteria: Trigger: server host given as a bracketed IPv6 address '[...]' in use_proxy()
Operation: strncpy(host, server+1, sl) into stack buffer host[NI_MAXHOST] copies exactly sl bytes
Missing guard: no NUL terminator written at host[sl] after strncpy
Sink: server reassigned to host and used as a C string in strstr(no_proxy, server), reading past valid data/buffer bounds
Code evidence: the PR adds the strncpy without termination and no later fix is present
judge.findings_summary: One finding: use_proxy strncpy of a bracketed IPv6 host into host[] lacks a NUL terminator. strstr(no_proxy, host) then reads past the copied data into uninitialized stack memory.
judge.ground_truth_summary: use_proxy strips IPv6 brackets with strncpy, which leaves host unterminated. strstr(no_proxy, server=host) then reads out of bounds, which can crash the process (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds strncpy(host, server+1, sl) with no host[sl]='\0', and then passes host to strstr. The scanner names this exact trigger, operation, missing terminator and strstr sink. Labelling it UninitializedMemory instead of OutOfBoundsRead does not change the root cause. The over-read past the stack buffer is the same flaw. Its line is 261 rather than 269, which is close enough.

criteria: Partial first-block pre-processing path in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc/dec (num != 0, left = min(16-num, len))
Unmasked vmovdqu8 loads ((%r11) iv+num and/or ($inp)) always read 16 bytes
Mask k1 for valid bytes exists but is applied only to stores, not to the pre-processing loads
Result is a read of 1-15 bytes past the valid buffer, which can fault at a page boundary (DoS)
Contrast: post-processing correctly uses {%k1}{z} masked loads
judge.findings_summary: Findings 1 and 3 flag unmasked 16-byte vmovdqu8 loads of the IV and input in partial-block pre-processing of enc/dec as OOB reads, recommending {%k1}{z}. Finding 2 is an unrelated num signedness issue.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Partial-block pre-processing in the AVX-512 CFB enc/dec uses unmasked vmovdqu8 loads that read 16 bytes regardless of the valid length, causing an OOB read and possible crash. Post-processing correctly uses masked loads.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows unmasked vmovdqu8 (%r11),%xmm0 and vmovdqu8 ($inp),%xmm1 in the pre-processing paths of both enc and dec. k1 is applied only to the stores. Scanner findings 3 (input) and 1 (IV) identify exactly these loads, the missing {%k1}{z} masking, page-fault DoS risk, and both functions. The fix they propose matches the GT. Nothing in the PR mitigates this.

criteria: Vulnerable function is check_delta_base in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c (delta CRL/base compatibility check)
Guards exist for delta->base_crl_number and base->crl_number, but none for delta->crl_number
Sink: ASN1_INTEGER_cmp(delta->crl_number, base->crl_number) dereferences a NULL first argument
Trigger: malformed delta CRL with the Delta CRL Indicator extension but no CRL Number extension, reachable via get_delta_sk when X509_V_FLAG_USE_DELTAS is set
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1 reports a NULL dereference of delta->crl_number in check_delta_base via ASN1_INTEGER_cmp for a delta CRL lacking a CRL number. The other findings cover delta time checks, critical-extension handling and delta selection.
judge.ground_truth_summary: check_delta_base checks base_crl_number and base->crl_number but not delta->crl_number. A crafted delta CRL without a CRL Number extension causes a NULL dereference in ASN1_INTEGER_cmp when use-deltas is enabled.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names check_delta_base, the missing delta->crl_number NULL check, and the ASN1_INTEGER_cmp sink. It also gives the same trigger: a delta indicator extension without a CRL number. The PR diff shows only base_crl_number and base->crl_number are guarded before that call. Nothing in the PR mitigates this; get_delta_sk calls check_delta_base on every CRL in the stack without filtering on EXFLAG_INVALID.

criteria: Source/trigger: attacker-supplied CMS KeyAgreeRecipientInfo whose optional keyEncryptionAlgorithm parameters field is absent
Sink: direct dereference of alg->parameter (->type / ->value.sequence) in dh_cms_set_shared_info (or the ECDH equivalent)
Missing guard: no NULL check on alg->parameter before the dereference
Reachable on the decrypt path via dh_cms_decrypt -> dh_cms_set_shared_info, causing a crash/DoS
Evaluated PR code still contains the unguarded dereference
judge.findings_summary: Nine findings in DH CMS/pmeth code. Finding #4 flags the missing NULL check on alg->parameter in dh_cms_set_shared_info at line 763. The others are adjacent issues: uninitialized variable, logic bugs, malloc and other NULL checks.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dh_cms_set_shared_info (and the ECDH counterparts) dereference alg->parameter without a NULL check. The parameters field is optional, so a crafted CMS KARI message passed to CMS_decrypt causes a NULL dereference and DoS.
judge.reasoning: Finding #4 matches the GT. It names the same function and line (dh_ameth.c:763) and the same unchecked alg->parameter->type dereference. It gives the same trigger, an omitted OPTIONAL KARI parameters field, and the same decrypt-path reachability. The PR diff adds the unguarded dereference with no NULL check. Finding #9 concerns kekalg->parameter, which is an adjacent issue, but #4 alone is sufficient.

criteria: Allocation size is computed as buflen*3 or 1+buflen*2 in openssl_buf2hexstr_sep
The multiplication has no overflow check and can wrap on 32-bit size_t
The wrapped size makes OPENSSL_malloc allocate an undersized buffer
buf2hexstr_sep then writes past that allocation (heap overflow), reachable via large attacker-controlled input such as a cert OCTET STRING
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: ebcdic2ascii length q-str-1 skips converting the last hex digit on EBCDIC platforms after the PR's --q change.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unchecked buflen*3 or 1+buflen*2 in openssl_buf2hexstr_sep can wrap on 32-bit platforms, giving an undersized malloc that buf2hexstr_sep then overflows on the heap.
judge.reasoning: The PR code still has the unchecked buflen*3 and 1+buflen*2 allocation sizes, so the GT overflow chain is present. The scanner's only finding is an EBCDIC off-by-one character-conversion logic error in buf2hexstr_sep. It does not mention integer overflow, an undersized allocation, or a heap write past the buffer. It hits the same function but describes a different bug, so it is not a detection.

criteria: Trigger: validate_addr==0 path sets qrx_src=qrx; qrx=NULL after initial-packet validation
Second unconditional 'qrx_src = qrx; qrx = NULL' in token-validation fallback overwrites qrx_src with NULL (missing NULL check)

judge.findings_summary: One finding: an RXE ends up in both the source QRX rx_free list and the destination QRX rx_pending list through ossl_qrx_inject_pkt, causing UAF/double-free when qrx_src is freed.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A second unconditional qrx_src=qrx assignment, made after qrx is already NULL, nulls the saved QRX pointer. ossl_qrx_read_pkt(NULL) is then called in the salvage loop, crashing the server.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff still contains the vulnerable chain: the second assignment unconditionally overwrites qrx_src with NULL, and the salvage loop then reads from it. The scanner instead reports a use-after-free/double-free caused by RXE list ownership in ossl_qrx_inject_pkt. It never mentions qrx_src being overwritten with NULL or the resulting NULL dereference. Same function, different bug, so not detected.

criteria: Identifies the explicit EVP_PKEY_CTX_ctrl_str(..., "rsa_pkcs1_implicit_rejection", "0") call in CMS/PKCS7 RSA key-transport decryption as the flaw
Recognizes that disabling implicit rejection removes the Bleichenbacher countermeasure for PKCS#1 v1.5
Explains that this restores a distinguishable padding success/failure oracle that attacker-crafted RecipientInfos can probe
Attributes the root cause to the CMS/PKCS7 layer depending on RSA decrypt success/failure for recipient matching, instead of fixing that logic
Treats the disablement itself as harmful, not as an intended behavior that might fail to apply
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: an unchecked ctrl_str return value in cms_env.c, a missing legacy ctrl_str handler meaning implicit rejection may stay enabled, and documentation macro-name and typo issues. None flags the Bleichenbacher oracle.
judge.ground_truth_summary: CMS/PKCS7 decryption explicitly disables RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 implicit rejection for internal control-flow convenience. This reopens a Bleichenbacher padding oracle against the recipient's RSA private key.
judge.reasoning: The PR code does disable implicit rejection, so the vulnerability is present. However, finding 1 only flags the unchecked return value of the ctrl call. Finding 2 complains that the disablement may not take effect in legacy mode. Both treat disabling as the intended, correct behavior. Neither identifies the Bleichenbacher oracle reintroduced by turning off the mitigation. Finding 2 effectively argues the opposite of the GT.

criteria: Location is selfsigned_verify_cb() in crypto/cmp/cmp_genm.c, in the custom chain-building path for DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT
X509_add_cert() is passed 'cert' where it should be passed the trusted 'issuer' found via check_issued
The result is a wrong chain: the trust anchor is never appended, so the issuer signature is not verified against the real issuer key
Impact: an attacker-supplied newWithOld/newWithNew rootCaKeyUpdate cert is accepted as a trust anchor without a valid cryptographic link to the old root
judge.findings_summary: Two NULL pointer dereference findings: X509_STORE_get0_param on a NULL ctx->trusted in verify_ss_cert_trans, and a NULL rootCaKeyUpdate union member in OSSL_CMP_ITAV_get0_rootCaKeyUpdate.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In selfsigned_verify_cb, X509_add_cert adds 'cert' instead of 'issuer' to the chain. This breaks verification of the self-signed rootCaKeyUpdate cert and lets an attacker-supplied root CA be accepted.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff still contains X509_add_cert(chain, cert, ...) inside the check_issued loop, so the GT bug is present. Neither scanner finding matches it. Finding 1 is a NULL trust-store dereference in verify_ss_cert_trans. Finding 2 is a NULL dereference in the cmp_asn.c getter. Both are different sinks and bug classes, and neither mentions the wrong-cert chain addition or the signature-verification bypass.

criteria: validate_email_name in crypto/x509/x509_vpm.c computes local_len as len - (at - name) instead of at - name
The wrong local_len means the 64-octet local-part limit is not enforced on the actual local part
The wrong lengths propagate to later reads on the caller buffer (validate_local_part/memchr/validate_hostname_part)
Attacker-controlled email input via X509_VERIFY_PARAM set1/add1 email APIs reaches this validation and causes an out-of-bounds read
judge.findings_summary: Five findings. Two describe the wrong local_len arithmetic in validate_email_name, causing a skipped local-part size check and an OOB read via dns_len. The others cover email bypass logic, NULL ordering in the get0_ip helper, and documentation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: validate_email_name computes local_len wrongly as len - (at - name) and passes the wrong length to validation helpers. This skips the local-part limit and causes an OOB read, reachable via the email APIs and S/MIME.
judge.reasoning: Findings 2 and 4 name the exact wrong expression local_len = len - (at - name), note the bypassed 64-octet check, and give the correct fix (at - name). They show the derived dns_len makes memchr and validate_hostname_part read past the buffer. The scanner does not mention the validate_local_part(name, len) misuse. That is a minor sink difference within the same root-cause chain. The PR code still contains the bug.

criteria: In ossl_synchronize_rcu, the next_to_retire increment, broadcast and unlock occur before the reader-count-zero wait loop.
The early signal lets the next waiting writer proceed before this writer's qp has been confirmed reader-free.
The racing writer calls retire_qp or reuses a qp slot in the rcu_qp ring that is still in use or not yet retired (the ring wraps when more than 3 QPs exist).
The impact is a use-after-free or double-retire on internal rcu_qp structures, not merely out-of-order API completion.
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: retire-in-order moved before the reader wait, so syncs complete out of order, labeled LogicError with no practical UAF. Finding 2: relaxed atomic ordering is informational only.
judge.ground_truth_summary: next_to_retire is signaled before qp readers drain, so a later writer can retire or reuse a qp slot still in use, causing a UAF or double-retire race on rcu_qp structures.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 identifies the exact reordering of the retire-in-order signal ahead of the reader drain, in both files. However, it places the consequence on caller-level resource ordering, not on reuse or retirement of internal rcu_qp slots. It also says current callers show no use-after-free and frames the issue as an API-contract regression for future callers. That makes the sink different and the impact hypothetical, so this is a near match.

criteria: Trigger: ossl_quic_wire_peek_frame_header() fails inside log_frame()
log_frame returns 0 without advancing the packet or setting *need_skip
Caller log_frames loop (while PACKET_remaining>0) handles failure via goto cont and re-iterates
Result: no progress on the same packet position, causing an infinite loop / DoS
judge.findings_summary: One finding: backwards comparison in the log_frames skip calculation (max instead of min) causes need_skip underflow and dropped QLOG frames after CRYPTO/STREAM frames.
judge.ground_truth_summary: log_frame returns 0 on peek_frame_header failure without advancing pkt or setting need_skip, so the log_frames while-loop spins forever on the same position (infinite loop/DoS).
judge.reasoning: The GT infinite loop is still present in the PR code: when peek_frame_header fails, log_frame returns 0 and the loop retries the same position forever. The scanner instead reports an inverted min/max comparison in the need_skip branch, causing over-advance, underflow and truncated logging. That is a different trigger and a different flaw in the same function. The scanner never mentions the peek failure or the non-terminating loop.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Vulnerable function is ossl_quic_get_peer_token in ssl/quic/quic_impl.c

It names the function, the NULL return from ossl_quic_build_new_token, the missing key NULL check, and the dereference in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve via the hash function. The PR diff confirms that key is used unchecked. It does not name the specific trigger (peer address not yet set), but the failure path it describes is the same source and sink.

criteria: Error branch after lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_insert checks lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_error in OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey
That branch runs after CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(cache->lock) has been acquired
The branch does 'goto err', and the shared err label does not call CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(cache->lock)
Result: the function returns with the write lock still held, so later lock attempts deadlock or fail
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: the insert-error path in OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey jumps to err without CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(cache->lock), leaking the write lock and causing deadlock.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_error check does 'goto err' after the write lock is taken. The err cleanup never releases cache->lock, so the lock is leaked.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds a 'goto err' after the hashtable-insert error check, while the write lock is held. The err path frees newcache and ctx but never unlocks. The scanner names this exact path, the missing unlock, and the resulting lock leak and deadlock. Nothing in the PR releases the lock on this path.

criteria: hashValue is declared OPTIONAL (ASN1_OPT) in the OSSL_HASH template, so the decoder can leave it NULL
i2r_HASH dereferences hash->hashValue->data/length without a NULL check
Trigger: crafted cert/CRL attributeDescriptor extension whose HASH omits hashValue, reached via extension printing
Sink: the print_hex call in i2r_HASH at lines 86-88 of crypto/x509/v3_attrdesc.c
No guard is added in the evaluated PR code

judge.ground_truth_summary: i2r_HASH in v3_attrdesc.c dereferences the OPTIONAL hash->hashValue without a NULL check. A crafted CRL or certificate that omits it crashes extension printing (found by OSS-Fuzz).
judge.reasoning: The scanner finding names the same optional hashValue as the source and the same unguarded dereference in i2r_HASH (print_hex at line 88) as the sink. It describes the same trigger: a crafted extension that omits hashValue and is reached through extension printing. The PR diff confirms the code is unguarded. The finding's line 67 is the function start, but it explicitly cites line 88.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Source: certificate-controlled notAfter ASN1_TIME data fetched via ASN1_STRING_get0_data()

Vulnerable code is added by the evaluated PR diff and no fix is present

The finding explains that ASN1 data has no NUL-termination contract, that DER decoding can produce unterminated buffers, and that strcmp can therefore read past the allocation. It recommends a length check with memcmp. The diff shows no mitigation, so the vulnerable chain is present.

criteria: Post-operation BIO_CB_RETURN callback in BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg passes NULL for processed out-parameter

bio_call_callback legacy-callback branch dereferences *processed when inret>0 and oper has BIO_CB_RETURN (non-CTRL)

criteria: ctx->length is 0 because EVP_DecodeInit set it, so the context was initialized for decoding but is then used for encoding
The zero-length context reaches the encoder through the BIO layer (b64_ctrl -> EVP_EncodeFinal)
The sink is the '% ctx->length' modulo in evp_encodeblock_int in enc_b64_scalar.c (lines 231/252/269)
The new scalar encoder has no guard that ctx->length is non-zero before the modulo
The result is a division-by-zero crash (SIGFPE)

judge.reasoning: Finding 2 reports a division by zero when ctx->length is 0, but at a different sink: 'inl % ctx->length' in EVP_EncodeUpdate. It also names a different trigger: a zero-initialized EVP_ENCODE_CTX_new context, or direct field writes in tests. criteria: Early CCS is buffered via has_change_cipher_spec=1 and goto redo in dtls_get_reassembled_message
No check that the current record buffer is fully consumed (trailing data) before the cipher state change
Delivering the buffered CCS triggers ssl_set_new_record_layer, which frees the old record buffer via ossl_tls_buffer_release
Dangling pointers to trailing record data are later dereferenced in dtls1_read_bytes, causing a heap use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError 'general safety analysis' on dtls_ccs_expected that calls the PR safe. It notes only state-list maintenance and leftover-flag concerns. No actionable security issues reported.

judge.reasoning: The PR diff still contains the vulnerable buffering path, with no check for trailing record data before the cipher change. The scanner's only finding judges the PR correct and security-positive and reports no vulnerabilities. It never mentions trailing record data, freeing the record layer, dangling pointers, or a use-after-free. This contradicts the GT and does not match it.

criteria: lua_close() is called in freeLuaScriptsSync/luaEngineFreeCtx without a prior explicit full GC (lua_gc LUA_GCCOLLECT)
lua_close() internally runs __gc finalizers on live userdata created by attacker-controlled scripts
The finalizers run after Redis has already released or invalidated related state, causing a use-after-free
The finding identifies the missing pre-close GC flush as the root cause and treats it as an active memory-safety bug
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: malloc_trim arena logic, stale lua_scripts_mem, async threshold gating, malloc.h _GNU_SOURCE include, and a hedged thread-safety note about __gc finalizers in lua_close on the BIO thread.
judge.ground_truth_summary: lua_close() is called without an explicit prior GC in freeLuaScriptsSync and luaEngineFreeCtx. Its __gc finalizers then run on freed or inconsistent Redis state, causing a use-after-free. The fix is lua_gc(LUA_GCCOLLECT) before lua_close.
judge.reasoning: The PR code calls lua_close() without a prior GC flush, so the GT chain is present. Finding 5 notes that lua_close runs __gc finalizers, but frames this as a thread-safety and contract concern on the BIO thread. It says it is 'not necessarily a defect today' and points to future modules. It never identifies a use-after-free on freed Redis state or the missing lua_gc call. The other findings are unrelated logic and build issues.

criteria: Source: user-supplied filepath from argv in redis_check_aof_main
Sink: memcpy into fixed-size stack buffer temp_filepath[PATH_MAX+1]
Missing guard: no check that strlen(filepath) <= PATH_MAX before copy
Impact: stack buffer overflow (attacker-controlled length) before dirname()
Vulnerable code present in evaluated PR snapshot without mitigation
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: stack overflow via unchecked memcpy of argv filepath into temp_filepath, plus a missing NUL terminator. Finding 2: FILE leak in checkSingleAof when the AOF is empty.
judge.ground_truth_summary: redis_check_aof_main memcpy's a user-supplied filepath into the PATH_MAX+1 stack buffer temp_filepath without a length check, causing a stack buffer overflow.
judge.reasoning: Scanner finding 1 matches the GT exactly. It names the argv filepath as the source and memcpy into temp_filepath[PATH_MAX+1] at lines 524/557 as the sink. It identifies the missing length validation as the cause and reports a stack overflow. The PR diff shows the unchecked memcpy, and nothing in the PR mitigates it. The extra note about the missing NUL terminator is additional, not contradictory.

criteria: Sandbox allow-list (lua_builtins_allow_list) permits environment-manipulation builtins getfenv/setfenv
Untrusted script can get or replace the environment of functions belonging to other execution contexts
Exposure negates the global-table readonly lock and enables code execution under another user's context
Related path: metatables of basic types are left unprotected by the recursive protection in scriptingInit/luaEngineInitEngine
judge.findings_summary: One finding: luaEngineCreate restores readonly on LUA_GLOBALSINDEX instead of the metatable, so the globals metatable stays mutable after FUNCTION LOAD.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The allow-list keeps getfenv/setfenv, letting scripts manipulate function environments and bypass the global-table lock. Basic-type metatables are also left unprotected.
judge.reasoning: The scanner reports that luaEngineCreate re-enables readonly on the wrong stack index, leaving the globals metatable writable. That is a different trigger and a different missing guard. The finding never mentions getfenv/setfenv being on the allow-list. It also does not cover the unprotected basic-type metatables. Same file family and broad sandbox-bypass class, but a different root cause, so this is an adjacent issue rather than the GT.

criteria: Location is src/blocked.c unblockClientOnKey, where a blocked client's pending command is re-executed
processCommandAndResetClient(c) can free/evict the client and return C_ERR
Return value is not checked before further use of c
Freed client c is then accessed (flags read, moduleCallCommandUnblockedHandler/queueClientForReprocessing, afterCommand) causing use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: CMD_CALL_REPROCESSING and CMD_CALL_FROM_MODULE share bit 2 in server.h, so RM_Call commands are hidden from MONITOR.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In unblockClientOnKey, processCommandAndResetClient may free the client, but its return value is unchecked. The code then reads flags, runs callbacks and calls afterCommand on the freed client, causing a use-after-free.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff shows the UAF chain is present: processCommandAndResetClient's return value is ignored, and c is used afterward for flag checks, callbacks and afterCommand. The scanner's only finding is about a flag-bit collision in server.h that hides RM_Call commands from MONITOR. That finding has a different file, mechanism and bug class. It does not address client eviction or the use-after-free.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Raw luaScript pointer `l` is cached from dictGetVal before luaCallFunction in evalGenericCommand
Active defrag runs during script execution (whileBlockedCron/defragWhileBlocked) and reallocates luaScript via activeDefragLuaScript
Cached pointer is not refreshed after script execution
Post-execution dereference of `l->node` for LRU bookkeeping touches freed memory (UAF)
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError finding: SCRIPT LOAD scripts bypass the 500-entry LRU eviction, allowing unbounded memory growth (DoS).
judge.ground_truth_summary: evalGenericCommand caches luaScript* l before script execution. Active defrag may reallocate the struct during execution, so the later l->node LRU access is a use-after-free.
judge.reasoning: The PR evidence supports the GT chain: the stale `l` is dereferenced via `l->node` after luaCallFunction, and defrag can reallocate the luaScript during execution. The scanner's only finding is a different issue: SCRIPT LOAD scripts are excluded from LRU eviction, which allows unbounded memory growth. It does not mention the stale pointer, defrag reallocation, or a use-after-free, so it does not match the GT root cause.

criteria: In readSyncBulkPayload's diskless non-SWAPDB path, functions_lib_ctx is captured via functionsLibCtxGetCurrent() before emptyData() runs
emptyData() frees and replaces the current functions library context when not in SWAPDB mode
The stale functions_lib_ctx pointer is then passed in loadingCtx to rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx and dereferenced (use-after-free)
Root cause is the reordering of emptyData() to after the pointer capture
judge.findings_summary: Twelve findings on AOF retry exits, the discardTempDb callback removal, module loading-event ordering, and a non-issue dangling conn pointer. None identifies the functions_lib_ctx use-after-free.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In diskless non-SWAPDB replica load, functions_lib_ctx is captured before emptyData(), which frees and replaces the functions context. The dangling pointer is then used during RDB function loading, a use-after-free introduced by the reorder.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff confirms the bug is present: functions_lib_ctx is fetched, then emptyData() runs, then loadingCtx uses the stale pointer. No scanner finding mentions functions_lib_ctx or its lifetime across emptyData(). Finding 5 is labeled UseAfterFree, but it is about a dangling conn after cancelReplicationHandshake and concludes there is no issue. Findings 8 and 10 discuss emptyData ordering only in terms of module events.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Trigger: client sends a partial multibulk header (multibulklen>0, argc==0) and stays idle for more than 2 seconds
Incorrect guard: clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle checks only argc/argv and does not check multibulklen
State corruption: the cron frees argv, sets it to NULL and sets argv_len=0 while parsing is still in progress
Sink: processMultibulkBuffer resumes parsing, computes min(argv_len*2, ...)=0, calls zrealloc(NULL,0), then writes argv[argc] and crashes or corrupts memory
Code introduced by this PR, with no mitigation present
judge.findings_summary: Cron frees argv mid-multibulk parse because only argc is checked. Resumed parsing reallocates to zero size and writes argv, causing heap overflow or NULL dereference.
judge.ground_truth_summary: clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle ignores multibulklen and frees argv mid-parse. processMultibulkBuffer later reallocates to 0 bytes, leaving argv NULL, and writing argv[argc] dereferences NULL.
judge.reasoning: The scanner names the same trigger: a partial multibulk header followed by a >2s pause. It names the same missing multibulklen check in clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle, the same argv=NULL/argv_len=0 state, and the same zero-size realloc in processMultibulkBuffer followed by the argv write. It labels the issue a buffer overflow but explicitly describes the NULL dereference. The PR diff confirms the guard lacks the check and adds no fix.

criteria: IO thread calls lookupCommand->dictFind on server.commands concurrently with the main thread
dictFind reads the useStoredKeyApi bit-field of struct dict
Main thread performs a non-atomic RMW on the adjacent pauserehash bit-field (pause/resume rehashing during iteration)
Both bit-fields share one storage unit, so these accesses form a data race
The PR's offloading of lookupCommand to IO threads introduces this concurrency
judge.findings_summary: 1) UAF via dangling c->iolookedcmd after moduleUnregisterCommands frees commands. 2) force_full_rehash loop no-ops when resizing is forbidden, leaving the dict half-rehashed.
judge.ground_truth_summary: IO-thread lookupCommand->dictFind reads the useStoredKeyApi bit-field while the main thread RMWs pauserehash in the same storage word, a data race introduced by offloading the lookup.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 shares the GT location but describes a use-after-free: a stale iolookedcmd pointer survives module unload. Finding 2 is a rehash logic error under DICT_RESIZE_FORBID. Neither finding identifies the shared-word bit-field race between pauserehash and useStoredKeyApi, or the main-thread RMW racing with the IO-thread dictFind read. Both are adjacent bugs, not the GT root cause.

criteria: Involves dbRandomKey() retry loop over volatile expired keys
expireIfNeeded() returns 1 without deleting when clients paused (new pause path)
maxtries safety guard gated only on server.masterhost, ignoring pause suppression
Primary (non-replica) under CLIENT PAUSE with all-volatile expired keys causes infinite loop/hang (DoS)
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: propagate() assert panic during Lua timeout plus CLIENT PAUSE; forceCommandPropagation assert reachable by modules; writes via MULTI/EXEC after a queued CLIENT PAUSE WRITE. None mention dbRandomKey or expire.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Client-pause expire suppression makes expireIfNeeded return 1 without deleting. dbRandomKey's maxtries break is gated on masterhost only, so a paused primary with all-expired volatile keys loops forever.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds the pause-driven early return in expireIfNeeded, and dbRandomKey's masterhost-only guard is not updated, so the GT chain is present. However, no scanner finding mentions dbRandomKey, expireIfNeeded, or the infinite loop. The findings cover a propagate() assertion under Lua timeout, a forceCommandPropagation assertion, and a MULTI/EXEC pause bypass. These are unrelated bugs in the same feature.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Loader path: rdbLoadObject reads minExpire for HASH_METADATA/HASH_LISTPACK_EX
Read failure detected via rioGetReadError after rdbLoadMillisecondTime
Error reported via rdbReportCorruptRDB (corruption_error=1) instead of rdbReportReadError
Diskless replication short read misclassified as corruption, leading to exit(1) on replica
judge.findings_summary: One finding: saving EB_EXPIRE_TIME_INVALID as 0 overloads the sentinel. It is a save-side future risk with no current impact.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new minExpire load code calls rdbReportCorruptRDB on a read error instead of rdbReportReadError. A network short read during diskless sync is then treated as corruption, and the replica exits.
judge.reasoning: The PR code still contains the GT bug: rdbReportCorruptRDB is used on read errors in both new load blocks. criteria: Location is dequantization_int_97() in libavcodec/jpeg2000dec.c

criteria: Error branch for an uncommon channel combination in decode_header (exr.c ~1836) assigns ret

criteria: payload_size from get_mb (uint64) stored or used in an int without range validation

criteria: Keys of AVTree nodes (poc, gop) are changed in place while the nodes are still linked in the tree

That is the fix, and in-place key mutation during enumeration is no longer present. The scanner findings cover adjacent issues: an assert abort on count overflow, integer overflow, and IDR initialization logic. None of them identifies in-place key mutation during enumeration.

criteria: Vulnerable sink is the binomial coefficient computation inside decode_tsd()

criteria: In decode_frame, the aligned coded_width/coded_height assignment comes before ff_set_dimensions()

criteria: Decoder.subtitle_header is assigned in dec_open from ist->dec_ctx->subtitle_header
The assignment is a shallow pointer alias with no buffer duplication

criteria: Search-or-allocate loop over c->heif_item[] matching item_id in mov_read_iloc/mov_read_infe

criteria: get_freq_strides() output buffer is ld->freq_res, sized MPS_MAX_PARAM_SETS (9) entries
Writes up to data_bands+1 (up to 29) entries, overflowing freq_res into adjacent struct fields

Missing guard: no check of these values against numBands derived from bsFreqRes

criteria: Ambient viewing environment struct (dst_env) is wrapped in an AVBufferRef and passed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext

criteria: Allocation of param via av_iamf_param_definition_alloc in param_parse

criteria: Location is escapeStringWin in devtools/client/shared/curl.js, in the caret-escape character class.

criteria: tt_face_load_any tag==1 path indexes face->ttc_header.offsets[] using face_index

criteria: Sink is the tilde-stretch rescaling multiplication (p->y - min_y) * target_height in af_latin_stretch_tilde

criteria: Set_High_Precision selects 12-bit precision (scale 64) when the High flag is set

criteria: Allocation of dists in sdf_generate_bounding_box uses FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, rows, width), treating width as raw byte item_size
Resulting buffer is rows*width bytes instead of sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance)*rows*width
Subsequent writes/reads of dists[index] (~12-byte elements) overflow the undersized heap buffer
Non-zeroed allocation causes uninitialized reads of dists[index].sign sentinel
Vulnerable allocation must be present in evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: One finding: possible divide-by-zero (SIGFPE) in the new overflow check `rows > FT_INT_MAX / width` when bitmap->width is 0, reached before the existing zero-size check.

So the GT undersized FT_ALLOC_MULT allocation is absent. The scanner reports a different issue: division by zero in the new guard when width==0. criteria: Sink is the per-point coordinate update in af_move_contour_vertically (point->y += movement)

Scanner finding 2 targets different operations: the distance and adjustment_amount subtractions in the caller, plus FT_Int narrowing of the movement parameter. It does not claim the point->y addition overflows. Finding 1 is a NULL dereference, which is unrelated. At best this is a near match in the same function family with a different sink.

criteria: Ins_SHZ glyph-zone (gep2==1) loop limit derived from font-controlled contours[n_contours-1]+1

criteria: Source: lookup indices from hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups/hb_set_next, driven by font data

criteria: Input is read into memory through a size-limited buffering helper (bio_to_mem) for one-shot sign/verify

criteria: In the OPT_ADDREJECT handler in apps/x509.c x509_main, the parsed object is pushed to the wrong stack (trust instead of reject)

The evaluated code must still push to 'trust' in the ADDREJECT case

The scanner's x509 finding is a different bug: objtmp leaks when the push fails. It never mentions pushing to the trust stack or the inverted policy. The other finding is in an unrelated file. Not detected.

criteria: Vulnerability is in the OCB encrypt/decrypt hardware-accelerated stream path (ctx->stream != NULL)
Stream branch processes full blocks without advancing the in/out pointers
Tail-handling code uses bare in/out pointers, assuming they were already advanced

The evaluated code must still lack pointer advancement in the stream branch

judge.reasoning: The PR adds processed_bytes = num_blocks*16 and advances in/out in both stream branches, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner's finding is a different issue: in-place aliasing in the partial-block checksum computation. It does not mention the missing pointer advancement in the stream path.

criteria: bmp_to_utf8 passes remaining UTF-16 source length as the UTF8_putc destination capacity
UTF8_putc returns -1 for a BMP char above U+07FF when only 2 source bytes remain
OPENSSL_uni2utf8 second (writing) pass adds the negative return to asclen with no check
The NUL terminator write at asctmp[asclen] lands before the heap buffer
judge.findings_summary: The scanner reports an integer overflow in utf82uni, a password leak in key_gen_utf8, lone-surrogate mishandling in bmp_to_utf8, and a negative-unilen OOB read in uni2utf8. None is the unchecked UTF8_putc -1 in the second pass.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bmp_to_utf8 misuses the source length as the UTF8_putc capacity, so it returns -1. uni2utf8's writing pass does not check this, asclen goes negative, and the NUL write lands before the heap buffer.

None of the scanner findings describe the len-as-capacity misuse or the unchecked negative return. Finding 4 covers a negative unilen read, and finding 3 covers surrogate handling. Both are adjacent bugs, not the GT chain.

criteria: Source is an attacker-controlled signed attribute (signingCertificate / signingCertificateV2) taken from a parsed PKCS7/TS response
Sink is a dereference of attr->value.sequence (->data/->length) in ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get or ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get
Missing guard: no check that attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE before the union access
Impact: a non-SEQUENCE ASN1_TYPE is interpreted as an ASN1_STRING, giving an invalid or NULL dereference and a DoS

criteria: Vulnerable sink is memcpy(out, tmp + 4, tmp[0]) in kek_unwrap_key
The guard on tmp[0] against inlen is incorrect: it is either inverted or uses tmp[0] - 4, which is off by 8 and underflows when tmp[0] < 4

The result is an out-of-bounds read of tmp and an out-of-bounds write of out
The flawed check must be present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: small-blocksize check-byte over-read, NULL parameter dereference, unchecked malloc, envelopedData type confusion, and kek_wrap_key short-key read. None identifies the inverted or underflowing length check.

Finding 1 is in the same function but blames a different root cause: cipher block size 1 and the check-byte reads of tmp[4..6]. It even quotes the corrected length check. criteria: use_proxy() strips brackets from an escaped IPv6 server string into a local host buffer using strncpy

server is reassigned to the unterminated host buffer
strstr(no_proxy, server) reads past the end of host while looking for a NUL (OOB read on host)
No explicit host[sl]='\0' termination is present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: One OOB-read finding: the "[]" server string becomes an empty needle, and the strstr loop then advances past the NUL terminator of no_proxy.

The scanner reports a different trigger: the empty host "[]" (sl==0), which makes the strstr loop walk past the end of no_proxy. criteria: Partial-block pre-processing path in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc/dec is the trigger (num != 0, left 1-15 bytes)

judge.findings_summary: Two findings: missing AVX512VL check in the eligibility function causing SIGILL, and a dead negative-num guard in the wrapper that could allow an OOB masked write if num is ever out of range.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unmasked vmovdqu8 loads in the partial-block pre-processing of the VAES CFB enc/dec routines read a full 16 bytes when fewer are valid, causing an out-of-bounds read and possible crash.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, both pre-processing loads already use masks: vmovdqu8 (%r11),%xmm0{%k1}{z} and vmovdqu8 ($inp),%xmm1{%k1}{z} in enc and dec. So the GT out-of-bounds read is fixed. Neither scanner finding covers unmasked loads. One reports a missing AVX512VL eligibility check (SIGILL). The other reports an unreachable negative-num guard that could cause an OOB write.

criteria: Source: a delta CRL that has the Delta CRL Indicator extension (base_crl_number) but no CRL Number extension (crl_number)
Sink: ASN1_INTEGER_cmp(delta->crl_number, base->crl_number) in check_delta_base

Reachable from get_delta_sk when X509_V_FLAG_USE_DELTAS is set
