criteria: Ambient viewing environment struct allocated and wrapped in AVBufferRef in h2645_sei_to_side_data
Buffer handed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext, which may take ownership of or free it
dst_env fields written AFTER that handoff call
Write to possibly freed or already-exposed memory (use-after-free)
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicError findings: decoded_side_data not cleared before appending, causing a spurious ENOMEM, and an unchecked update_context_from_thread return in init_thread. Neither is a UAF.
judge.ground_truth_summary: UAF in h2645_sei_to_side_data: AVAmbientViewingEnvironment fields were written after the buffer was handed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext, which may free or take ownership of it.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the dst_env fields are initialized before ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext is called, so the GT use-after-free chain is broken. Neither scanner finding addresses the ambient viewing environment write ordering or a use-after-free. Finding 1 is a logic error about pre-existing decoded_side_data. Finding 2 concerns an unchecked return value in pthread_frame.c.

criteria: Index computed as i - filt_w/2 + filt_i (or the j equivalent) in vif_filter1d near image edges
Boundary mirroring is a single-step reflection that fails when the overshoot exceeds the image dimension
Small image dimensions (h or w < filt_w/2) leave the index outside [0, dim-1]
OOB read happens at src[ii*src_stride+j] or temp[jj]
judge.findings_summary: 1) OOB read in offset_8bit/10bit when frame dimensions differ from the cached link size. 2) height*sizeof(float) overflow before the av_calloc call on 32-bit builds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Single-step index reflection in vif_filter1d fails for images smaller than filt_w/2. Indices stay out of range, causing OOB reads of src and temp. The evaluated PR fixes this with avpriv_mirror.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR replaces the single-step reflection with avpriv_mirror(), which mirrors indices repeatedly, so the GT causal chain is broken. No scanner finding targets the mirroring in vif_filter1d. One finding covers stale per-frame dimensions in offset_fn. The other covers allocation-size overflow in config_input_ref. Both use different triggers and sinks from the GT.

criteria: The energy array `en` in ff_aac_search_for_tns is undersized (2 elements) for the up-to-3-filter loop.
The trigger is n_filt=3, reached with long windows when order == TNS_MAX_ORDER (AAC Main profile).
The out-of-bounds operation is the direction computation reading en[g] or en[!g] with g=2.
No bound or array-size guard ensures the en indices stay below the array length.
A scanner finding must identify this stack out-of-bounds read on `en`.
judge.findings_summary: Three LogicError findings: NaN gain bypasses the TNS threshold check, the remainder branches of the ternaries are dead code, and TNS coefficient compression is enabled despite a stale comment. None concerns the en array bounds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unifying the TNS filter loop to support 3 filters kept `float en[2]`. With n_filt=3 (Main profile, long windows), the direction comparison reads en[2], a stack out-of-bounds read.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR declares `float en[4]` and uses en[g] < en[g+1]. With n_filt at most 3, the highest index read is en[3], which is in bounds, so the GT overflow is fixed. None of the scanner findings mention out-of-bounds access on `en`. They cover a NaN gain bypassing the threshold check, an unreachable remainder branch in the ternaries, and coefficient compression now being enabled. These are adjacent logic issues, not the GT chain.

criteria: avformat_free_context guards ff_flush_packet_queue() behind s->iformat
Muxer contexts (iformat NULL) skip the flush entirely
si->packet_buffer on FFFormatContext, filled by mux.c ff_interleave_add_packet, is therefore never freed
No separate free of packet_buffer exists outside the guarded call, so leftover interleave packets leak on muxer teardown
judge.findings_summary: Latent union aliasing/type-confusion hazard in ff_flush_packet_queue on muxer contexts. Acknowledges the iformat guard and the explicit packet_buffer free, and says no current path is vulnerable.
judge.ground_truth_summary: An overly broad iformat guard on ff_flush_packet_queue in avformat_free_context means muxer si->packet_buffer is never freed, leaking interleave-queue packets.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds an unconditional avpriv_packet_list_free(&si->packet_buffer) before the iformat-guarded flush, so muxer packet_buffer is freed and the GT leak is absent. The scanner reports a different issue: union type-confusion if ff_flush_packet_queue is ever called on a muxer. It admits current call sites are guarded, which makes this a future-risk concern. It also notes that the packet_buffer free exists, describing the fix rather than an active leak.

criteria: param is allocated via av_iamf_param_definition_alloc in param_parse
A subblock-duration sum check (total_duration != duration) returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA
That error path returns without calling av_free(param), leaking the allocation
Triggered by malformed IAMF input whose subblock durations do not sum to duration
The finding must report the missing free / memory leak on this specific path
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: integer wraparound bypass of the total_duration check, the check being trivially true when constant_subblock_duration is nonzero, and default_w mutated before validation. None report a leak.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new subblock-duration validation in param_parse returns AVERROR_INVALIDDATA without av_free(param), leaking the allocated param definition when malformed IAMF input is parsed.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the new duration-check path in param_parse calls av_free(param) before returning, so the GT leak is absent. No scanner finding reports a memory leak of param. The findings cover other issues instead: 32-bit wraparound bypassing the check, the check being a no-op for constant durations, and default_w being mutated before validation. Finding 3 even says param is freed on this path, which contradicts an active leak.

criteria: Trigger is an empty-string exprs value (e.g. aeval=:1) that is non-NULL

criteria: Trigger: JSObject::swap between a nursery object and a tenured object where the object has dynamic elements
Flawed guard: prepareForSwap copies element buffers only when they are physically inside the nursery (ChunkPtrIsInsideNursery) and ignores buffer-allocator nursery-ownership metadata
Result: the tenured object retains a buffer marked as nursery-owned, the next minor GC frees it, and a later access is a use-after-free
Secondary: the copy ignores shifted elements, using the shifted header for memmove and the newElements pointer
Code support: the evaluated code must still lack the ownership-based copy and the numShifted handling
judge.findings_summary: 1) Speculative stale pointer from tracing elements by value in traceChildren. 2) Major-GC marking now skips nursery-owned buffers, raising a hypothetical UAF if a store-buffer entry is missing.
judge.ground_truth_summary: prepareForSwap copied element buffers only when they were physically in the nursery, so tenured objects could hold nursery-owned buffers that minor GC frees (UAF). Shifted elements were also mishandled during the copy.
judge.reasoning: The PR snapshot already contains the fix. The code copies whenever IsInsideNursery(this) differs from IsInsideNursery(other), allocates with the correct ownership through AllocBuffer, copies from the unshifted header, and adds numShifted. Finding 1 is a speculative concern about traceChildren pointer relocation, which is an adjacent issue. Finding 2 is a future-invariant concern about marking and itself describes the new swap handling as intentional. Neither finding identifies the active GT chain.

criteria: ServiceWorkerContainer can live on a worker thread (exposed via WorkerNavigator.serviceWorker)

judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already uses NS_DispatchToCurrentThread in EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch, and DispatchMessage checks CheckCurrentGlobalCorrectness. That breaks the GT chain. None of the scanner findings address the wrong-thread dispatch. They cover a cycle-collection leak, a null-container risk guarded by a debug-only assert, and a principal substitution. All three are adjacent issues, not the GT race.

criteria: The startAt parameter delays emplaceBack into stackChain, so stackChain can be empty while frames are being walked

judge.reasoning: This PR adds '&& seenStartAt' to the reparenting condition, which blocks the GT trigger (startAt not yet seen). The scanner's main finding admits that guard exists. It instead describes a different trigger: the matched startAt frame is the only frame in its activation. That is an adjacent variant, not the GT causal chain, which is mitigated in this snapshot. Finding 2 is an unrelated MaxFrames logic issue.

criteria: mStylesheetDocument is a strong RefPtr that cycle collection traverses and unlinks
The CC Unlink clears mStylesheetDocument without first calling RemoveMutationObserver(this)
ImportStylesheet registers the processor as a mutation observer on the document via AddMutationObserver

judge.ground_truth_summary: The CC macro unlinks mStylesheetDocument without calling RemoveMutationObserver(this). The document keeps a dangling observer pointer to the freed processor, causing a use-after-free when the document is destroyed.
judge.reasoning: This is a benign task: the PR already contains the fix, so the GT use-after-free is absent. The scanner reports a different bug. It says mStylesheetDocument is missing from CC traverse/unlink, which would cause a reference-cycle memory leak. The GT bug is the opposite case: the field is unlinked without deregistering the mutation observer, which causes a use-after-free. The scanner names a different sink, a different missing guard and a different bug class.

criteria: Writer: EnsureLocale() on the main thread modifies the shared mLocale member
Missing guard: EnsureLocale has no idempotency or synchronization protection, so repeated calls can reassign or reallocate mLocale
Reader: GetLocale() reads mLocale on DOM worker threads via IDBFactory::OpenInternal

judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: a compromised content process sends an unvalidated system locale over PBackgroundIDBFactory IPC. The parent uses it for ICU collation and locale-aware index rewrites.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Non-idempotent, unsynchronized EnsureLocale writes mLocale from several main-thread callers while worker threads read it through GetLocale. This causes a data race or UAF. The benign PR adds an mLocaleInitialized guard.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds an mLocaleInitialized guard, so EnsureLocale writes mLocale only once, before workers read it. That idempotency check breaks the GT chain. The scanner instead reports a trust-boundary issue: a content-supplied locale reaches the parent-side Factory and ICU collation code. It never mentions a data race between EnsureLocale writes and worker-thread GetLocale reads. Different root cause and sink.

criteria: GetAction in AlertNotification.cpp returns an nsIAlertAction via a double-pointer out-param
The out-param is assigned a raw pointer (*aAlertAction = action) with no AddRef/forget

criteria: Main-thread code in nsHttpChannel::ContinueProcessResponse1 reads transaction connection info to pass to ProcessAltService
Read goes through unsynchronized nsHttpTransaction::GetConnInfo accessing mConnInfo without mLock
Concurrent socket-thread write to mConnInfo (DisableHttp3 swap) without synchronization

criteria: The vulnerable site is createManyLazyEntryStubs in js/src/wasm/WasmCode.cpp, where calleePtr is computed.
The wrong base is used: segment->base() instead of CodeBlock::base()/codeBase.
Code offsets are now relative to CodeBlock::codeBase, which can differ from segment->base() when several blocks share a segment.

The evaluated code must still use segment->base() at that site.
judge.findings_summary: One TypeConfusion finding: CodeBlock::base()/codeBase lost const-qualification on the executable memory pointer, a loss of defense-in-depth. It is not about the calleePtr base calculation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: createManyLazyEntryStubs used segment->base() instead of CodeBlock::base() after offsets became codeBase-relative. This yields a wrong calleePtr in lazy entry stubs. The evaluated PR has this fixed.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, createManyLazyEntryStubs already uses tierCodeBlock.base() to compute calleePtr, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner's only finding is a different issue: CodeBlock::base() now returns a non-const pointer, which it describes as a defense-in-depth or future-maintenance concern. It does not mention the wrong base in calleePtr. This is not the GT bug.

criteria: readAllocSiteIndex captures allocSitesPatches().length() as the index before calling masm.append

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, readAllocSiteIndex returns !masm.oom(), and every caller is [[nodiscard]] and returns false on failure before loadAllocSiteInstanceData runs. That breaks the GT chain. None of the scanner findings covers the unchecked append or the OOB index. The findings are a register leak, a weakened assert, and a Baseline/Ion dead-code index mismatch, all adjacent issues.

criteria: CachedBAxisMeasurement is stored as a DELETABLE heap property and accessed through a raw pointer
The pointer is obtained before parent->ReflowChild() and kept in a local variable
ReflowChild triggers MarkIntrinsicISizesDirty/MarkCachedGridMeasurementsDirty, which removes and frees the property

criteria: promoteString handles a dependent string whose root base (from rootBaseDuringMinorGC) is not in the collected nursery region
In that branch only forwardDependentString is called; setBase is never called to update d.s.u3.base
rootBaseDuringMinorGC can return a different string than the direct base (intermediate chain), so the base pointer goes stale

judge.ground_truth_summary: promoteString skipped setBase when the root base was outside the collected nursery. This left the dependent string's base pointer stale and caused a use-after-free during GC tracing.
judge.reasoning: The PR's promoteString calls setBase(promotedBase) unconditionally before forwardDependentString, and TraceWholeCell also calls setBase in the non-nursery branch. That removes the GT flaw. Finding 1 describes a different trigger: an untracked tenured D->T2->N3 chain with a stale chars pointer, plus a missing store-buffer registration. criteria: size_t numBytes is passed into AllocateCellBuffer, whose count parameter is uint32_t
numBytes can actually exceed UINT32_MAX on a reachable path (large Map/Set growth)
The truncation produces an undersized buffer allocation
Later writes or copies (rehash/getBufferParts layout) use the full size, causing a heap overflow
No effective bound keeps numBytes under 4GB before the narrowing
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: size_t-to-uint32_t truncation in allocateCellBuffer, explicitly called unreachable because of the MinHashShift gate (future risk only). Finding 2: release-mode-unchecked pointer rebasing in maybeMoveBufferOnPromotion.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Map/Set allocateCellBuffer passes size_t numBytes to AllocateCellBuffer, which takes uint32_t. Sizes over 4GB truncate, the buffer is undersized, and rehash then overflows the heap.
judge.reasoning: Finding 1 names the exact sink and the size_t-to-uint32_t truncation. However, the PR adds MinHashShift and MaxDataCapacity bounds, and rehash rejects newHashShift < MinHashShift. That keeps numBytes far below 4GB, which breaks the causal chain. The scanner itself says the bug is unreachable today and frames it only as a future-maintenance risk. Finding 2 is an unrelated pointer-rebasing concern.

criteria: TRRServiceChannel::OnStartRequest obtains transaction connection info for ProcessAltService

judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR's TRRServiceChannel::OnStartRequest uses TakeResponseHeadAndConnInfo(), which takes the lock, so the GT race is fixed here. Neither scanner finding mentions GetConnInfo, a missing lock, or a data race. One finding raises an ECH hash-key logic issue and the other raises IPC trust of conn info in Alt-Svc validation. Both are unrelated logic issues.

criteria: Trigger: rendering with present=false (offscreen) in UpdateAndRender

criteria: Trigger: FinalizationRegistry.prototype.unregister called with zero arguments
Sink: unchecked args[0] / CallArgs::operator[] index before argc is validated

criteria: Non-owning BytecodeSource raw pointer/length is captured from a user-supplied BufferSource
User-controllable JS (FeatureOptions::init on the options argument, e.g. a Proxy getter) runs after the pointer is captured
That JS can detach or transfer the buffer, freeing the backing store
The stale pointer is then dereferenced in Validate/CompileBuffer (WebAssembly_validate, Module construct, compile)

judge.findings_summary: Unpinned BytecodeSource in wasm::Eval, presented as hypothetical; a missing return in getOrCreateBuffer causing an extra copy; and a ShareableVector::fromSpan leak on OOM.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A raw BytecodeSource pointer is captured before FeatureOptions::init runs user JS that can detach the buffer. Validate/CompileBuffer then read freed memory in WebAssembly_validate and sibling paths.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already reorders the calls: FeatureOptions::init runs before GetBytecodeSource, and AutoPinBufferSourceLength protects Validate and CompileBuffer, so the GT chain is broken. criteria: Inline-data branch of StableWasmArrayObjectElements constructor copies array data into a Vector sized numElements_
std::copy source is byte-typed (uint8_t*) with a byte-count range (numElements_*sizeof(T)) while destination is T*
Iteration count mismatch writes sizeof(T)x more T elements than the destination holds (heap/stack OOB write)
Source pointer is inlineStorage() (includes DataHeader) instead of the array-data offset

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the inline branch uses inlineArrayElements<T>() with a T-typed range of numElements_, so there is no element/byte mismatch and the GT overflow is absent. criteria: Vulnerable code is the escapeStringWin caret-escape allow-list in devtools/client/shared/curl.js
The root cause is the `\s` shorthand in the allow-list, which lets tab, VT, FF and Unicode whitespace pass unescaped
Those whitespace or control characters act as argument or token separators in cmd.exe or the CRT argv parser
Attacker-controlled request data (URL, headers, body) can then inject extra arguments into the copied curl command
No later normalization replaces non-space whitespace before output
judge.findings_summary: Two LogicErrors in escapeStringWin. First, the `"`→`""` doubling desynchronizes quotes under the MS CRT parser. Second, `&` in the allow-list is left unescaped as a cmd.exe command separator.
judge.ground_truth_summary: escapeStringWin's allow-list uses `\s`, so tab, VT, FF and Unicode whitespace pass unescaped and split arguments, enabling curl command injection via Copy as cURL (Windows).
judge.reasoning: The PR adds `.replace(/[^\S\r\n]/g, " ")`, which turns all non-newline whitespace into a plain space. That breaks the GT causal chain, so the vulnerability is not present. The scanner's findings are also different bugs: one is about quote-doubling parity with the MS CRT parser, the other about `&` being allow-listed. Neither identifies `\s` letting whitespace control characters through as argument separators. These are only adjacent issues in the same function.

criteria: MGuardShape::foldsTo folds an outer guard into an inner GuardShape testing the same shape
No check that both guards share the same alias-set dependency()
An intervening shape-mutating effect can occur between the two guards
Folding leaves stale shape/slot-layout assumptions, leading to layout or type confusion
judge.findings_summary: One TypeConfusion finding: MGuardShape::foldsTo relies on dependency() equality without a dominance check, so loops or OSR might allow an unsound fold. Explicitly flagged as unproven and needing review.
judge.ground_truth_summary: MGuardShape::foldsTo folded same-shape nested guards without checking alias dependency(), so intervening shape mutations could leave stale shape assumptions and cause object layout confusion.
judge.reasoning: The PR's foldsTo already requires dependency() to be non-null and object()->dependency()==dependency(). That is the exact missing check named in the GT, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner sees this check and instead speculates about a different missing guard, a dominance check across loops/OSR. It labels this unproven and suspicious. That is an adjacent, hypothetical concern, not the GT root cause.

criteria: NukeCrossCompartmentWrappers skips nuking CCWs whose target is a DebuggerInstanceObject
AllowNewWrapper lacks the matching DebuggerInstanceObject exception and blocks new wrappers into nuked compartments/realms

judge.ground_truth_summary: Debugger CCWs were exempted from nuking, but AllowNewWrapper still blocked creating new ones. This mismatch broke Compartment::wrap invariants and caused a use-after-free.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds the DebuggerInstanceObject exception to AllowNewWrapper, so nuke and create rules are now symmetric and the GT chain is broken. Finding 1 treats that exemption itself as a security-isolation weakness, which is a different issue. Finding 2 concerns singular NukeCrossCompartmentWrapper paths and removed tracing, an adjacent hypothetical future risk. Neither finding describes the asymmetric AllowNewWrapper gap.

criteria: Object.keys iteration (LoadIteratorElement) is routed into the iterator-indices indexed-slot fast path in OptimizeIteratorIndices
Iterator cache/enumeration path (GetIteratorImpl) can reuse or enumerate prototype properties, so Object.keys iterators are not enforced as own-properties-only
A Proxy on the prototype chain runs script (trap) during enumeration, a side effect the JIT fast path does not account for

judge.findings_summary: Three findings: no bounds check in extractIndexAndKindFromIteratorByIterIndex, cross-object iterator index reuse in OptimizeIteratorIndices, and removed isReusable asserts in the Object.keys fast paths. All are speculative and none mention Proxy side effects.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The Object.keys iterator-indices JIT fast path assumes no prototype side effects, but the iterator cache/enumeration did not enforce own-only. A Proxy trap on the prototype runs script, which can invalidate a reused bounds check.
judge.reasoning: This is a benign snapshot. The PR adds JSITER_OWNONLY for Object.keys, an OwnPropertiesOnly flag, and recreation of cached iterators, which breaks the GT chain. No scanner finding names the Proxy-trap side effect or prototype enumeration as the trigger. criteria: Same-thread fast path in atomics_notify_impl resolves the waitAsync promise directly (waiter->cx()==cx)

The context's current realm may differ from the promise's realm in multi-realm embeddings

No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: data_ in BaseScript points to a BufferAllocator-managed (nursery-capable) PrivateScriptData allocation

criteria: Vulnerable code is in the PUSH instruction handlers (NPUSHB/NPUSHW/PUSHB/PUSHW) after they were refactored to do their own IP advance and bounds checking

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, all four PUSH handlers already use '>=' bounds checks, so the off-by-one is fixed. The scanner only flags SkipCode() for dropping a full-instruction-length check. That is a different function and a different concern. The scanner also says it could not construct an out-of-bounds access. It never mentions the push-handler bounds comparison.

criteria: Vulnerable function is af_map_lookup in src/autofit/afgsub.c

criteria: Vulnerable function is tt_face_get_class in a Format 1 ClassDef in src/sfnt/ttgpos.c

criteria: fd_select is obtained via cid_get_offset() from callback-supplied glyph data in the incremental branch of cid_load_glyph

criteria: Attacker-controlled 16-bit class1Count/class2Count read in tt_face_validate_pair_pos2

criteria: Source/trigger: the gzip trailer ISIZE field in an SVG document (attacker-controlled) is read as uncomp_size in tt_face_load_svg_doc

criteria: tag==1 branch in tt_face_load_any indexes ttc_header.offsets with face_index & 0xFFFF

criteria: Sink is the multiplication (p->y - min_y) * target_height in the tilde stretch scaling loop

criteria: Set_High_Precision applies 12-bit precision (precision_scale=64) when High is set
There is no guard on target bitmap dimensions (bTop/bRight), so high precision also applies to large bitmaps
Coordinates scaled by 64x in rasterization (Line_Up/Bezier_Up) overflow integer types for large bitmaps

Finding 1 accepts this gate and argues about overflow from raw outline coordinates on small bitmaps, which is a different trigger. criteria: Allocation of the dists array in sdf_generate_bounding_box uses FT_ALLOC_MULT with bitmap->width as a raw byte item_size
The allocation is undersized: rows*width bytes instead of sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance)*rows*width
Subsequent writes to dists[index] overflow the heap buffer
The non-zeroed allocation leads to uninitialized reads of the dists[index].sign sentinel
The vulnerable FT_ALLOC_MULT call is present in the evaluated code

The scanner reports a different bug: division by zero when width==0 in the new guard. It accepts FT_NEW_ARRAY as correct and never mentions the undersized FT_ALLOC_MULT allocation.

criteria: Vulnerable operation is the signed addition of movement to point->y in af_move_contour_vertically
Addition uses raw '+=' rather than the overflow-safe ADD_LONG helper
Movement comes from vertical separation adjustment on attacker-controlled glyph coordinates

criteria: In Ins_SHZ, the gep2==1 branch derives the loop limit from font-controlled contours[n_contours-1]+1.
No bounds check validates the contour-derived limit against zp2.n_points.
The loop for (i < limit) calls Move_Zp2_Point with indices beyond the cur/tags arrays.
The root cause is an attacker-supplied contour end index exceeding the real point count. It is not a different arithmetic error.
judge.findings_summary: One finding: an integer underflow in Ins_SHZ (n_points-4U with n_points<4) gives limit 65532, causing an OOB write via MOVE_Zp2_Point.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Ins_SHZ derived limit from font-controlled contours[n_contours-1]+1 with no bounds check against n_points, so Move_Zp2_Point overflows the heap. This PR replaces it with the validated n_points-4.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the limit is n_points-4 and no longer comes from contours, so the GT causal chain (an unchecked contour-derived limit) is absent. The scanner reports a different trigger: unsigned underflow when n_points<4 in fpgm/prep. Same function, same sink, different source and missing guard, so it is a near match only.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Source: lookup indices from hb_ot_layout_collect_lookups/hb_set_next, which can be influenced by the font

criteria: Allocation is refactored into a single shared pool whose total size is computed by hand
The peak_coords sub-buffer size omits the sizeof(FT_Fixed) multiplier
Writes covering 3*num_axis FT_Fixed values through peak_coords, im_start_coords and im_end_coords overflow the undersized region

The missing multiplier is present in the evaluated code

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, peak_coords_size already includes sizeof(*peak_coords), so the GT causal chain is fixed. The scanner reports a different issue: hypothetical integer overflow in the pool_size sum. It explicitly says this cannot currently overflow and calls it a latent, future-change risk. criteria: Untrusted PKCS#12 PBMAC1 PBKDF2 parameters (keylength/salt) parsed from input file
PBMAC1_PBKDF2_HMAC in p12_mutl.c uses keylength without bounds check (<=0 or >EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE)
PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC writes keylen bytes into fixed stack buffer key[EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE] in pkcs12_gen_mac, causing overflow

criteria: Attacker-controlled IV length is parsed from ASN.1 AEAD (GCM) parameters in evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params
IV bytes are copied into the fixed-size stack buffer iv[EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH]
Length is checked only for i<=0, with no check that i<=EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH before the copy
The copy uses the unchecked length as the buffer size, so the stack buffer overflows

judge.findings_summary: Seven CMS/GCM findings: short GCM tag, type confusion, missing NULL checks, plaintext released before tag verification, GCM used in EnvelopedData. None report an IV stack buffer overflow.

No scanner finding reports an IV-length stack overflow. Finding 1 mentions evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params only because the parsed tag length is discarded. criteria: Vulnerable function is ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char in ssl/quic/quic_impl.c
Source is ssl3_get_cipher_by_char() returning NULL for an unknown or unsupported cipher ID
Sink is dereferencing ciph->algorithm2 on that return value
Missing guard is a NULL check on the ssl3_get_cipher_by_char() result
Impact is a crash (DoS) when a QUIC object looks up an unknown cipher
judge.findings_summary: One OutOfBoundsRead finding: ssl3_get_cipher_by_char reads p[0] and p[1] with no length validation, now reachable through SSL_CIPHER_find on a QUIC connection object.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ossl_quic_get_cipher_by_char dereferences ciph->algorithm2 without checking whether ssl3_get_cipher_by_char returned NULL for an unknown cipher, causing a NULL dereference and DoS.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already includes the NULL check (if (ciph == NULL) return NULL;) before ciph->algorithm2 is read, so the GT causal chain is broken. The scanner's finding is a different bug class: a possible out-of-bounds read of the caller's 2-byte input buffer. criteria: Input to one-shot sign/verify in dgst is buffered via bio_to_mem with a size limit
When input exceeds the limit, bio_to_mem stops reading and returns success instead of an error
The caller treats the truncated buffer as complete and signs or verifies only a prefix
Bytes after the limit are left unauthenticated, so the signature integrity guarantee is broken
judge.findings_summary: Two pkeyutl findings: the sigfile limit went from keysize-proportional to a flat 16MB (resource concern), and %zd is used with a size_t argument.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bio_to_mem silently truncated input at 16MB and returned success, so dgst one-shot signing/verification covered only the first 16MB and later bytes were unauthenticated.
judge.reasoning: The PR's bio_to_mem returns 0 when sz exceeds maxlen, and do_fp_oneshot_sign checks !bio_to_mem and reports a read error, so the silent-truncation chain is broken. The scanner's findings are about pkeyutl: a looser signature-file size bound and a %zd format mismatch. Neither addresses silent truncation in dgst one-shot signing.

criteria: In the -addreject option handler, the parsed ASN1_OBJECT is pushed onto the wrong stack ('trust' instead of 'reject').
The error is a copy-paste mistake from the -addtrust handler.
Consequence: an intended reject purpose becomes trust, inverting the certificate's policy.
The evaluated code must still push to 'trust' inside OPT_ADDREJECT.
judge.findings_summary: Three memory/resource-leak findings on new push-failure paths: e_capi.c CAPI_KEY leak, x509.c objtmp leak on push failure, and engine.c ENGINE reference leak. None report a push to the wrong stack.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A copy-paste error in apps/x509.c made the -addreject handler push to the trust stack instead of reject, inverting the intended policy. This benign PR already pushes to reject.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR diff, OPT_ADDREJECT calls sk_ASN1_OBJECT_push(reject, objtmp), so the wrong-stack copy-paste bug is absent. No scanner finding reports a wrong-stack push or a trust/reject inversion. The x509.c finding is an adjacent bug: it describes an ASN1_OBJECT leak on the push-failure path. Finding 2 also quotes the reject push correctly, which contradicts the GT bug.

criteria: Hardware-accelerated stream path (ctx->stream) in OCB encrypt/decrypt processes full blocks
Stream path fails to advance in/out pointers by num_blocks*16
Tail handling uses bare in/out pointers assuming prior advancement
Result: trailing 1-15 bytes left unencrypted/unauthenticated, with the tail operation applied at buffer start
judge.findings_summary: One finding: in-place encryption (in==out) corrupts the partial-block checksum because ciphertext overwrites plaintext before the checksum memcpy in CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The OCB stream path does not advance in/out pointers after bulk block processing. Tail handling then uses unadvanced pointers, so the real trailing bytes stay unencrypted and unauthenticated.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds in/out advancement by processed_bytes in both stream branches, which breaks the GT causal chain. The scanner instead reports an in==out aliasing issue in the partial-block checksum, where plaintext is re-read after being overwritten. That is a different trigger and mechanism, unrelated to the missing pointer advancement in the stream path.

criteria: bmp_to_utf8 passes remaining UTF-16 source length as UTF8_putc destination capacity
UTF8_putc returns -1 for a valid BMP char >= U+0800 when only 2 source bytes remain
OPENSSL_uni2utf8 second (write) pass fails to check for a negative return
asclen becomes negative and the NUL write at asctmp[asclen] lands before the heap buffer
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: bmp_to_utf8 len misuse that fails closed, a negative unilen OOB read, an integer overflow in utf82uni, and a password leak in key_gen_utf8. None claims a negative-index heap write.
judge.ground_truth_summary: bmp_to_utf8 misuses source length as output capacity. UTF8_putc returns -1, the unchecked second pass makes asclen negative, and asctmp[asclen]='\0' writes before the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds a j<0 check in the second loop that frees the buffer and returns NULL. That breaks the negative-index write chain. Finding 1 correctly identifies the len misuse but explicitly says the code fails closed: it returns NULL with no memory corruption. So it describes the fixed state, not an active overflow. The other findings cover unrelated issues.

criteria: Source: an attacker-controlled signed attribute (signingCertificate or signingCertificateV2) in a TS response or PKCS7 SignerInfo
Sink: attr->value.sequence is dereferenced in ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get or ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get

Impact: type confusion leads to an invalid or NULL pointer dereference and a DoS crash

judge.findings_summary: Three findings: the CAdES attribute is added after signing when CMS_REUSE_DIGEST is set; an unchecked X509_digest return can leak uninitialized memory; a negative i2d length can reach malloc. None concern ASN1_TYPE type confusion.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get access attr->value.sequence without verifying attr->type == V_ASN1_SEQUENCE. A malformed TS response therefore causes type confusion and a crash.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, both ESS_SIGNING_CERT_get and ESS_SIGNING_CERT_V2_get check attr->type != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE before using the union member, so the GT chain is broken. None of the scanner findings mention ASN1_TYPE union access or a missing type check. They cover CAdES attribute ordering, an unchecked X509_digest return, and a missing i2d length check, which are unrelated bugs.

criteria: Sink is the memcpy(out, tmp + 4, tmp[0]) in kek_unwrap_key
Length tmp[0] comes from attacker-controlled decrypted header byte
Bounds check compares inlen against tmp[0] - 4 (inverted/off-by-8) instead of 4 + tmp[0]
size_t underflow when tmp[0] < 4 defeats the check
Result is OOB read past tmp and OOB write past out
judge.findings_summary: Five findings: check-byte OOB read with stream-mode ciphers, NULL parameter dereference, unchecked malloc, size_t-to-int truncation, and a key buffer leak. None addresses the tmp[0]-based memcpy bounds check.
judge.ground_truth_summary: kek_unwrap_key checks inlen < tmp[0] - 4, which is inverted and can underflow. This lets memcpy of tmp[0] bytes from tmp + 4 read and write out of bounds.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR already contains the corrected check `inlen < 4 + (size_t)tmp[0]`, so the GT causal chain is broken. No scanner finding targets the length check before memcpy. Finding 1 is an adjacent bug: an over-read of the check bytes tmp[4..6] when blocklen is 1. It has a different trigger and a different sink.

criteria: use_proxy() strips the brackets from an escaped IPv6 server name by copying it into a local host buffer with strncpy(host, server+1, sl)
No NUL terminator is written after strncpy copies exactly sl bytes
server is reassigned to the unterminated host buffer
strstr(no_proxy, server) treats host as a C string and reads past the end of the host buffer
judge.findings_summary: One OutOfBoundsRead finding: "[]" becomes an empty needle, and the strstr loop with an empty needle walks past the end of the no_proxy buffer. The finding does not mention the missing NUL terminator after strncpy.
judge.ground_truth_summary: strncpy copies an IPv6 host without its brackets but adds no NUL terminator. strstr on the unterminated host buffer then reads out of bounds. The evaluated PR already adds the terminator.
judge.reasoning: The PR code adds host[sl] = '\0' right after strncpy, which breaks the GT chain of a missing NUL terminator. The scanner reports a different trigger: server "[]" strips to an empty needle, and the strstr loop then scans past the end of no_proxy. That is a distinct bug with a different trigger and a different buffer read out of bounds. It is not the GT root cause, so detected is false.

criteria: Partial-block pre-processing path in ossl_aes_cfb128_vaes_enc/dec loads IV/input bytes
Loads use unmasked vmovdqu8 that always read 16 bytes regardless of $left
Mask k1 computed for valid bytes but not applied to pre-processing loads
Results in reading 1-15 bytes past the input buffer end (page-boundary crash/DoS)
judge.findings_summary: One IntegerOverflow finding: the wrapper's num<0 sentinel check is dead because of unsigned-to-signed widening, so out-of-range *num could cause an OOB read/write via ivp+num in the asm. Scanner says this is currently blocked by validation.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unmasked vmovdqu8 loads in the partial-block pre-processing of the VAES CFB enc/dec always read 16 bytes, over-reading the input buffer even though the k1 mask exists. This is fixed in the evaluated PR.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR's pre-processing loads already use the {%k1}{z} mask, so the GT bug is fixed. The scanner reports something else: an out-of-range *num reaching the asm because a sign-conversion makes the sentinel check dead. It also admits that set_params validation currently blocks this, which makes it a future-risk concern. Different trigger and guard, and not an active bug.

criteria: Vulnerable function is check_delta_base() in crypto/x509/x509_vfy.c
Trigger: delta CRL has the Delta CRL Indicator (base_crl_number) but no CRL Number extension (crl_number NULL)
Sink: ASN1_INTEGER_cmp(delta->crl_number, base->crl_number) dereferences the NULL pointer
Missing guard: no NULL check on delta->crl_number before the comparison
Reachable when X509_V_FLAG_USE_DELTAS is set and the attacker supplies a crafted CRL
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError in crl_cb (x_crl.c): 'break' instead of 'continue' stops the critical-extension scan early, so unhandled critical CRL extensions are silently skipped.
judge.ground_truth_summary: check_delta_base() lacks a NULL check on delta->crl_number before ASN1_INTEGER_cmp, so a delta CRL without a CRL Number extension can crash the verifier; the evaluated PR already contains the fix.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds 'if (delta->crl_number == NULL) return 0;' before the ASN1_INTEGER_cmp call, so the NULL dereference cannot happen. The scanner's only finding concerns a different file and function (x_crl.c crl_cb): a break/continue logic error when handling critical extensions. That finding has a different bug class, trigger and sink, so it does not match the GT chain.

criteria: Source: attacker-supplied CMS KeyAgreeRecipientInfo whose keyEncryptionAlgorithm AlgorithmIdentifier omits the optional parameters field
Sink: direct dereference of alg->parameter (->type or ->value) in dh/ecdh_cms_set_shared_info
Missing guard: no NULL check on alg->parameter before the dereference
Reachable via CMS_decrypt, causing a crash (DoS) before any crypto validation
Evaluated code must still dereference alg->parameter directly, not through X509_ALGOR_get0
judge.findings_summary: Six findings: inverted parameter-type check in peerkey, unchecked DHparams_dup, unchecked malloc in pkey_dh_derive, wrong field checked before UKM copy, uninitialized dukmlen, and OBJ_dup(NULL) failing ctx dup. None covers the alg->parameter NULL dereference.
judge.ground_truth_summary: dh/ecdh_cms_set_shared_info dereference alg->parameter->type without a NULL check. Absent optional AlgorithmIdentifier parameters in a crafted CMS KARI message crash CMS_decrypt (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR snapshot uses X509_ALGOR_get0 in dh_cms_set_shared_info and ecdh_cms_set_shared_info. That call returns V_ASN1_UNDEF when the parameter is NULL, and the code then fails the atype != V_ASN1_SEQUENCE check, so the GT dereference is gone. No scanner finding targets the alg->parameter NULL dereference. Finding 2 is a different NULL bug: an unchecked DHparams_dup result, triggered by allocation failure, in a different function.

criteria: Allocation size computed as buflen*3 or 1+buflen*2 in openssl_buf2hexstr_sep
Multiplication can wrap size_t (32-bit) with no overflow check before malloc
Undersized heap buffer allocated via OPENSSL_malloc
buf2hexstr_sep writes full hex output past the undersized allocation
No guard rejecting buflen > SIZE_MAX/3 or (SIZE_MAX-1)/2 present in evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: q[-1] write when buflen==0 in buf2hexstr_sep, an LLP64 (unsigned long) truncation in the bounds check, and NULL lib/reason passed to %s in ERR_print_errors_cb.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unchecked buflen*3 / 1+buflen*2 overflow on 32-bit in openssl_buf2hexstr_sep yields an undersized malloc, and the subsequent hex conversion overflows the heap buffer.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds explicit SIZE_MAX/3 and (SIZE_MAX-1)/2 checks in both openssl_buf2hexstr_sep and buf2hexstr_sep before computing the allocation size, so the GT overflow chain is broken. Scanner findings cover adjacent issues: a buflen==0 underflow write, an unsigned long truncation on LLP64 (a different mechanism, not size_t wraparound in the malloc size), and NULL %s arguments. None matches an active GT vulnerability.

criteria: Vulnerable code is port_default_packet_handler in ssl/quic/quic_port.c, where qrx_src is reassigned in the token-validation-failure path when validate_addr==0
The second assignment 'qrx_src = qrx; qrx = NULL;' has no NULL guard on qrx, so it overwrites the already-saved qrx_src with NULL
Trigger is an Initial packet carrying an invalid token on a listener with address validation disabled
Sink is ossl_qrx_read_pkt(qrx_src, ...) called with NULL in the salvage branch after port_bind_channel
Bug class is a NULL pointer dereference that crashes the server remotely
judge.findings_summary: One finding: a use-after-free and list corruption in ossl_qrx_inject_pkt, where the RXE is recycled onto qrx_src->rx_free and then inserted into the new QRX's rx_pending; it is later freed by ossl_qrx_free(qrx_src).
judge.ground_truth_summary: An unguarded second 'qrx_src = qrx' in the invalid-token path (validate_addr==0) sets qrx_src to NULL, so ossl_qrx_read_pkt(NULL) is called and the server crashes. This snapshot already has the fix.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff wraps the second reassignment in 'if (qrx != NULL)', so qrx_src is no longer overwritten with NULL and the GT chain is broken. The scanner also reports a different bug: intrusive-list corruption and use-after-free in ossl_qrx_inject_pkt in quic_record_rx.c, caused by recycling into the source QRX. That finding does not cover the NULL overwrite of qrx_src or the NULL dereference sink.

criteria: CMS/PKCS7 RSA key-transport decrypt (cms_RecipientInfo_ktri_decrypt / pkcs7_decrypt_rinfo) explicitly sets rsa_pkcs1_implicit_rejection=0
Disabling happens because the upper-layer RecipientInfo matching logic relies on distinguishing RSA decrypt success from failure
Result restores a distinguishable padding-valid/invalid oracle in CMS_decrypt/PKCS7_decrypt multi-recipient or cert-less flows
Attacker-crafted CMS/S-MIME ciphertexts can exploit this as a Bleichenbacher oracle against the victim's private key
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the new implicit-rejection control lets callers disable Bleichenbacher protection. Finding 2: the internal padding constant 8 could reach third-party RSA_METHOD engines. Neither finding concerns CMS/PKCS7 disabling the protection.
judge.ground_truth_summary: CMS/PKCS7 ktri decryption explicitly disables RSA implicit rejection to support its recipient-matching logic. This reopens a Bleichenbacher oracle in CMS_decrypt/PKCS7_decrypt.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR only adds the generic implicit-rejection knob, which defaults to enabled. It contains no change to cms_env.c or pk7_doit.c that disables implicit rejection. The scanner flags the existence of a configurable control, which is a design/configuration concern, and a separate engine padding-constant issue. Neither finding identifies the CMS/PKCS7 code turning the protection off. The GT chain is absent from this benign snapshot.

criteria: Vulnerable code is selfsigned_verify_cb() in crypto/cmp/cmp_genm.c, the custom chain builder for self-signed rootCaKeyUpdate targets.
When check_issued() matches a trusted cert, the code passes the wrong variable ('cert' instead of 'issuer') to X509_add_cert().
As a result the chain lacks the real old-root issuer, so the signature check binding the new root to the old root's key is ineffective.
Impact: an attacker-supplied newWithOld/newWithNew is accepted as a verified root CA trust anchor.
A scanner finding must name this wrong-certificate chain append, or the equivalent signature-verification bypass, in selfsigned_verify_cb.
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: NULL dereference in OSSL_CMP_ITAV_get0_rootCaKeyUpdate, dangling *newWithNew on failure, 'no update' returned as failure, and a memory leak in mock_srv_ctx_free. None concern selfsigned_verify_cb chain building.
judge.ground_truth_summary: selfsigned_verify_cb adds 'cert' instead of 'issuer' to the verification chain. This makes the newWithOld root-certificate signature check ineffective, so a forged root CA trust anchor can be accepted. The benign PR already uses 'issuer'.
judge.reasoning: The PR snapshot calls X509_add_cert(chain, issuer, ...) after check_issued() matches, so the typo is fixed and the GT chain is absent. No scanner finding addresses selfsigned_verify_cb or a chain-building or signature-verification bypass. The findings cover a NULL dereference in the ASN.1 accessor, a dangling output pointer, a wrong return code for 'no update', and a mock-server memory leak. All are unrelated or adjacent issues.

criteria: validate_email_name computes the local-part length incorrectly (len - (at - name) instead of at - name)
The 64-octet local-part bound check uses that wrong length
validate_local_part is called with the full email len instead of the local-part length
The resulting over-length scan reads past the intended local-part bounds (OOB read)
Reachable via X509_VERIFY_PARAM_add1/set1_email/rfc822/smtputf8 or S/MIME From: parsing
judge.findings_summary: 7 findings: UAF in the buffer-stack add helpers, a dangling buffer_from_bytes return, a check_email smtputf8 bypass, and several NULL dereferences (get0_ip, SSL_add1_dnsname, add1_ip_asc, add1_rfc822/smtputf8). None concern the validate_email_name length.
judge.ground_truth_summary: validate_email_name used the wrong local-part length (len - (at - name)) and passed the full len to validate_local_part, causing an OOB read and a bypass of the 64-octet limit. The benign PR has the correct at - name and local_len.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, validate_email_name sets local_len = at - name, checks local_len > 64, and passes local_len to validate_local_part. The GT causal chain is therefore fixed. None of the scanner findings mention a local-part length miscalculation or an OOB read in validate_email_name. They cover UAF, NULL dereferences, and check_email logic, which are unrelated to the GT bug.

criteria: In ossl_synchronize_rcu, the next_to_retire increment, broadcast and prior_lock unlock happen before the reader-count-zero wait on the current qp.
The early signal lets the next writer proceed and retire its own qp out of order.
This out-of-order retirement causes premature retire/reuse of rcu_qp slots (use-after-free or double-retire).
The finding must place the bug in the signal-before-drain ordering in threads_pthread.c and/or threads_win.c.
The evaluated code must still have the signal before the drain wait.
judge.findings_summary: Two DataRace findings. One says prior_lock is held across the reader spin, serializing writers (a performance/DoS concern). The other says the reader_idx store was weakened from RELEASE to RELAXED.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The RCU writer increments next_to_retire and broadcasts before confirming its qp has zero readers. The next writer can then race ahead and retire or reuse qp slots prematurely, causing a use-after-free. The fix moves the signal after the drain loop.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, both files run the reader-count drain loop before the next_to_retire++, broadcast and unlock, so the GT chain is broken. Finding 1 describes this corrected ordering and calls it a serialization/DoS performance regression, not a premature-signal use-after-free. That contradicts the GT. Finding 2 is an unrelated memory-ordering concern about reader_idx. Neither finding matches the GT root cause.

criteria: Trigger: ossl_quic_wire_peek_frame_header() fails inside log_frame()
log_frame returns 0 without setting *need_skip on that failure path
Caller log_frames loop on PACKET_remaining>0 makes no progress (position not advanced, need_skip 0)
Result: infinite loop / DoS in qlog frame logging
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: inverted min comparison in the log_frames skip logic causing underflow, swapped ect0/ect1 in ACK logging, and unbounded need_skip accumulation from CRYPTO/STREAM lengths. None concern the header-peek failure loop.
judge.ground_truth_summary: log_frame returns 0 on peek_frame_header failure without setting need_skip, so the log_frames while-loop never advances and spins forever. The fix sets need_skip on failure, and that fix is present in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR already sets *need_skip = SIZE_MAX when peek_frame_header fails, so the infinite-loop chain is broken. No scanner finding covers the peek_frame_header failure path or a non-terminating loop. The findings are about the inverted adv comparison, swapped ECN fields, and need_skip accumulation overflow, which are adjacent bugs rather than the GT root cause.

criteria: Vulnerable operation is a dereference of s->session (ext.max_fragment_len_mode) in final_maxfragmentlen() in ssl/statem/extensions.c
The dereference happens before any NULL check of s->session (the check comes after the use)
s->session can be NULL when final_maxfragmentlen is called during handshake extension finalization
A peer can drive the handshake to that point, causing a NULL deref crash (DoS)
judge.findings_summary: (1) LogicError: a mismatched MFL on resumption is no longer rejected in tls_parse_ctos_maxfragmentlen. (2) Speculative NPD in tls_parse_ctos_maxfragmentlen, acknowledged as safe today and contrasted with the new guard in final_maxfragmentlen.
judge.ground_truth_summary: final_maxfragmentlen() dereferences s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode before the existing NULL check, so a NULL session at extension finalization gives a remotely triggerable NULL pointer dereference (DoS).
judge.reasoning: The PR puts 'if (s->session == NULL) return 1;' before any s->session use in final_maxfragmentlen, so the GT chain is broken. The scanner's NPD finding targets a different function, tls_parse_ctos_maxfragmentlen in extensions_srvr.c. It says that path is safe today and raises only a future-risk concern, while pointing to the new guard as the fix. Its other finding is an unrelated logic issue.

criteria: ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL when BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on an unset peer address
ossl_quic_get_peer_token uses the returned key without a NULL check
The NULL key is passed to lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve and dereferenced, causing a crash
The evaluated code still lacks the NULL check after ossl_quic_build_new_token
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: an out-of-bounds or NULL write via the caller buffer contract in get_peer_token, an unchecked lh insert causing a leak in update_peer_token, and missing token_len bounds/overflow checks in build_new_token.
judge.ground_truth_summary: ossl_quic_get_peer_token passes a NULL key from ossl_quic_build_new_token (peer address unset) into lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve without checking it, causing a NULL dereference. This PR snapshot includes the fix.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff already adds 'if (key == NULL) return 0;' after ossl_quic_build_new_token in ossl_quic_get_peer_token, so the GT causal chain is broken. No scanner finding describes a NULL key from a failed BIO_ADDR_rawaddress reaching lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve. The findings cover an ambiguous output-buffer contract, an unchecked insert return value, and token_len validation. These are adjacent concerns, not the GT bug.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: hashValue is an OPTIONAL ASN.1 field that the decoder can leave NULL
i2r_HASH dereferences hash->hashValue->data/length without a NULL check
A crafted cert/CRL that omits hashValue reaches i2r_HASH during extension printing
The result is a NULL pointer dereference crash
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: i2r_HASH returns 0 when the optional hashValue is NULL, so printing a conformant extension fails. The finding acknowledges that the NULL check exists.
judge.ground_truth_summary: i2r_HASH dereferences the optional hashValue without a NULL check, so a crafted cert/CRL that omits it crashes extension printing.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds 'if (hash->hashValue == NULL) return 0;' before the dereference, so the GT NULL-deref chain is broken. The scanner explicitly cites this guard and reports a different issue: absent hashValue is treated as a print failure. That is a logic/robustness problem, not the NULL pointer dereference.
No vulnerabilities reported by the scanner.

criteria: Source is the notAfter ASN1_TIME data from an untrusted or malformed certificate
The data comes from ASN1_STRING_get0_data(), which does not guarantee NUL termination
The sink is strcmp() or another NUL-dependent read on that buffer
The explicit length field is not checked before the comparison
Result is a heap out-of-bounds read past the ASN1_STRING allocation
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: the '99991231235959Z' sentinel check ignores notafter->type, so a UTCTime-tagged 15-byte payload bypasses expiry validation. No out-of-bounds read is claimed.
judge.ground_truth_summary: strcmp() on non-NUL-terminated ASN1_STRING notAfter data in ossl_x509_check_cert_time, with no length validation, causes a heap out-of-bounds read.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR checks notafter->length == 15 and then uses memcmp with a bounded length of 15, so the strcmp out-of-bounds read is fixed. The scanner reports a different issue: a logic error where the sentinel check ignores the ASN1 type. It also acknowledges that the length check and memcmp are in place. This is not the GT out-of-bounds read.

criteria: BIO_sendmmsg/BIO_recvmmsg invoke the BIO_CB_*MMSG|BIO_CB_RETURN callback via bio_call_callback
That RETURN call passes a positive inret (the real ret value) while passing NULL as the processed pointer
bio_call_callback's legacy (non-_ex) shim dereferences *processed when inret>0 on non-CTRL RETURN calls
Triggered by a legacy BIO_set_callback callback plus at least one message successfully sent or received
Evaluated code must still pass NULL processed alongside a nonzero inret
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: size_t-to-int truncation, an unbounded msgs_processed loop, and a missing NULL check, all in s_cb.c bio_dump_callback; plus a negative-to-size_t cast bypass in BIO_sendmmsg's pre-callback.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The BIO_sendmmsg/recvmmsg RETURN callback passes NULL processed with positive inret, so the legacy bio_call_callback shim dereferences NULL. This is fixed in the evaluated PR, which passes msgs_processed.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, the RETURN callback calls pass msgs_processed rather than NULL, so the GT NULL-dereference chain is broken. Scanner finding 3 is about a missing NULL check in apps/lib/s_cb.c bio_dump_callback, which is a different sink and a hypothetical risk. Finding 4 is about a signed/unsigned cast on the pre-call path. No finding matches the bio_call_callback NULL processed dereference.

criteria: Encoder (evp_encodeblock_int) performs modulo/division by ctx->length
ctx->length can be zero because EVP_DecodeInit sets ctx->length = 0
Encode path reached with decode-initialized ctx (e.g., BIO b64_ctrl -> EVP_EncodeFinal)
Missing validation/non-zero guarantee on the divisor causes division-by-zero crash
judge.findings_summary: Four findings: EVP_ENCODE_LENGTH int overflow in b64_write, lost data on short writes, AVX2 used without a runtime check, unbounded allocation. None concern a zero divisor.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The new scalar base64 encoder computes modulo by ctx->length, which EVP_DecodeInit sets to 0; reaching EVP_EncodeFinal through the BIO layer causes a division-by-zero FPE. This PR fixes it by using a constant length.
judge.reasoning: The PR replaces ctx->length with the constant EVP_ENCODE_B64_LENGTH in the modulo operations and removes ctx->length = 0 from EVP_DecodeInit, so the divisor can no longer be zero and the GT chain is broken. None of the scanner findings mention division by zero, ctx->length, or EVP_DecodeInit. They cover b64_write integer overflow, partial-write handling, the AVX2 CPU check, and allocation size, which are all unrelated.

criteria: Early DTLS CCS is buffered via has_change_cipher_spec=1 and goto redo, then later delivered when dtls_ccs_expected() is true
Delivered CCS triggers ssl_set_new_record_layer() for READ while unconsumed trailing records remain (curr_rec < num_recs)
Old record layer buffer is freed via tls_int_free/ossl_tls_buffer_release, leaving dangling pointers to trailing data
Subsequent dtls1_read_bytes reads the freed buffer (heap UAF)
No guard rejects an epoch change while trailing record data is still pending
judge.findings_summary: Three LogicError findings: the new trailing-record guard rejects bundled CCS+Finished (DoS); spoofed early CCS is buffered and replayed later; and an EAP-FAST CCS case is missing from dtls_ccs_expected. No UAF is reported.
judge.ground_truth_summary: A buffered early DTLS CCS triggers a read record-layer switch while trailing record data remains. The old buffer is freed, and later dtls1_read_bytes accesses the dangling pointers (heap UAF).
judge.reasoning: The PR adds a check in ssl_set_new_record_layer that fatally errors when curr_rec < num_recs for DTLS, which breaks the UAF chain. Scanner finding 1 describes this guard as a harmful interoperability break rather than reporting an active UAF, so it contradicts the vulnerability. Findings 2 and 3 cover adjacent CCS-spoofing and state-mapping logic issues, not the UAF.

criteria: lua_close() is called on the Lua VM during script flush/engine teardown
No explicit full GC (lua_gc LUA_GCCOLLECT) runs before lua_close()
__gc finalizers on live userdata run inside lua_close() after Redis state teardown has begun
Finalizers touch freed/inconsistent memory, giving a use-after-free
Finding identifies UAF via finalizers at freeLuaScriptsSync/luaEngineFreeCtx
judge.findings_summary: One LogicError: SCRIPT FLUSH ASYNC picks sync vs. async by script count rather than Lua heap size, so main-thread blocking can be triggered via collectgarbage('stop'). This is a DoS issue, not a UAF.
judge.ground_truth_summary: lua_close() is called without a prior full GC in freeLuaScriptsSync and luaEngineFreeCtx, so __gc finalizers run during VM shutdown on freed Redis state (UAF). The fix adds lua_gc(LUA_GCCOLLECT) before lua_close.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff adds lua_gc(lua, LUA_GCCOLLECT, 0) before lua_close() in freeLuaScriptsSync, which breaks the GT causal chain. The scanner reports a different issue: a performance/DoS logic flaw where the async threshold depends on script count instead of heap size. It does not describe a use-after-free or finalizers, and it treats the GC-before-close call as present.

criteria: User-supplied filepath (argv) is the source
Copied into fixed-size stack buffer temp_filepath[PATH_MAX+1] via memcpy before dirname()
Copy length strlen(filepath) is not validated against PATH_MAX
Overlong path writes past the buffer end (stack overflow), not merely a missing terminator
No length check present in evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Missing NUL terminator before dirname (OOB read), uninitialized buf in fileIsManifest, empty manifest reported valid, stale static error and line counters.
judge.ground_truth_summary: Unbounded memcpy of a user-supplied filepath into a PATH_MAX+1 stack buffer without a length check lets a path longer than PATH_MAX overflow the stack.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR adds a check that rejects any filepath longer than PATH_MAX before the memcpy, which breaks the overflow chain. Scanner finding 1 targets the same memcpy but reports a different defect: the NUL terminator is not copied, causing an out-of-bounds read in dirname(). That is not the GT overflow from an unbounded length. The other findings are unrelated.

criteria: Lua sandbox allow-list exposes getfenv/setfenv (environment-manipulation builtins) by default
Untrusted script can obtain and replace the environment of a function belonging to another user/context
Missing guard: no gating or removal of the deprecated fenv APIs
Basic-type metatables left writable, giving an additional bypass
Result is cross-user code execution under another user's ACL identity
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: the _G metatable is left writable after FUNCTION LOAD in luaEngineCreate. Finding 2: recursive protection skips table-valued keys, described as latent. Neither covers getfenv/setfenv exposure.
judge.ground_truth_summary: getfenv/setfenv were included in the Lua builtins allow-list. This lets scripts manipulate other functions' environments and execute code under another user's identity. Unprotected basic-type metatables added a further bypass.
judge.reasoning: The PR fixes the GT issue. It moves getfenv/setfenv/newproxy to a deprecated list that is gated by the lua_enable_deprecated_api config, and it adds luaSetTableProtectionForBasicTypes. Neither scanner finding mentions getfenv/setfenv. One finding covers the _G metatable readonly flag in luaEngineCreate. The other is a latent table-key recursion gap. Both are adjacent issues, not the GT causal chain.

criteria: Source is unblockClientOnKey in src/blocked.c re-executing a blocked client's pending command
processCommandAndResetClient(c) can free or evict the client and return C_ERR
The C_ERR return value is not checked before c is used again
Freed c is then accessed through flag reads, module or reprocessing callbacks, afterCommand(c), or flag writes
The evaluated code must still lack the C_ERR check for the chain to be active
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: uninitialized promise CallReply fields readable via RM_CallReplyProto, and type confusion from an unchecked private_data cast in the RM_CallReplyPromise* APIs. Neither involves blocked.c.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In unblockClientOnKey, the code ignores a C_ERR return from processCommandAndResetClient (client freed) and keeps using c. This is a use-after-free. The evaluated PR includes the C_ERR check.
judge.reasoning: The PR diff already checks processCommandAndResetClient(c) == C_ERR and returns immediately, so the use-after-free chain is broken in this code. Neither scanner finding addresses unblockClientOnKey or client lifetime. Finding 1 is about uninitialized fields in promise CallReply objects, and finding 2 is about an unchecked private_data cast in the promise APIs. Both are unrelated to the GT bug.

criteria: In _sdsnewlen, the trymalloc path (sdstrynewlen) applies an unconditional assert on initlen+hdrlen+1 size_t overflow instead of returning NULL
Trigger: RESTORE/RDB payload with a huge string length reaches rdbGenericLoadStringObject -> sdstrynewlen
Impact: assert abort, i.e. server crash/DoS, or an undersized allocation if no guard exists
zipmapValidateIntegrity lacks a check that lengths < ZIPMAP_BIGLEN must use a 1-byte encoding
The vulnerable code must still be present in the evaluated snapshot
judge.findings_summary: Two findings: (1) a weak overflow assert in sdsMakeRoomFor that compares against len instead of reqlen; (2) unbounded 32-bit zipmap length causing pointer wraparound on 32-bit builds.
judge.ground_truth_summary: The unconditional assert in _sdsnewlen crashes Redis on size_t overflow via sdstrynewlen during RESTORE. Separately, zipmapValidateIntegrity lacks the check that small lengths use a 1-byte encoding.
judge.reasoning: The PR fixes the GT. On the trymalloc path, _sdsnewlen now returns NULL on overflow, and zipmapValidateIntegrity now rejects lengths below 254 that are not 1-byte encoded. Finding 1 targets the sdsMakeRoomFor reqlen/len assert, which is a different function and guard. Finding 2 is about pointer wraparound on 32-bit builds in zipmap validation, a different missing guard. Neither matches the GT trymalloc assert chain or the encoding check, and both acknowledge the PR's added checks.

criteria: A raw luaScript* `l` is cached in evalGenericCommand before luaCallFunction()
Active defrag runs during script execution via whileBlockedCron, relocating luaScript structs in lua_scripts
No guard stops defrag during blocked scripts, so cached pointers are never invalidated or refreshed
After the script returns, `l->node` is dereferenced and used in listUnlinkNode/listLinkNodeTail, causing use-after-free
judge.findings_summary: One UAF finding: stale `l` used after luaCallFunction when defrag relocates the luaScript. It admits the PR's AOF-loading guard closes the common case and claims a residual AOF-loading path.
judge.ground_truth_summary: evalGenericCommand caches luaScript* `l` across script execution. Active defrag in whileBlockedCron can reallocate and free it, so the post-run `l->node` LRU update reads freed memory.
judge.reasoning: The evaluated PR wraps activeDefragCycle in whileBlockedCron with an isAOFLoadingContext() guard, so defrag no longer runs while a normal client's script is blocked. That breaks the GT causal chain. The scanner says this guard closes the common case. Its remaining claim relies on a different trigger, a slow EVAL replayed during AOF loading. This is an adjacent, speculative scenario, not the GT vulnerability.

criteria: readSyncBulkPayload diskless non-SWAPDB path is the trigger
functions_lib_ctx is fetched via functionsLibCtxGetCurrent() before emptyData() runs
emptyData() frees/replaces the current functions lib ctx, leaving the captured pointer dangling
The dangling pointer is later used through loadingCtx in rdbLoadRioWithLoadingCtx

criteria: lookupKey() dereferences server.executing_client->cmd->proc in the CLIENT_NO_TOUCH check

criteria: Idle-free routine (clientsCronFreeArgvIfIdle) frees c->argv and zeroes argv_len

The scanner reports a different issue: retained argv capacity is left out of client memory accounting, which lets clients bypass maxmemory-clients. It also states the cron frees argv only when there is no in-flight multibulk, which describes the fix. Not a match.

criteria: IO thread calls lookupCommand()->dictFind() on server.commands concurrently with the main thread
dictFind reads the useStoredKeyApi bit-field

None of the scanner findings mention the bit-field storage-unit race. The findings cover a stale cached-pointer UAF, a subcommands_dict mutation race, and force_full_rehash ignoring pauserehash. These are adjacent bugs, not the GT.

criteria: dbRandomKey() retries in a while(1) loop when the picked key is volatile and logically expired
expireIfNeeded() returns 1 without deleting the key while clients are paused on a primary
The maxtries break-out guard in dbRandomKey() is gated only on server.masterhost and does not account for client pause

None of the scanner findings mention dbRandomKey, the maxtries guard, or expireIfNeeded pause suppression. All five findings cover other client-pause issues: stale end time, failover reset, the propagate assert, MULTI queueing, and the master link.

criteria: In incrDecrCommand, the reply is built from the heap robj 'new' (addReplyLongLongFromStr) that is stored in the keyspace

criteria: Client-controlled argv/argc reaches key-position/slot lookup (getSlotFromCommand/getKeysFromCommand) in the IO-thread path of processInputBuffer

Finding 2 concerns reentrancy of the prefetch batch. Neither matches the GT, and the GT is fixed in this snapshot.

criteria: Short read of the HFE min-expire time while loading RDB_TYPE_HASH_METADATA / HASH_LISTPACK_EX in rdbLoadObject
Read-error check calls rdbReportCorruptRDB (corruption_error=1) instead of rdbReportReadError

judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, both min-expire short-read checks already call rdbReportReadError, so the GT misclassification is fixed. The scanner's finding is different: a missing return after an invalid-minExpire corruption check under RESTORE, leading to an overflow in the TTL arithmetic. That is a different trigger and sink, and its quoted code even shows rdbReportReadError being used for the short read.

criteria: Trigger: a Lua error object that is a table lacking a string 'err' field (e.g. error{})
luaExtractErrorInformation leaves err_info->msg NULL because there is no else/default branch
The NULL msg reaches a format sink (sdscatfmt/addReplyErrorFormatEx %s) in luaCallFunction or luaReplyToRedisReply

Finding 1 is about lua_getfield on a nil/false error object panicking outside pcall, which is a different trigger and sink. Finding 2 is about pcall() argc underflow. Neither matches the GT.

criteria: Pointer (keystr) derived from original kvobj memory in activeDefragHExpiresOB

Both are unrelated to the GT.

criteria: Vulnerable function is setupLookaside(), which handles caller-supplied sz/cnt lookaside configuration
sz has no upper-bound check (no clamp at 65528) before being stored as (u16)sz, so sz>=65536 truncates to 0 or a wrong value
cnt has no bound relative to sz (no 0x7fff0000/sz clamp), allowing overflow in szAlloc or slot arithmetic
Truncated slot size corrupts lookaside free-list and pointer arithmetic, leading to out-of-bounds access
The evaluated code lacks these clamps
judge.findings_summary: Two malloc.c findings: the mini-lookaside pool does not fail over to the full-size pool in sqlite3DbMallocRawNN, and sqlite3DbRealloc uses '<' where '<=' is expected for exact-size reuse.
judge.ground_truth_summary: setupLookaside lacks an upper bound on sz and a bound on cnt. sz>=65536 truncates to 0 when stored as a u16 slot size, and sz*nBig overflows, causing free-list corruption and out-of-bounds access. The fix clamps sz to 65528 and bounds cnt.
judge.reasoning: The PR adds 'if( sz>65528 ) sz = 65528;' and the cnt clamp 'cnt>(0x7fff0000/sz)' before szAlloc is computed, so the GT causal chain is broken. Neither scanner finding addresses sz/cnt bounds or u16 truncation in setupLookaside. Both target different functions in malloc.c: mini-pool failover in sqlite3DbMallocRawNN and a '<' off-by-one in sqlite3DbRealloc.

criteria: Size computation in concatFuncCore multiplies (argc-1)*nSep in 32-bit int arithmetic
The product overflows before being widened to the i64 accumulator n
The undersized n feeds sqlite3_malloc64(n+1), giving a buffer that is too small
Later memcpy of separators and arguments writes past the end of the heap buffer
CONCAT_WS lets an attacker control a large separator (nSep) and a large argc
judge.findings_summary: One finding: concatFuncCore allocates and fills a potentially huge buffer before the SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH check, a memory-exhaustion/DoS issue (CWE-789/400).
judge.ground_truth_summary: A 32-bit overflow in (argc-1)*nSep inside concatFuncCore undersizes the malloc, so the following memcpy causes a heap buffer overflow. The fix casts nSep to i64, which is already present in this PR.
judge.reasoning: The PR code already computes (argc-1)*(i64)nSep, so the multiplication is 64-bit and cannot overflow; the GT chain is broken. The scanner reports a different bug: missing early SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH check, i.e. unbounded allocation and resource exhaustion. It does not identify a 32-bit overflow or an undersized buffer and heap overflow. This is an adjacent issue, not the GT vulnerability.

criteria: Source is an untrusted ZIP header uncompressed size (nOut/szUncompressed) used to size the output buffer
inflate() can return Z_STREAM_END after writing fewer bytes than nOut
Sink is sqlite3_result_blob() given nOut instead of str.total_out as the length
Result is an exposure of uninitialized heap bytes past the bytes actually written
Must be in zipfileInflate() in ext/misc/zipfile.c
judge.findings_summary: Three findings: uninitialized rc in zipfileDeflate, missing pData/nData when method=0, and an attacker-chosen sz causing large allocations in zipfileInflate (DoS). None describes exposing uninitialized bytes via the nOut blob length.
judge.ground_truth_summary: zipfileInflate returns a blob of length nOut, the header-declared size, rather than str.total_out. A crafted ZIP with an inflated size field therefore leaks uninitialized heap bytes.
judge.reasoning: In the evaluated PR, zipfileInflate passes (int)str.total_out to sqlite3_result_blob, which breaks the GT chain. No finding claims an over-read or uninitialized-heap disclosure through the blob length. Finding 3 shares the attacker-controlled sz source, but its sink is a huge allocation (DoS), not exposure of unwritten bytes. The other findings cover unrelated deflate and update logic.

criteria: Tombstone array size in fts5SegIterAllocTombstone is computed from attacker-controlled nPgTombstone taken from the serialized FTS5 structure record
nTomb and/or nByte are 32-bit int, so nTomb*sizeof(Fts5Data*) wraps around
The wrapped (small or negative) size is passed to sqlite3Fts5MallocZero, causing under-allocation
Later writes to apTombstone entries go out of bounds of the undersized buffer
No 64-bit widening of the size arithmetic is present in the evaluated code
judge.findings_summary: Finding 1: a fragile contract where tombstone allocation is skipped for SCANONETERM. Finding 2: an unbounded allocation size from nPgTombstone causing memory-pressure DoS, explicitly noting the i64 arithmetic and graceful failure.
judge.ground_truth_summary: In fts5SegIterAllocTombstone, 32-bit int nTomb/nByte overflow when multiplied by the pointer size, using attacker-controlled nPgTombstone. This under-allocates the tombstone array and allows out-of-bounds writes.
judge.reasoning: The PR declares nTomb and nByte as i64, so the size calculation cannot wrap and no under-allocation occurs. Finding 2 targets the right function and input but reports only a large-allocation/DoS concern. It says the allocation fails gracefully, which contradicts an active overflow. Finding 1 is a logic/maintenance concern about SCANONETERM handling. No finding establishes the GT overflow chain.

criteria: Bounds check on the CDS variable-length payload (nFile+nExtra) in the in-memory blob path of zipfileGetEntry
Guard uses the wrong fixed-size constant (LFH, 30) instead of the CDS constant (46)
aRead is set to aBlob[iOff+46], so the 16-byte gap allows a read past nBlob
Sink is the sqlite3_mprintf/memcpy of nFile+nExtra bytes from aRead
The evaluated code still contains the wrong constant
